# What is TensorDict?

A [`TensorDict`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) is a dictionary of tensors that behaves
like one tensor. You index, reshape, move, and save the whole group with one
call. TensorDict also makes sure that every tensor keeps the dimensions that
the group shares. A [`TensorClass`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) gives the same behavior
to a class with typed fields and methods.

## TensorDict: the dict form

All the entries of a TensorDict share their first dimensions, called the
batch size. This TensorDict holds the state of 4 robots: 7 joint angles for
each robot, and the camera images in a nested TensorDict:

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> robots = TensorDict(
... {
... "joints": torch.zeros(4, 7),
... "camera": {
... "rgb": torch.zeros(4, 3, 32, 32, dtype=torch.uint8),
... "depth": torch.zeros(4, 32, 32),
... },
... },
... batch_size=[4],
... )
```

A string, or a tuple of strings for a nested entry, reads one entry. Any
other index applies to the batch dimensions of every entry, nested entries
too. Device moves and dtype casts also apply to every entry:

```
>>> robots["camera", "depth"].shape
torch.Size([4, 32, 32])
>>> robots[:2]["camera", "rgb"].shape
torch.Size([2, 3, 32, 32])
>>> robots.to(torch.float64)["camera", "rgb"].dtype
torch.float64
```

You can also save a TensorDict to disk, send it to other processes or nodes,
and pass it to [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module) objects through [`tensordict.nn`](reference/nn.html#module-tensordict.nn).
With [`torch.func`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/func.api.html#module-torch.func), a TensorDict of parameters makes model ensembles and
parameter edits shorter to write (see [torch.compile, torch.func, torch.export, and CUDA graphs](compile.html#compile)). TensorDict started as
part of TorchRL and is now a separate library.

## TensorClass: the class form

A [`TensorClass`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) declares its fields as class annotations,
like a dataclass, and it has the tensor behavior of a TensorDict. A method
that you write once runs on one item or on a batch of any shape. This class
holds bounding boxes for object detection, with a batch of 8 images and 5
boxes for each image:

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Box(TensorClass):
... low: torch.Tensor # [*batch, 2], the lower corner
... high: torch.Tensor # [*batch, 2], the upper corner
...
... def area(self) -> torch.Tensor:
... return (self.high - self.low).prod(-1)
>>> boxes = Box(
... low=torch.zeros(8, 5, 2), high=torch.full((8, 5, 2), 2.0), batch_size=[8, 5]
... )
>>> boxes.area().shape
torch.Size([8, 5])
>>> boxes[0, 1].area()
tensor(4.)
>>> type(boxes.reshape(40)).__name__
'Box'
```

Use a TensorDict when your code chooses the keys at run time. Use a
TensorClass when the fields are fixed and you want methods on them.
[Which container should I use?](choosing_a_container.html#choosing-a-container) covers the other containers.

## What it replaces: a dictionary and tree_map

`torch.utils._pytree.tree_map()` applies a function to each tensor of a
nested dictionary. It does some of the work of a TensorDict, but it does not
know about a batch dimension. The examples below use a batch of 3 graphs,
each with 5 nodes and 10 edges:

```
>>> from torch.utils._pytree import tree_map
>>> graphs = {
... "nodes": torch.randn(3, 5, 16),
... "edges": {"index": torch.randint(5, (3, 2, 10)), "weight": torch.rand(3, 10)},
... }
>>> td = TensorDict(graphs, batch_size=[3])
```

To split the graphs with tree_map, you get one dictionary of tuples. You
must then build the three dictionaries by hand, and that code grows with
each level of nesting:

```
>>> unbound = tree_map(lambda x: x.unbind(0), graphs)
>>> type(unbound["edges"]["weight"])
<class 'tuple'>
>>> samples = [
... {
... "nodes": unbound["nodes"][i],
... "edges": {
... "index": unbound["edges"]["index"][i],
... "weight": unbound["edges"]["weight"][i],
... },
... }
... for i in range(3)
... ]
```

[`unbind()`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDictBase.unbind.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unbind) returns the three tensordicts
directly, at any nesting depth. [`split()`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDictBase.split.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.split) and
[`chunk()`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDictBase.chunk.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.chunk) work the same way:

```
>>> g0, g1, g2 = td.unbind(0)
>>> g0["edges", "weight"].shape
torch.Size([10])
```

tree_map applies an index to each tensor as it is, so the result depends on
the shape of each tensor. A TensorDict applies the index to the batch
dimensions only:

```
>>> mapped = tree_map(lambda x: x[..., :2], graphs)
>>> mapped["nodes"].shape, mapped["edges"]["weight"].shape
(torch.Size([3, 5, 2]), torch.Size([3, 2]))
>>> sliced = td[..., :2]
>>> sliced["nodes"].shape, sliced["edges", "weight"].shape
(torch.Size([2, 5, 16]), torch.Size([2, 10]))
```

A dictionary accepts a tensor of any shape. A TensorDict raises an error
when an entry does not match the batch size:

```
>>> graphs["edges"]["type"] = torch.zeros(5) # no error
>>> td["edges", "type"] = torch.zeros(5)
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
RuntimeError: batch dimension mismatch, got self.batch_size=torch.Size([3]) and value.shape=torch.Size([5]) for key 'type'. The leading dimensions of a value must match the batch size.
```

TensorDict is registered as a pytree node, so tree_map and [`torch.func`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/func.api.html#module-torch.func)
also work on a TensorDict. The result is a TensorDict:

```
>>> type(tree_map(lambda x: x + 1, td)).__name__
'TensorDict'
```

## What it is not

A TensorDict is not *exactly* a [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict). A dict is a good model: a
TensorDict has the methods of a mapping, `keys`, `values`, `items`,
`get`, `pop`, `update`, `in`, and `**data`. But `for x in data`,
`len(data)`, `bool(data)`, and `data == other` follow the rules of a
tensor:

```
>>> isinstance(robots, dict)
False
>>> len(robots) # the size of the first batch dimension, not the number of keys
4
>>> sorted(robots.keys())
['camera', 'joints']
```

[A TensorDict is not exactly a dict](concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size-not-a-dict) lists these differences.

A TensorDict is not a [`torch.Tensor`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) either. Each entry keeps its own
dtype, device, and the dimensions after the batch dimensions.
`robots.shape` is the batch size, not the shape of an entry:

```
>>> isinstance(robots, torch.Tensor)
False
>>> robots.shape
torch.Size([4])
```

A TensorDict is not a data frame. For tables that you filter, group, and
join, use pandas or Polars. [`to_pandas()`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas) and
[`from_pandas()`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pandas.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pandas) convert between the two.

[Slicing, indexing, and masking](tutorials/tensordict_slicing.html), and [Changing the shape of a TensorDict](tutorials/tensordict_shapes.html).

# Printing and display

`print(td)` shows the structure of a [`TensorDict`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)
without the values of its tensors: one line for each tensor, whatever its
size. [`set_printoptions`](reference/generated/tensordict.set_printoptions.html#tensordict.set_printoptions) chooses the attributes
that the display shows, and [`parse_tensor_dict_string()`](reference/generated/tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string.html#tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string)
rebuilds a tensordict from a printed one. All the options are in
Available options.

## What `print` shows

By default, the display shows the shape, device, dtype, and `is_shared` of
each entry, and the batch size, device, and `is_shared` of the tensordict:

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... {
... "image": torch.randn(32, 3, 64, 64),
... "label": torch.randint(10, (32,)),
... },
... batch_size=[32],
... )
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([32]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

## Choose what the display shows

If all your work is on the CPU and nothing is shared, `device=cpu` and
`is_shared=False` repeat on every line and tell you nothing.
[`set_printoptions`](reference/generated/tensordict.set_printoptions.html#tensordict.set_printoptions) selects the attributes that appear. It
works for the whole process, as a context manager, or as a decorator, as
[`torch.no_grad`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.no_grad.html#torch.no_grad) does for the last two. Its role is similar to
[`torch.set_printoptions()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.set_printoptions.html#torch.set_printoptions), which is only a function.

### For the whole process

Call `set_printoptions(...).set()` to change the defaults for the rest of
the process. `show_device` and `show_is_shared` control the lines of the
tensordict, and `show_field_device` and `show_field_is_shared` the
attributes of each field:

```
>>> from tensordict import set_printoptions
>>> set_printoptions(
... show_device=False,
... show_is_shared=False,
... show_field_device=False,
... show_field_is_shared=False,
... ).set()
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64]), dtype=torch.float32),
 label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]), dtype=torch.int64)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([32]))
```

`set()` changes only the options that it gets, so
`set_printoptions().set()` without arguments does not reset anything. To go
back to the defaults, set the changed options again:

```
>>> set_printoptions(
... show_device=True,
... show_is_shared=True,
... show_field_device=True,
... show_field_is_shared=True,
... ).set()
```

### For one block of code

Use the context manager to change the options for one block of code. At the
end of the block, the previous options come back:

```
>>> with set_printoptions(show_dtype=False, show_field_is_shared=False):
... print(td) # dtype and per-field is_shared hidden
TensorDict(
 fields={
 image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64]), device=cpu),
 label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]), device=cpu)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([32]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(td) # back to defaults
TensorDict(
 fields={
 image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([32]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

### For one function

Decorate a function to use the options for every `repr` call in it. Here,
`show_is_shared=False` hides the `is_shared=` line of the tensordict:

```
>>> @set_printoptions(show_is_shared=False)
... def summarize(td):
... print(td)
>>> summarize(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([32]),
 device=None)
```

### Shapes only: `verbose=False`

To see only the shapes, pass `verbose=False`. This one argument hides the
device, the dtype, and `is_shared`:

```
>>> with set_printoptions(verbose=False):
... print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64])),
 label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]))},
 batch_size=torch.Size([32]))
```

`verbose=True` (the default) changes nothing. Explicit keyword arguments
take precedence over `verbose`, so you can mix the two:

```
>>> with set_printoptions(verbose=False, show_dtype=True):
... print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64]), dtype=torch.float32),
 label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]), dtype=torch.int64)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([32]))
```

### Compact display: `compact=True`

With `compact=True`, each entry prints as its dtype and its shape after
the batch dims, and the batch size prints once, at the start. The display
stays on one line if it fits in 80 columns, and otherwise puts one entry on
each line:

```
>>> with set_printoptions(compact=True):
... print(td)
TensorDict(batch_size=[32], fields={image: f32[3,64,64], label: i64[]})
>>> sample = TensorDict(
... points=torch.zeros(1000, 3),
... cells=torch.zeros(1000, 4, dtype=torch.int64),
... data=TensorDict(pressure=torch.zeros(1000), mask=torch.zeros(1000, dtype=torch.bool)),
... batch_size=[1000],
... device="cpu",
... )
>>> with set_printoptions(compact=True):
... print(sample)
TensorDict(batch_size=[1000], device=cpu, fields={
 cells: i64[4],
 data: {mask: bool[], pressure: f32[]},
 points: f32[3]})
```

The dtype codes are those of JAX and polars: `f32` for `torch.float32`,
`i64` for `torch.int64`, `u8`, `c64`, `bf16`, `bool`. The rules:

- A nested tensordict prints as `{...}`, and with its class name when it is
not a [`TensorDict`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (`Mesh{...}` for a tensorclass). A
nested tensordict with more batch dims than its parent shows them first:
`sub: [5]{y: f32[3]}`.
- In a lazy stack, a dim whose size differs between the members prints as
`-1`, the header shows `stack_dim=`, and the keys that only some members
have follow under `exclusive_fields=`. A lazy stack nested in another
entry shows only the keys that all its members have; the default display
shows the others.
- A non-tensor entry prints as the type name of its value (`str`). In a
[`PersistentTensorDict`](reference/generated/tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict), it prints as `NonTensorData` or
`NonTensorStack` instead, since reading the type of the value would read
the file.
- When the tensordict has no device (`device=None`), a leaf that is not on
the CPU shows its device: `f32[3]@cuda:0`.
- `show_batch_size`, `show_device`, `show_dtype` and `sort_keys`
apply; `show_dtype=False` (or `verbose=False`) prints the shapes only,
as `[3]`. The other options, `plain` included, are ignored.
- The display reads no data and syncs no device: it uses only the shape,
dtype and device of each leaf, and stacks no leaf of a lazy stack.
- A [`TensorDictStore`](reference/generated/tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore) and a
[`NonTensorStack`](reference/generated/tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) keep their usual display, and
[`parse_tensor_dict_string()`](reference/generated/tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string.html#tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string) does not read this format.

### Available options

These options control the lines of the outer `TensorDict(...)` block:

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `show_batch_size` | `True` | Show the `batch_size=` line. |
| `show_device` | `True` | Show the `device=` line. |
| `show_is_shared` | `True` | Show the `is_shared=` line. |

These options control the attributes in the `Tensor(...)` description of
each field:

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `show_shape` | `True` | Show the `shape=` attribute. |
| `show_field_device` | `True` | Show the `device=` attribute. |
| `show_dtype` | `True` | Show the `dtype=` attribute. |
| `show_field_is_shared` | `True` | Show the `is_shared=` attribute. |

This option is a shortcut for several of the options above:

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verbose` | `True` | When `False`, hides `show_device`, `show_is_shared`, `show_field_device`, `show_dtype`, and `show_field_is_shared`. Explicit keyword arguments override `verbose`. |

These options add attributes that are hidden by default, and change the order
of the keys:

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `show_grad` | `False` | Show `requires_grad=`. |
| `show_is_contiguous` | `False` | Show `is_contiguous=`. |
| `show_is_view` | `False` | Show `is_view=` (whether `._base` is set). |
| `show_storage_size` | `False` | Show `storage_size=` (bytes). |
| `plain` | `False` | Append a short value summary (mean/std for floats, min/max for ints). |
| `sort_keys` | `"alphabetical"` | Key ordering: `"alphabetical"` (default), `"insertion"` (dict order), or a callable passed as `key` to [`sorted()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#sorted). |
| `compact` | `False` | Print each entry as its dtype and its shape after the batch dims (`f32[3]`), on one line when it fits. See Compact display: compact=True. |

### Read the current options

[`get_printoptions()`](reference/generated/tensordict.get_printoptions.html#tensordict.get_printoptions) returns a dict with the current values:

```
>>> from tensordict import get_printoptions
>>> get_printoptions()
{'show_batch_size': True, 'show_device': True, ...}
```

## Rebuild a tensordict from its printed form

When you debug, you sometimes have only the printed form of a tensordict, for
example from a log file or from the terminal of a colleague.
[`parse_tensor_dict_string()`](reference/generated/tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string.html#tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string) builds a
[`TensorDict`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) from that string. The result has the keys,
shapes, dtypes, batch size, and device of the printed tensordict. All the
values are zeros, because the repr does not contain the data:

```
>>> from tensordict import parse_tensor_dict_string
>>> s = """TensorDict(
... fields={
... image: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
... label: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([32]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
... batch_size=torch.Size([32]),
... device=cpu,
... is_shared=False)"""
>>> td = parse_tensor_dict_string(s)
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([32])
>>> td["image"].shape
torch.Size([32, 3, 64, 64])
```

[`parse_tensor_dict_string()`](reference/generated/tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string.html#tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string) is a debugging aid. It reads
the default print format, with `shape=`, `device=`, `dtype=`, and
`is_shared=` for each field. It reads nested tensordicts at any depth, keys
with any character, such as `my-key`, and devices with an index, such as
`cuda:0`. It has these limits:

- It reads only tensor fields and nested tensordicts. For a non-tensor field,
it raises `ValueError: Cannot parse the field ...`.
- If [`set_printoptions`](reference/generated/tensordict.set_printoptions.html#tensordict.set_printoptions) hid a field attribute or added one
(for example `plain=True`), it raises the same `ValueError`.
- It makes each tensor on the printed device. To parse the repr of a CUDA
tensordict, run it on a machine with CUDA.
- It does not keep `is_shared`, and it returns a
[`TensorDict`](reference/generated/tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) for the repr of a lazy stack. For a lazy
stack with exclusive keys, it raises
`ValueError: Cannot parse the exclusive_fields of a lazy stack ...`.

## See also

- The reference entries of [`set_printoptions`](reference/generated/tensordict.set_printoptions.html#tensordict.set_printoptions),
[`get_printoptions()`](reference/generated/tensordict.get_printoptions.html#tensordict.get_printoptions), and
[`parse_tensor_dict_string()`](reference/generated/tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string.html#tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string).
- [Devices, dtypes, and memory](concepts/devices.html#devices): what `device=None` in the repr means.
- [Non-tensor data and unbatched entries](concepts/non_tensor.html#non-tensor-data): how non-tensor entries appear in the repr.

# LazyStackedTensorDict

`LazyStackedTensorDict` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `LazyStackedTensorDict` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict(**tensordicts: T*, *stack_dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *hook_out: callable | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *hook_in: callable | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: Sequence[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: Sequence[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *stack_dim_name: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *strict_shape: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Bases: [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

A stack of tensordicts that keeps each input as a separate tensordict.

[`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack) and [`tensordict.stack()`](tensordict.stack.html#tensordict.stack) return a dense
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). They raise an error when the inputs have
different keys, entry shapes or batch sizes. A lazy stack accepts these
inputs: it keeps a list of the input tensordicts and stacks their entries
only when you read them. Use it for data whose size changes from one
sample to the next, such as text or episodes of different lengths.
[Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking) explains when to use a dense or a lazy stack, and
[Which container should I use?](../../choosing_a_container.html#choosing-a-container) compares the containers.

Build a lazy stack with [`tensordict.lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) or
`LazyStackedTensorDict(*tds, stack_dim=dim)`. To get a dense
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) when the inputs allow it and a lazy stack
otherwise, use [`tensordict.maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.maybe_dense_stack.html#tensordict.maybe_dense_stack).

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> tds = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.ones(4))]
>>> td_stack = LazyStackedTensorDict(*tds, stack_dim=0)
>>> td_stack.batch_size
torch.Size([2])
>>> td_stack[0] is tds[0]
True
>>> td_stack.get("a", as_padded_tensor=True)
tensor([[0., 0., 0., 0.],
 [1., 1., 1., 1.]])
```

A lazy stack behaves as follows:

- Indexing along the stack dimension returns the input objects:
`td_stack[i] is tds[i]`.
- Reading a key (`td_stack["a"]`) stacks the entries into a new tensor.
In-place changes to that tensor do not reach the inputs. Writes through
the lazy stack (`td_stack["a"] = value`, [`apply_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply_))
do reach them.
- If the entry shapes differ, `td_stack["a"]` raises an error. Pass
`as_nested_tensor`, `as_padded_tensor` or `as_list` to [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get)
to read the entries as a nested tensor, a padded tensor or a list.
These arguments apply even when the shapes match.
- [`keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys) lists only the keys that every
input has. The printed lazy stack shows the other keys under
`exclusive_fields`.
- The batch sizes of the inputs must have the same number of dimensions.
If a dimension differs between inputs, it is `-1` in the stacked
`batch_size`. Use `strict_shape=True` to raise an error instead.
An entry shape has `-1` in the same way for each dimension that
differs between inputs.

Parameters:

***tensordicts** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordicts to stack.

Keyword Arguments:

- **stack_dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension of the batch size along which the
tensordicts are stacked. It must be between `-td.ndim - 1` and
`td.ndim`, where `td` is one of the inputs. Defaults to `0`.
- **hook_out** (*Callable**,**optional*) - 

a callable to execute after [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get).

Deprecated since version 0.15: `hook_out` belongs to the [`vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap) support of lazy
stacks and has no replacement.
- **hook_in** (*Callable**,**optional*) - 

a callable to execute before [`set()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set).

Deprecated since version 0.15: `hook_in` belongs to the [`vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap) support of lazy
stacks and has no replacement.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - if no tensordict is
given, the batch size of the stacked tensordicts: the empty stack
has a `batch_size` with `0` at `stack_dim`. If tensordicts
are given, it must equal the stacked batch size, or the
constructor raises a `RuntimeError`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - the device of an empty stack. If
tensordicts are given, the stack takes the device of the first
one and ignores this argument. Defaults to `None`.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the dimension names of an empty stack.
If tensordicts are given, the names come from them, and this
argument is ignored with a `FutureWarning`. To name the dimensions
of such a stack, pass `stack_dim_name`, or set `names` on the
stack. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
applying these names to the stack.
- **stack_dim_name** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the name of the stack dimension.
Defaults to `None`.
- **strict_shape** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch sizes of the
inputs must be equal, or the constructor raises a
`RuntimeError`. Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> tds = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, 4), batch_size=[3]) for _ in range(10)]
>>> td_stack = LazyStackedTensorDict.lazy_stack(tds, -1)
>>> td_stack.shape
torch.Size([3, 10])
>>> td_stack.get("a").shape
torch.Size([3, 10, 4])
>>> td_stack[:, 0] is tds[0]
True
```

Inputs with different batch sizes give `-1` in the batch size:

```
>>> td_stack = LazyStackedTensorDict(
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]),
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(4), batch_size=[4]),
... )
>>> td_stack.batch_size
torch.Size([2, -1])
```

Inputs with different keys keep their own keys:

```
>>> td_stack = LazyStackedTensorDict(
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b=torch.ones(2))
... )
>>> list(td_stack.keys())
['a']
>>> td_stack[1]["b"]
tensor([1., 1.])
```

Note

You can assign a list to a key of a lazy stack. The list must
have the structure that `tensor.tolist()` returns: the length of
its first level must equal the first dimension of the lazy stack,
whether or not it is the stack dimension.

```
>>> td = LazyStackedTensorDict(TensorDict(), TensorDict(), stack_dim=0)
>>> td["a"] = [torch.ones(2), torch.zeros(1)]
>>> assert td[1]["a"] == torch.zeros(1)
>>> td["b"] = ["a string", "another string"]
>>> assert td[1]["b"] == "another string"
```

append(*tensordict: T*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Appends a tensordict to the lazy stack, like [`list.append()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list.append).

Same as `insert()` at the end of the stack.

Parameters:

**tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict to append. It must have
the device of the other members and as many batch dimensions.
Its sizes must match theirs, except where the batch size of
the lazy stack is `-1`.

extend(*tensordict: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[T] | T*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Appends several tensordicts to the lazy stack, like [`list.extend()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list.extend).

Parameters:

**tensordict** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the
tensordicts to append. A tensordict is unbound along the stack
dimension and its parts are appended.

*classmethod*from_dict(*input_dict: [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]] | [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]*, **other*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_size=None*, *device=None*, *batch_dims=None*, *stack_dim_name=None*, *stack_dim=0*, *names: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Builds a lazy stack from a list of dicts, one tensordict per dict.

Each dict goes through [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict), then the
results are stacked lazily, so the dicts can have different keys and
entry shapes. A dict whose keys are `"0"`, `"1"`, ... is read as
that list.

Parameters:

- **input_dict** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*, or*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*of*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the data of each
stacked tensordict.
- ***other** - passed to [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict).

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size
of each tensordict to the largest leading shape that all its
entries share. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
each stacked tensordict, without the stack dimension. Defaults
to `None`, which gives each tensordict the batch size `[]`
unless its batch size is set automatically.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of each
stacked tensordict. Defaults to `None`, which keeps each leaf
where it is.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions of each tensordict. Defaults to
`None`.
- **stack_dim_name** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the name of the stack dimension.
Defaults to `None`.
- **stack_dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the stack dimension. Defaults to `0`.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the dimensions of the
result, stack dimension included. Exclusive with
`stack_dim_name`. Without a `batch_size`, only
`names[stack_dim]` is used today and the members get no
names. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change
to giving the others to the members once their batch size is
known (a [`FutureWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#FutureWarning) is emitted when this changes
the result). Passing other entries whose number differs from
the member batch dimensions is deprecated and will be removed
in TensorDict 0.17 (a [`DeprecationWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#DeprecationWarning) is emitted);
use `stack_dim_name` instead.

Returns:

A `LazyStackedTensorDict`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict
>>> td = LazyStackedTensorDict.from_dict(
... [{"a": torch.zeros(3)}, {"a": torch.zeros(4)}], stack_dim_name="t"
... )
>>> td.batch_size, td.names
(torch.Size([2]), ['t'])
>>> td[1]["a"].shape
torch.Size([4])
```

*classmethod*from_list(*input: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)]*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *lazy: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Builds a lazy stack from a list of dicts, one tensordict per dict.

Same as [`from_dict()`](tensordict.from_dict.html#tensordict.from_dict) with a list, stacked along dimension `0`.
The dicts can have different keys and entry shapes.

Parameters:

**input** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the data of each stacked tensordict.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size
of each tensordict to the largest leading shape that all its
entries share. Defaults to `None`, which turns it on when
`batch_dims` is given.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
each stacked tensordict, without the stack dimension. Defaults
to `None`, which gives each tensordict the batch size `[]`
unless its batch size is set automatically.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of each
stacked tensordict. Defaults to `None`, which keeps each leaf
where it is.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the maximum number of batch dimensions
of each tensordict when the batch size is set automatically.
Defaults to `None`.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the dimensions of the
result, stack dimension first. See [`from_dict()`](tensordict.from_dict.html#tensordict.from_dict). Defaults
to `None`.
- **lazy** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - ignored: the result is always a lazy stack.
Defaults to `None`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict
>>> td = LazyStackedTensorDict.from_list(
... [{"a": torch.zeros(3)}, {"a": torch.zeros(4)}], auto_batch_size=True
... )
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([2, -1])
```

get_item_shape(*key*)

Returns the shape of an entry of the lazy stack, with `-1` where the members differ.

The shape of a tensor entry is read from the members without stacking
them. Other entries are read with [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get), which stacks them.

Parameters:

**key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key of the entry.

Raises:

[**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if the stack has no entry at `key`, or only some of
 its members have one.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> td = LazyStackedTensorDict(
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(4))
... )
>>> td.get_item_shape("a")
torch.Size([2, -1])
```

get_nestedtensor(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *default: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = NO_DEFAULT*, ***, *layout: [layout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Returns an entry of the lazy stack as a nested tensor.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Use `get(key, as_nested_tensor=True)` instead. It differs in three
ways: it builds a `torch.jagged` nested tensor unless you pass
`layout=torch.strided`, whereas this method builds a
`torch.strided` one by default; when a tensor `default` is
given and some tensordicts lack `key`, it returns `default`
itself, whereas this method uses `default` as the value of the
tensordicts that lack `key`; and when the stack dim is not 0, it
nests the tensors along the stack dim and puts that dim first,
whereas this method raises.

Parameters:

- **key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the entry to nest.
- **default** (*Any**,**optional*) - the value for the tensordicts that lack
`key`. If it is a tensor, it is nested with the entries of
the other tensordicts. Otherwise, it is returned as is.
Without a default, a missing key raises a `KeyError`.

Keyword Arguments:

**layout** ([*layout*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout)*,**optional*) - the layout of the nested tensor.
Defaults to `None`, which builds a `torch.strided` one.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> td0 = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(4), "b": torch.zeros(4)}, [])
>>> td1 = TensorDict({"a": torch.ones(5)}, [])
>>> td = LazyStackedTensorDict.lazy_stack([td0, td1], 0)
>>> a = td.get_nestedtensor("a")
>>> # using a tensor as default uses this default to build the nested tensor
>>> b = td.get_nestedtensor("b", default=torch.ones(4))
>>> assert (b[1] == 1).all()
>>> # using anything else as default returns the default
>>> b2 = td.get_nestedtensor("b", None)
>>> assert b2 is None
```

*property*hook_in*: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*

The callable that the lazy stack applies to the values it writes.

Deprecated since version 0.15: `hook_in` belongs to the [`vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap) support of lazy
stacks and has no replacement.

*property*hook_out*: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*

The callable that the lazy stack applies to the values it returns.

Deprecated since version 0.15: `hook_out` belongs to the [`vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap) support of lazy
stacks and has no replacement.

insert(*index: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *tensordict: T*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Inserts a tensordict into the lazy stack at `index`, like [`list.insert()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list.insert).

The lazy stack is changed in place and its batch size grows by one
along the stack dimension. The new tensordict is stored as is, not
copied.

Parameters:

- **index** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the position of the new tensordict along the stack
dimension.
- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict to insert. It must have
the device of the other members and as many batch dimensions.
Its sizes must match theirs, except where the batch size of
the lazy stack is `-1`.

Raises:

- [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - if `tensordict` is not a tensordict.
- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if the device of `tensordict` differs from that of
 the members, or if its batch size does not fit the lazy stack.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the lazy stack is locked.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> td = LazyStackedTensorDict(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)))
>>> td.insert(0, TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3)))
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([2])
>>> td[0]["a"]
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```

*classmethod*lazy_stack(*items: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)]*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out: T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *stack_dim_name: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *strict_shape: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *as_list: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *as_padded_tensor: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *as_nested_tensor: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *padding_side: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'right'*, *layout: [layout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *padding_value: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = 0.0*) → Self

Stacks tensordicts into a lazy stack.

The result keeps each input as a separate tensordict, so the inputs
can have different keys, entry shapes and batch sizes. See
`LazyStackedTensorDict` for the behavior of the
result, and [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking) for the choice between a dense and a lazy
stack.

If `items` holds tensorclass instances of one class, the result is
an instance of that class that holds a lazy stack. If `items` holds
tensors, they are stacked with [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack), unless one of
`as_list`, `as_padded_tensor` or `as_nested_tensor` is set.
These arguments, `layout`, `padding_side` and `padding_value`
apply only to a list of tensors. To read padded or nested entries from
a lazy stack of tensordicts, pass them to [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) instead.

Parameters:

- **items** (*Sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordicts to stack. It
must not be empty, or a `RuntimeError` is raised.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension along which to stack. Defaults
to `0`. A `dim` below `-batch_dims - 1` warns and wraps
around once more (and raises if it is still out of range).
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
raising an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - not used: the stack takes the
device of the first item.
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a lazy stack to write the data
into. Its batch size must be the stacked batch size. Defaults
to `None`.
- **stack_dim_name** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the name of the stack dimension.
Defaults to `None`.
- **strict_shape** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch sizes of the
items must be equal, or a `RuntimeError` is raised.
Defaults to `False`.
- **as_list** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - tensors only. If `True`, the tensors
are returned as a list.
Exclusive with `as_padded_tensor` and `as_nested_tensor`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **as_padded_tensor** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - tensors only. If `True`, the
tensors are padded to the largest shape and stacked into one tensor: each
dim is padded to its largest size. `padding_value` sets the
padding value and `padding_side` sets the side of every
padded dim.
Exclusive with `as_list` and `as_nested_tensor`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **as_nested_tensor** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - tensors only. If `True`, the
tensors are returned as a nested tensor ([`torch.nested`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/nested.html#module-torch.nested)). `layout`
sets its layout. Tensors that are nested tensors themselves
raise a `ValueError`, as a nested tensor has a single nested
level.
Exclusive with `as_list` and `as_padded_tensor`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **layout** ([*layout*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout)*,**optional*) - the layout of the nested tensor
when `as_nested_tensor=True`: `torch.jagged` or
`torch.strided`. Defaults to `torch.jagged`.
- **padding_side** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the side to pad with
`as_padded_tensor`: `"left"` or `"right"`. Defaults to
`"right"`.
- **padding_value** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*,*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the padding value
with `as_padded_tensor`. Defaults to `0.0`.

Returns:

A `LazyStackedTensorDict`, or a tensorclass
instance if `items` holds tensorclass instances.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> td_stack = LazyStackedTensorDict.lazy_stack(
... [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(4))]
... )
>>> type(td_stack).__name__
'LazyStackedTensorDict'
>>> td_stack.get("a", as_list=True)
[tensor([0., 0., 0.]), tensor([0., 0., 0., 0.])]
```

*classmethod*maybe_dense_stack(*items: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)]*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *out: T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *strict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Stacks tensordicts densely if possible, or into a lazy stack otherwise.

Use this function when the inputs usually match, but can differ. If
every item has the same keys and the same entry shapes, the result is
the dense stack that [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack) returns. Otherwise, the result
is the lazy stack that [`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) returns. See [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking).

Parameters:

- **items** (*Sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to stack.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the new dimension. Defaults to `0`. A
`dim` outside `[-batch_dims - 1, batch_dims]` warns, and
is used on the dims of the leaves. Starting with TensorDict
0.17, the default will change to raising an `IndexError`,
as for a tensor.
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into. Defaults to `None`.
- **strict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - used only with `out`. If `True`,
`out` must have the same keys as the items, or a
`RuntimeError` is raised. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (or the tensorclass of the
items) if the items can be stacked densely, a
`LazyStackedTensorDict` otherwise.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> td0 = TensorDict({"a": 0}, [])
>>> td1 = TensorDict({"b": 0}, [])
>>> out = LazyStackedTensorDict.maybe_dense_stack([td0, td0]) # same keys: dense stack
>>> assert type(out) is TensorDict and out.shape == (2,)
>>> out = LazyStackedTensorDict.maybe_dense_stack([td0, td1]) # different keys: lazy stack
>>> assert isinstance(out, LazyStackedTensorDict) and out.shape == (2,)
```

non_tensor_items(*include_nested: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns the non-tensor leaves as `(key, value)` pairs, each stacked across the members.

Only the keys that every member holds are listed. If
`include_nested` is `True`, the nested tensordicts are searched as
well.

valid_keys(*include_nested: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *leaves_only: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *is_leaf: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Type)], [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *sort: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → _LazyStackedTensorDictKeysView

Returns the keys of the lazy stack, like [`keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys).

Deprecated since version 0.15: Use [`keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys) instead, which takes the same arguments. Will be
removed in TensorDict 0.17.

# MemoryMappedTensor

*class*tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor(*source*, ***, *dtype=None*, *shape=None*, *index=None*, *device=None*, *handler=None*, *filename=None*)

Bases: [`Tensor`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

A CPU tensor whose storage is a file on disk, or anonymous shared memory when no filename is given.

Use it to share a tensor between processes, or to work with data that is
larger than RAM: the operating system reads from the file only the pages
that you access. When a MemoryMappedTensor is sent through a
multiprocessing queue or an RPC call, only its file or shared-memory
reference is sent, not the data. [`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap)
turns every leaf of a tensordict into a MemoryMappedTensor. See
[Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving) and [Load data and share it between processes](../../data_loading.html#data-loading).

Build one with a class method rather than with the constructor:

- `from_tensor()` copies a tensor;
- `empty()`, `zeros()`, `ones()` and `full()` make a new
tensor of a given shape, and `empty_like()`, `zeros_like()`,
`ones_like()` and `full_like()` one with the shape and dtype of
another tensor;
- `from_filename()` maps an existing file, and `from_storage()`
wraps an existing storage.

The methods that write new data take a `filename`: with one, the data
is in that file; without one, it is in anonymous shared memory, and
`filename` raises an error. Indexing a MemoryMappedTensor, `unbind()`,
`chunk()` and `split()` give MemoryMappedTensors on the same
storage. Other operations (`x + 1`, for example) give a regular
[`torch.Tensor`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor).

A MemoryMappedTensor has these constraints:

- It must be on CPU, and it cannot require gradients.
- With RPC, every node must have read access to the file path. If it
does not, the result of sending the tensor is undefined.

Warning

A caller that supplies `filename` must control its parent directory.
Existing symbolic links are rejected, but path-based memory mapping
cannot prevent another process with directory write access from
replacing a path after it has been validated.

The `handler` argument is internal.

Parameters:

**source** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,*[*TypedStorage*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/storage.html#torch.TypedStorage)*,*[*UntypedStorage*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/storage.html#torch.UntypedStorage)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - the data. A str is the name of an existing file, mapped as
`from_filename()` does with `dtype`, `shape` and
`index`. With `filename`, the tensor is copied to that file,
as `from_tensor()` does. A storage is passed to
`from_storage()` with the other arguments. A tensor without
`filename` is wrapped as it is: the result shares its memory but
has no file or shared-memory handle, so it cannot be pickled.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - with a str `source`, the dtype of
the data in the file (required). With a storage, the dtype of the
tensor, as in `from_storage()`. Not accepted with the
`filename` keyword. Defaults to `None`.
- **shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - the shape of the result, as in
`from_filename()`, `from_tensor()` or `from_storage()`;
required with a str `source`. Ignored for a tensor without
`filename`. Defaults to `None`, which keeps the shape of
`source`.
- **index** (*index**,**optional*) - an index applied to the result, as in
`tensor[index]`. With a str or storage `source`, `shape` is
the shape of the data before `index` is applied. Defaults to
`None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - `None` or `"cpu"`;
another device raises a `ValueError`. Defaults to `None`.
- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path**,**optional*) - the file to copy `source` to.
Defaults to `None`.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import MemoryMappedTensor
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... filename = os.path.join(tmpdir, "x.memmap")
... x = MemoryMappedTensor.from_tensor(torch.arange(4.0), filename=filename)
... x[0] = 10.0 # writes to the file
... print(MemoryMappedTensor.from_filename(filename, dtype=torch.float32, shape=(4,)))
MemoryMappedTensor([10., 1., 2., 3.])
```

Without a filename, the data is in anonymous shared memory:

```
>>> z = MemoryMappedTensor.zeros(2, 3)
>>> z.shape, z.dtype
(torch.Size([2, 3]), torch.float32)
>>> type(z[0]).__name__, type(z + 1).__name__
('MemoryMappedTensor', 'Tensor')
```

chunk(*chunks*, *dim=0*)

Splits the tensor into `chunks` views, as [`torch.Tensor.chunk()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.chunk.html#torch.Tensor.chunk) does.

The chunks are MemoryMappedTensors on the same storage, so they keep
the file and can be pickled. Under [`torch.compile()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile.html#torch.compile), they are
regular tensors.

*classmethod*empty(**size*, *dtype=None*, *device=None*, *filename=None*, *existsok: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

*classmethod*empty(*shape*, ***, *dtype=None*, *device=None*, *filename=None*, *existsok: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns an uninitialized MemoryMappedTensor of the given shape.

Parameters:

***size** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,*[*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the
shape, as ints (`2, 3`) or as one sequence (`(2, 3)`). It
can also be passed as the `shape` keyword. A 2-D tensor gives
a nested tensor, with the shape of each element in one row.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of the tensor. Defaults to
`None`, which uses the default dtype
([`torch.get_default_dtype()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.get_default_dtype.html#torch.get_default_dtype)).
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - `None` or
`"cpu"`; another device raises a `RuntimeError`. Defaults
to `None`.
- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path**,**optional*) - the file to write the data to.
Defaults to `None`, which keeps the data in anonymous shared
memory.
- **existsok** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, an existing file at
`filename` is overwritten. If `False`, it raises a
`RuntimeError`. Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import MemoryMappedTensor
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... filename = os.path.join(tmpdir, "x.memmap")

... print(x.shape, os.path.getsize(filename))
torch.Size([2, 3]) 48
```

*property*filename

The absolute path of the file that holds the data.

Raises a `RuntimeError` if the data is in anonymous shared memory.

*classmethod*from_filename(*filename*, *dtype*, *shape*, *index=None*, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Returns a MemoryMappedTensor that maps an existing file.

The file holds raw data with no header, so the dtype and the shape
must be given. [`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap) records them
in the `meta.json` file of the directory it writes.

Parameters:

- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the path to the file.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)) - the dtype of the data.
- **shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the shape of
the tensor. A 2-D tensor gives a nested tensor, with the shape
of each element in one row.
- **index** (*index**,**optional*) - an index applied to the result, as in
`tensor[index]`. Defaults to `None`.
- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - `"r"` maps the file copy-on-write:
in-place writes stay in memory. `"r+"` maps it shared:
in-place writes reach the file, and a [`PermissionError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#PermissionError)
is raised if the file is not writable. Defaults to `None`,
which maps the file shared if it is writable and copy-on-write
otherwise.

Raises:

- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if `mode` is not `None`, `"r"` or `"r+"`.
- [**PermissionError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#PermissionError) - if `mode="r+"` and the file is not writable.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import MemoryMappedTensor
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... filename = os.path.join(tmpdir, "x.memmap")
... _ = MemoryMappedTensor.from_tensor(torch.arange(6), filename=filename)
... x = MemoryMappedTensor.from_filename(filename, torch.int64, (2, 3), mode="r")
... x[0, 0] = 100 # copy-on-write: the file is unchanged
... print(MemoryMappedTensor.from_filename(filename, torch.int64, (2, 3)))
MemoryMappedTensor([[0, 1, 2],
 [3, 4, 5]])
```

*classmethod*from_handler(*handler*, *dtype*, *shape*, *index=None*)

Rebuilds a MemoryMappedTensor from a shared-memory handler.

Deprecated since version 0.15: The handler is private, and this method has no replacement.

Parameters:

- **handler** - the shared-memory handler of the data.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)) - the dtype of the data.
- **shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the shape of the tensor, or
a 2-D tensor with the shape of each element of a nested
tensor.
- **index** (*index**,**optional*) - an index applied to the result.
Defaults to `None`.

*classmethod*from_storage(*storage*, ***, *shape: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *index: IndexType | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *filename: Path | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = None*, *handler: _handler = None*)

Returns a MemoryMappedTensor that views an existing storage.

The data is not copied: writes to the result change the storage. If
the storage was mapped from a file (for example with
[`torch.UntypedStorage.from_file()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/storage.html#torch.UntypedStorage.from_file)), the result keeps that file
and can be pickled; other storages give a tensor that cannot be
pickled.

Parameters:

**storage** ([*UntypedStorage*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/storage.html#torch.UntypedStorage)*or*[*TypedStorage*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/storage.html#torch.TypedStorage)) - the storage
to view.

Keyword Arguments:

- **shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**optional*) - the shape of the
result. A tensor gives a nested tensor with one shape per
row. Defaults to `None`, which gives a 1-D tensor.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype to read the storage
with. Defaults to `None`, which reads an untyped storage as
`torch.int64` and accepts a typed storage only if its dtype
is the default dtype ([`torch.get_default_dtype()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.get_default_dtype.html#torch.get_default_dtype)). Pass
`dtype` to read another dtype.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - `None` or `"cpu"`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **index** (*index**,**optional*) - an index applied to the result. Defaults
to `None`.
- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path**,**optional*) - the file of the storage, if it
has one and does not record it. Defaults to `None`.
- **handler** - internal.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the storage has a file and `filename` names
 another one.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import MemoryMappedTensor
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... filename = os.path.join(tmpdir, "x.memmap")
... _ = MemoryMappedTensor.from_tensor(torch.arange(6.0), filename=filename)
... storage = torch.UntypedStorage.from_file(filename, shared=True, nbytes=24)
... x = MemoryMappedTensor.from_storage(storage, dtype=torch.float32, shape=(2, 3))
... print(x, x.filename == filename)
MemoryMappedTensor([[0., 1., 2.],
 [3., 4., 5.]]) True
```

*classmethod*from_tensor(*input*, ***, *filename: [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = None*, *existsok: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *copy_existing: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *copy_data: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *shape: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Returns a MemoryMappedTensor with a copy of the content of `input`.

If `input` is a MemoryMappedTensor, it is returned unchanged in two
cases: `filename` is `None` and `input` has no file, or
`filename` is the file of `input` (and `input` was not opened
with `mode="r"`). A file-backed `input` with `filename=None` is
copied to anonymous shared memory. In all other cases, a new
`MemoryMappedTensor` is produced.

Parameters:

**input** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the tensor to copy. A nested tensor must
have the `torch.strided` layout.

Keyword Arguments:

- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path**,**optional*) - the file to write the data to.
Defaults to `None`, which keeps the data in anonymous shared
memory.
- **existsok** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, an existing file at
`filename` is overwritten. If `False`, it raises an error.
Defaults to `False`.
- **copy_existing** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a MemoryMappedTensor
with a file can be copied to another file. If `False`, this
raises an error, so that data is not duplicated on disk by
mistake. Defaults to `False`.
- **copy_data** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, the result has the
shape and dtype of `input` but its content is not written.
Defaults to `True`.
- **shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**optional*) - the shape of the
result, when it differs from that of `input`; `input` is
broadcast to it. For a nested tensor, a tensor with the shape
of each element, one per row. Defaults to `None`, which keeps
the shape of `input`.

Returns:

A MemoryMappedTensor, which is `input` itself in the two cases
above.

Raises:

- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `input` requires gradients, if `input` has
 a file, `filename` is another file and `copy_existing` is
 `False`, or if `filename` exists and `existsok` is
 `False`.
- [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - if `input` is a NumPy array.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import MemoryMappedTensor
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... filename = os.path.join(tmpdir, "tensor.memmap")
... mmap = MemoryMappedTensor.from_tensor(torch.arange(3.0), filename=filename)
... print(mmap)
... print(MemoryMappedTensor.from_tensor(mmap, filename=filename) is mmap)
MemoryMappedTensor([0., 1., 2.])
True
```

*property*parent_shape*: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*

The shape of the tensor that this tensor was built from.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This is internal to pickling and has no replacement.

split(*split_size*, *dim=0*)

Splits the tensor into views of `split_size`, as [`torch.Tensor.split()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.split.html#torch.Tensor.split) does.

The parts are MemoryMappedTensors on the same storage, so they keep
the file and can be pickled. Under [`torch.compile()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile.html#torch.compile), they are
regular tensors.

unbind(*dim*)

Removes a dimension and returns the slices along it, as [`torch.Tensor.unbind()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.unbind.html#torch.Tensor.unbind) does.

The slices are MemoryMappedTensors on the same storage, so they keep
the file and can be pickled. Under [`torch.compile()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile.html#torch.compile), they are
regular tensors. Unlike [`torch.Tensor.unbind()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.unbind.html#torch.Tensor.unbind), `dim` has no
default.

*classmethod*zeros(**size*, *dtype=None*, *device=None*, *filename=None*, *existsok: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

*classmethod*zeros(*shape*, ***, *dtype=None*, *device=None*, *filename=None*, *existsok: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns a MemoryMappedTensor of the given shape filled with zeros.

Parameters:

***size** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,*[*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the
shape, as ints (`2, 3`) or as one sequence (`(2, 3)`). It
can also be passed as the `shape` keyword. A 2-D tensor gives
a nested tensor, with the shape of each element in one row.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of the tensor. Defaults to
`None`, which uses the default dtype
([`torch.get_default_dtype()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.get_default_dtype.html#torch.get_default_dtype)).
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - `None` or
`"cpu"`; another device raises a `RuntimeError`. Defaults
to `None`.
- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path**,**optional*) - the file to write the data to.
Defaults to `None`, which keeps the data in anonymous shared
memory.
- **existsok** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, an existing file at
`filename` is overwritten. If `False`, it raises a
`RuntimeError`. Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import MemoryMappedTensor
>>> MemoryMappedTensor.zeros(2, 3)
MemoryMappedTensor([[0., 0., 0.],
 [0., 0., 0.]])
```

*classmethod*zeros_like(*input*, ***, *filename=None*)

Returns a MemoryMappedTensor filled with zeros, with the shape and dtype of `input`.

Parameters:

**input** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the tensor whose shape and dtype the result
takes.

Keyword Arguments:

**filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path**,**optional*) - the file to write the data to.
It must not exist. Defaults to `None`, which keeps the data
in anonymous shared memory.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import MemoryMappedTensor
>>> MemoryMappedTensor.zeros_like(torch.ones(3))
MemoryMappedTensor([0., 0., 0.])
```
