# TensorAttrs

`TensorAttrs` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `TensorAttrs` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.TensorAttrs(*tgt_device: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = None*, *tgt_dtype: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = None*, *tgt_shape: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = None*, ***, *batch_size*, *device=None*, *names=None*)

Bases: [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass)

A tensorclass that holds the device, dtype and shape of one tensor.

[`attrs()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.attrs.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.attrs) returns a tensordict with one
`TensorAttrs` per leaf. Pass it to
[`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) to move or cast each leaf of another
tensordict to the device and dtype of the matching leaf, for example when
the leaves are on different devices. The names follow the [PyTorch Tensor
Attributes](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html).

The fields start with `tgt_` so that they do not hide the `device`,
`dtype` and `shape` attributes of the tensorclass.

Parameters:

- **tgt_device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - the device of the tensor.
Defaults to `None`.
- **tgt_dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of the tensor. Defaults
to `None`.
- **tgt_shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - the shape of the tensor. Defaults
to `None`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3, device="cpu"),
... "b": torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int32)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> attrs = td.attrs()
>>> attrs["a"].tgt_device, attrs["a"].tgt_dtype
(device(type='cpu'), torch.float32)
```

*property*device*: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*

The device of the tensorclass, or `None` if its leaves may be on different devices.

It is read-only: use [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) to move the
tensorclass to another device.

extend(*tensordict: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)] | [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Appends tensordicts to the lazy stack that the instance holds.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Build a new instance with [`tensordict.lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) or
[`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat) instead.

*classmethod*fields() → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Field](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html#dataclasses.Field), ...]

Returns the fields of the tensorclass.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Use `dataclasses.fields(cls)` instead. It returns the same tuple of
[`dataclasses.Field`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html#dataclasses.Field) objects.

from_module(*as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Returns a tensordict that holds the parameters and buffers of a module.

The entries are the parameters and buffers of the module themselves,
not copies. Submodules become nested tensordicts.

Note

This method does not lock the result by default (`lock=False`).
The function [`tensordict.from_module()`](tensordict.from_module.html#tensordict.from_module) locks it by default
(`lock=True`).

Parameters:

- **module** ([*Module*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `TensorDictParams`
instance is returned, which can be used to store parameters
within a [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `False`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict from the
module is used and unflattened into a TensorDict with
the tree structure of the model. Use it when the module has
state-dict hooks. Defaults to `False`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, submodules without
parameters or buffers (`nn.ReLU`, for example) get no
entry. If `False`, they get an empty tensordict.
Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), or a
`TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> module = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 4), nn.ReLU())
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> params["0", "weight"] is module[0].weight
True
>>> list(params.keys())
['0']
>>> params.is_locked
False
```

*classmethod*from_tensor(*tensor*, ***, *fields=('device', 'dtype', 'shape')*)

Returns a `TensorAttrs` with the attributes of `tensor`.

Parameters:

**tensor** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the tensor to describe.

Keyword Arguments:

**fields** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the attributes to read, among
`"device"`, `"dtype"` and `"shape"`. The other fields
are `None`. Defaults to `("device", "dtype", "shape")`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorAttrs
>>> attrs = TensorAttrs.from_tensor(torch.zeros(2, 3), fields=("dtype",))
>>> attrs.tgt_dtype, attrs.tgt_shape
(torch.float32, None)
```

*classmethod*from_tensordict(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *non_tensordict: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Wraps a tensordict in a new instance of the tensorclass, without copying the leaves.

If `tensordict` is a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), the entries of the fields
annotated with a tensorclass (or `Optional` of one) that are tensordicts become
instances of that tensorclass, recursively. They are set in a shallow copy of
`tensordict`, which keeps its own entries. An entry with keys that the annotated
class does not declare stays a tensordict. Other backends are wrapped as they are:
setting a tensorclass in them would write to their storage (e.g. an H5 file).

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict that holds the tensor fields.
- **non_tensordict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - the values of the non-tensor fields. The
fields that neither argument holds are set to `None`. Defaults
to `None`.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - deprecated in 0.15, will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.
If `False`, skips the check that `tensordict` is a
[`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase). By default, the check runs, and
another type raises a `RuntimeError`.

Returns:

A new instance of the class, whose fields are the entries of
`tensordict`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Pose(TensorClass):
... q: torch.Tensor
>>> class Obs(TensorClass):
... a: Pose
>>> obs = Obs(a=Pose(q=torch.zeros(5, 4), batch_size=[5]), batch_size=[5])
>>> type(Obs.from_tensordict(obs.to_tensordict()).a).__name__
'Pose'
```

rename_keys(*mapping*, ***, *strict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Returns a tensorclass with several keys renamed at once.

Works as [`rename_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename_keys), which describes
`mapping` and `strict`, with two differences: each destination must be
a field of the class, or the call raises an `AttributeError`, and a
field that the renaming empties is kept.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... y: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3), y=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> foo.rename_keys({"x": "y", "y": "x"}).x
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```

select(**keys*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *strict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *as_tensordict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns a tensorclass that holds only the fields of `keys`, with the other fields set to `None`.

Works as [`select()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.select.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.select), which describes
`keys`: the leaves are not copied.

Keyword Arguments:

- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the other fields of the
tensorclass to `None` and returns `self`. Defaults to
`False`.
- **strict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a missing key raises a
`KeyError`. If `False`, missing keys are ignored. Defaults to
`True`.
- **as_tensordict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, returns the selected
entries in a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) instead of a
tensorclass. Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... y: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3), y=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> print(foo.select("x").y)
None
>>> type(foo.select("x", as_tensordict=True)).__name__
'TensorDict'
```

---

# TensorClass

`TensorClass` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `TensorClass` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.TensorClass(**args*, ***kwargs*)

Bases: [`TensorCollection`](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

A base class for dataclass-like containers of tensors.

Subclass `TensorClass` and annotate fields, as with
[`dataclasses.dataclass()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html#dataclasses.dataclass). The instances behave like a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict): they have a batch size, and they support
indexing, reshaping, `to(device)`, [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack),
[`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat) and memory-mapping. A field can hold a tensor, a
tensordict, another tensorclass, or any Python object (stored as
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)). This class replaces the
[`tensorclass()`](tensordict.tensorclass.html#tensordict.tensorclass) decorator, which is kept for existing code.

Use a tensorclass instead of a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) when the
data has a fixed set of named fields, when you want editors and type
checkers to know the fields, or when you want to add methods. Use a
[`TypedTensorDict`](tensordict.TypedTensorDict.html#tensordict.TypedTensorDict) instead if you need a
[`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) subclass (`state["key"]`,
`**state` unpacking). [Which container should I use?](../../choosing_a_container.html#choosing-a-container) compares the
containers, and [TensorClass](../../tensorclass.html#tensorclass-guide) is the user guide.

The constructor of a subclass takes the fields, by name or in order, and
these keyword arguments: `Foo(tensor=..., batch_size=[3])`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the instance: the leading dimensions that all its fields share.
See [Batch size, shapes, and indexing](../../concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size). Defaults to `torch.Size([])`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
instance. Tensors on another device are moved to it. Defaults to
`None`, which leaves each tensor where it is.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the batch dimensions, one
per dimension. Defaults to `None`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the instance is locked: writing a
field raises a `RuntimeError`. See [Locking and temporary changes](../../concepts/keys.html#keys-locking).
Defaults to `False`.

The class flags below go to the class definition instead.

Class flags

A flag changes the behavior of every instance of the class. Set it in
one of three equivalent forms:

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass, tensorclass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["autocast"]): # bracket form
... integer: int
>>> class Foo(TensorClass, autocast=True): # keyword form
... integer: int
>>> @tensorclass(autocast=True) # legacy decorator form
... class Foo:
... integer: int
```

To combine flags, list them in the brackets:

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["nocast", "frozen"]):
... integer: int
```

The flags are:

- No flag: tensor-compatible values (`int`, `float`, `np.ndarray`)
are cast to tensors. Other values are stored as
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData).

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: int
>>> Foo(x=1).x
tensor(1)
```
- `autocast`: when a field is set, the value is converted to the
annotated type. For example, an `int` field set to
`torch.ones(())` holds `1`.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["autocast"]):
... x: int
>>> Foo(x=torch.ones(())).x
1
```
- `nocast`: tensor-compatible values are stored as they are, not cast
to tensors.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["nocast"]):
... x: int
>>> Foo(x=1).x
1
```
- `tensor_only`: every field annotation must be a tensor type, a tensor
collection, or an optional or union of these. Other annotations raise
a `TypeError` when the class is defined. Values that can be cast to
a tensor (Python scalars, numpy arrays) are cast. Reading a field then
skips the lookup in the non-tensor storage.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["tensor_only"]):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> Foo(x=1).x
tensor(1)
```
- `frozen`: assigning a field raises `FrozenInstanceError`, as with
`@dataclass(frozen=True)`. Subclasses of a frozen class are frozen
too. A frozen class cannot subclass a non-frozen tensorclass: this
raises a `TypeError`.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["frozen"]):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3))
>>> foo.x = torch.ones(3)
Traceback (most recent call last):
 ...
dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field 'x'
```
- `shadow`: by default, a field whose name is a tensorclass member
(`batch_size`, `device`, `names`, `sum`, `apply` and the
other TensorDict methods) raises an `AttributeError` when the class
is defined. `shadow=True` allows these names. The field then hides
the member of the same name.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["shadow"]):
... sum: torch.Tensor
>>> Foo(sum=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3]).sum
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```
- `skip_post_init_on_rebuild`: `__post_init__` runs on the data that
comes in (the generated `__init__`, `from_tensordict`,
`from_dict`, the other constructors such as `from_any` or
`fromkeys`, and loads), but not when tensordict makes a new instance
from an existing one (indexing, `clone`, `to`, `apply`, stacking
and the other operations). Subclasses inherit the flag.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["skip_post_init_on_rebuild"]):
... x: torch.Tensor
... def __post_init__(self):
... print("checked")
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3))
checked
>>> foo = foo.clone()
```

`autocast`, `nocast` and `tensor_only` are exclusive: combining two
of them raises a `TypeError`.

A class keyword that is not a flag, `cast_filter`, sets the default
`cast_filter` of [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) and of the dtype
shorthands (`float()`, `bfloat16()`, ...): a predicate
`fn(key, value) -> bool` that selects the tensor leaves a dtype cast
applies to. A `cast_filter` passed to the call overrides it, and
`cast_filter=None` there casts every leaf. Subclasses inherit it. It
applies to calls on the tensorclass itself, not when the tensorclass is a
value of another tensordict or tensorclass that is cast.

```
>>> from tensordict import is_inexact
>>> class Mesh(TensorClass, cast_filter=is_inexact):
... points: torch.Tensor
... cells: torch.Tensor
>>> mesh = Mesh(points=torch.zeros(4, 3), cells=torch.zeros(2, 3, dtype=torch.long))
>>> mesh.bfloat16().points.dtype, mesh.bfloat16().cells.dtype
(torch.bfloat16, torch.int64)
```

Subclassing

A class with flags is a regular class. You can subclass it and add
flags:

```
>>> class Base(TensorClass["autocast"]):
... x: int
>>> class Sub(Base, shadow=True): # autocast inherited, shadow added
... y: float
```

Type checking

`TensorClass[...]` is implemented with [`__class_getitem__()`](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__class_getitem__),
so pyright resolves it to the class with flags, not to a generic
parameter. Mypy does not evaluate `__class_getitem__` in a list of base
classes and rejects the bracket form. In code that mypy checks, use the
keyword form: `class Foo(TensorClass, autocast=True)`. Editors complete
the annotated fields on instances.

Note

`TensorClass` itself is not a tensorclass: only its
subclasses become dataclasses. The reason is that a non-frozen base
cannot have a frozen subclass, and the base cannot know whether a
subclass sets `frozen`.

See also

- [`tensorclass()`](tensordict.tensorclass.html#tensordict.tensorclass) for the decorator form.
- [`from_dataclass()`](tensordict.from_dataclass.html#tensordict.from_dataclass) to migrate an existing `@dataclass` to a tensorclass.
- [`TensorClassModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase) for typed `nn.Module` I/O backed by
tensorclasses.

Examples

```
>>> from typing import Any
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... tensor: torch.Tensor
... non_tensor: Any
... nested: Any = None
>>> foo = Foo(tensor=torch.zeros(3), non_tensor="a string!", batch_size=[3])
>>> print(foo)
Foo(
 non_tensor=NonTensorData(data=a string!, batch_size=torch.Size([3]), device=None),
 tensor=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 nested=None,
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> foo[0].non_tensor
'a string!'
>>> foo.reshape(1, 3).batch_size
torch.Size([1, 3])
```

*classmethod*from_dict(*input_dict*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size=None*, *device=None*, *batch_dims=None*)

Builds an instance of the tensorclass from a dictionary of its fields.

The fields that `input_dict` misses are set to `None`, also those that
declare a default or a default factory. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the
default will change to filling these fields with their defaults, as the
constructor does. Until then, a call that misses such a field warns with a
[`FutureWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#FutureWarning).

Parameters:

**input_dict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the values of the fields. Nested dictionaries become
tensordicts, or tensorclasses for the fields annotated with one.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Defaults to
`None`, which behaves like `False`, unless `batch_dims` is
passed: then it behaves like `True`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Defaults to `None`, which gives an empty batch size unless
`auto_batch_size` is on.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. Defaults to
`None`, which leaves each leaf where it is.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Exclusive with `batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A new instance of the class.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... y: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo.from_dict({"x": torch.zeros(3, 4), "y": torch.zeros(3)}, auto_batch_size=True)
>>> foo.batch_size
torch.Size([3])
```

from_tensordict(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *non_tensordict: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Wraps a tensordict in a new instance of the tensorclass, without copying the leaves.

If `tensordict` is a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), the entries of the fields
annotated with a tensorclass (or `Optional` of one) that are tensordicts become
instances of that tensorclass, recursively. They are set in a shallow copy of
`tensordict`, which keeps its own entries. An entry with keys that the annotated
class does not declare stays a tensordict. Other backends are wrapped as they are:
setting a tensorclass in them would write to their storage (e.g. an H5 file).

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict that holds the tensor fields.
- **non_tensordict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - the values of the non-tensor fields. The
fields that neither argument holds are set to `None`. Defaults
to `None`.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - deprecated in 0.15, will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.
If `False`, skips the check that `tensordict` is a
[`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase). By default, the check runs, and
another type raises a `RuntimeError`.

Returns:

A new instance of the class, whose fields are the entries of
`tensordict`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Pose(TensorClass):
... q: torch.Tensor
>>> class Obs(TensorClass):
... a: Pose
>>> obs = Obs(a=Pose(q=torch.zeros(5, 4), batch_size=[5]), batch_size=[5])
>>> type(Obs.from_tensordict(obs.to_tensordict()).a).__name__
'Pose'
```

get(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, **args*, ***kwargs*)

Returns the value of a field, or `default` if the key is missing.

`tc.get("x")` is the same as `tc.x`: a non-tensor field returns the
Python object, not a [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData). The keyword
arguments of [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) (`as_list`,
`as_padded_tensor`, ...) are passed to the tensordict that holds the
fields.

Parameters:

- **key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key to read. A tuple reads an entry of a nested
field: `tc.get(("a", "b"))` is `tc.a.get("b")`.
- **default** (*optional*) - the value returned if the key is missing.
Defaults to `None`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... name: str
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3), name="a", batch_size=[3])
>>> foo.get("name")
'a'
>>> foo.get("z", "missing")
'missing'
```

load_memmap_(*prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, ***, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Loads a memory-mapped tensorclass into this instance, and returns `self`.

Works as [`load_memmap_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap_), and also loads
the non-tensor fields.

Parameters:

- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the directory, or the `".tdz"` archive file,
to read.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the key encoding used when the data was
saved. See [`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap). Defaults to
`True`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - whether pickled non-tensor fields may
be loaded. See [`load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap).
Defaults to `None`, which loads pickled fields with a
`FutureWarning`.
- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the mode of the memory maps. See
[`load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap). Defaults to
`None`.

load_state_dict(*state_dict: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*, *strict=True*, *assign=False*, *from_flatten=None*)

Loads a state dict made by `state_dict()` into the tensorclass, and returns `self`.

Works as [`load_state_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_state_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_state_dict), which
describes the arguments, and also loads the non-tensor fields. It also
reads the state dicts of older versions, which hold `"_tensordict"` and
`"_non_tensordict"` entries.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... name: str
>>> sd = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3), name="a", batch_size=[3]).state_dict()
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.ones(3), name="b", batch_size=[3])
>>> _ = foo.load_state_dict(sd)
>>> foo.x, foo.name
(tensor([0., 0., 0.]), 'a')
```

set(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *value: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Sets a field, and returns the tensorclass.

`tc.set("x", value)` is the same as `tc.x = value`: the value is cast
according to the class flags (see `TensorClass`).
Otherwise, it works as [`set()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set).

Parameters:

- **key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the field to set. A tuple sets an entry of a nested
field: `tc.set(("a", "b"), value)` is `tc.a.set("b", value)`.
- **value** (*Any*) - the value of the field.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and the field holds a tensor,
the value is copied into it, which keeps its storage. Defaults to
`False`. See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

- [**AttributeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#AttributeError) - if `key` is not a field of the class.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the tensorclass is locked, also with
 `inplace=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> foo.set("x", torch.ones(3)).x
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
>>> foo.set("z", torch.ones(3))
Traceback (most recent call last):
 ...
AttributeError: Cannot set the attribute 'z': Foo has no such field. Its fields are ['x'].
```

state_dict(*destination=None*, *prefix=''*, *keep_vars=False*, *flatten=True*) → [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

Returns the state dict of the tensorclass.

Works as [`state_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.state_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.state_dict), which describes
the arguments. The tensor fields are the entries of the state dict. The
non-tensor fields and the name of the class go to the `_metadata`
attribute, under the `"_non_tensor"` and `"_type"` keys of their
level.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... name: str
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3), name="a", batch_size=[3])
>>> sd = foo.state_dict()
>>> list(sd.keys())
['x']
>>> sd._metadata[""]["_non_tensor"]
{'name': 'a'}
```

to_tensordict(***, *retain_none: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Returns a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) with a copy of the fields of the tensorclass.

The tensors are copied, and memory-mapped or shared tensors become regular
tensors. Nested tensorclasses become tensordicts, and non-tensor fields
become [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) entries.

Keyword Arguments:

**retain_none** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, fields set to `None` are
written as `None` entries. Defaults to `None`, which drops
them.

Examples

```
>>> from typing import Any
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... y: Any = None
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3))
>>> sorted(foo.to_tensordict().keys())
['x']
>>> sorted(foo.to_tensordict(retain_none=True).keys())
['x', 'y']
```

unbind(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*)

Returns a tuple of tensorclasses, one per index along a batch dimension.

Works as [`unbind()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unbind.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unbind): the results share
the storage of the tensorclass.

Parameters:

**dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch dimension to remove.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.arange(6).reshape(2, 3), batch_size=[2, 3])
>>> [item.x for item in foo.unbind(1)]
[tensor([0, 3]), tensor([1, 4]), tensor([2, 5])]
```

update_(*input_dict_or_td: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *clone: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *keys_to_update: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs*)

Copies the entries of a dictionary, a tensordict or a tensorclass into the existing entries.

Returns `self`. Works as [`update_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_), which describes the
arguments: the existing tensors keep their storage. The fields can also
be passed as keyword arguments, `tc.update_(x=value)`. `inplace` has
no effect.

A tensorclass or dict source ignores `clone`, `non_blocking` and
`keys_to_update`: the entries that `keys_to_update` leaves out are
written too, and the call warns. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default
will change to writing only the entries in `keys_to_update`, as for a
TensorDict source.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> x = foo.x
>>> _ = foo.update_({"x": torch.ones(3)})
>>> x
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```

update_at_(*input_dict_or_td: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | T*, *idx: [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [slice](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#slice) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), ...]*, *clone: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *keys_to_update: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Writes the entries of a dictionary, a tensordict or a tensorclass in place at an index, and returns `self`.

Works as [`update_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_), which describes
the arguments, with one difference. A tensorclass or dict source that
[`update()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update) accepts, such as one with the
batch size of the tensorclass, goes to
[`update()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update) instead: its entries replace
those of the tensorclass whatever the index, and the call warns. Starting
with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to writing such a source in
place at the index, as [`update_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_)
does.

# TensorCollection

*class*tensordict.TensorCollection(**args*, ***kwargs*)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The abstract base class of tensordicts and tensorclasses.

[`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) and [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass)
inherit from it. It cannot be instantiated.

Use it in type hints and `isinstance` checks for "a tensordict or a
tensorclass". Classes decorated with `@tensorclass` do not inherit from
it, only subclasses of [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) do; to check both,
use [`is_tensor_collection()`](tensordict.is_tensor_collection.html#tensordict.is_tensor_collection).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass, TensorCollection, TensorDict
>>> class Data(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> isinstance(td, TensorCollection)
True
>>> isinstance(Data(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]), TensorCollection)
True
>>> isinstance(torch.zeros(3), TensorCollection)
False
```

# TensorDict

`TensorDict` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `TensorDict` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.TensorDict(*source: T | [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*)

Bases: [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

A dictionary of tensors that share a batch size.

The batch size is the leading part of the shape that every entry has in
common. With `batch_size=[3, 4]`, every entry has a shape that starts
with `(3, 4)`. Shape operations (indexing, `reshape`, `view`,
`unsqueeze`, `permute`, masking) act on the batch dimensions of every
entry at once. Pointwise operations (`td + other`, `td * 2`),
`td.to(device)` and `td.to(dtype)` apply to every entry. An entry can
be another tensordict, so keys can be nested: `td["a", "b"]` reads the
entry `"b"` of the nested tensordict `"a"`. [Batch size, shapes, and indexing](../../concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size) and
[Keys, nested keys, and locking](../../concepts/keys.html#keys) explain these ideas.

Use `TensorDict` for most data. To stack tensordicts whose keys or
entry shapes differ, use [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict). To
declare a fixed set of fields with types, use
[`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) or [`TypedTensorDict`](tensordict.TypedTensorDict.html#tensordict.TypedTensorDict).
[Which container should I use?](../../choosing_a_container.html#choosing-a-container) compares the containers.

Build a tensordict from a dict, or from keyword arguments as with
`dict(...)`:

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... {"obs": torch.zeros(3, 4, 5), "reward": torch.zeros(3, 4)},
... batch_size=[3, 4],
... )
>>> td[0]["obs"].shape
torch.Size([4, 5])
>>> td.view(-1)["obs"].shape
torch.Size([12, 5])
>>> (td + 1)["reward"].sum()
tensor(12.)
>>> td.to(torch.float64)["obs"].dtype
torch.float64
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.ones(3, 2)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> td["b", "c"].shape
torch.Size([3, 2])
```

A tensordict has these constraints:

- The batch size is not inferred from the data: it defaults to `[]`.
Call [`auto_batch_size_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_) to set it to
the largest leading shape that all entries share.
- The shape of every entry must start with the batch size. If it does
not, setting the entry raises a `RuntimeError`.
- If `device` is set, every entry is moved to that device. If it is
not set, the entries can be on different devices. See [Devices, dtypes, and memory](../../concepts/devices.html#devices).
- A key is a string, or a tuple of strings for a nested entry. Other keys
raise a `KeyError`.

The values of `source` are stored as given, not copied, except when
they are moved to `device`. A nested `dict` becomes a nested
tensordict with the same batch size. Numbers and arrays become tensors,
and other values such as strings are stored as non-tensor data (see
[Non-tensor data and unbatched entries](../../concepts/non_tensor.html#non-tensor-data)).

Parameters:

- **source** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**Mapping**or*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the entries, read
like a `dict`: string or nested keys to tensors, tensordicts,
nested dicts or other values. Exclusive with `**kwargs`.
Defaults to `None`, which gives an empty tensordict that can be
filled later.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size
of the tensordict: the leading dimensions that all its entries
share. It can be changed later if the entries allow it. Defaults
to `None`, which gives the batch size `[]`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensordict. Entries on another device are moved to it. Defaults to
`None`, which leaves each entry where it is, and the tensordict
has no device.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the batch dimensions, one
per dimension. Defaults to `None`, which leaves the dimensions
unnamed.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - with `device`, if `True`, the
entries are copied to the device asynchronously with respect to
the host, with no synchronization: this is safe only from CPU to
CUDA. If `False`, every copy is synchronous. Defaults to
`None`, which copies asynchronously and synchronizes after the
copies when needed.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict is locked: its
entries cannot be added, removed or replaced. See
[Locking and temporary changes](../../concepts/keys.html#keys-locking). Defaults to `False`.
- ****kwargs** - the entries, as keyword arguments, instead of `source`.

Raises:

- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if both `source` and `**kwargs` are given, or if the
 length of `names` differs from that of `batch_size`.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the shape of an entry does not start with
 `batch_size`.

Examples

Name the batch dimensions. Shape operations keep the names:

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... obs=torch.zeros(3, 4), action=torch.zeros(3, 2), batch_size=[3], names=["time"]
... )
>>> td.names
['time']
>>> td.unsqueeze(0).names
[None, 'time']
```

Set the batch size from the data:

```
>>> td = TensorDict(obs=torch.zeros(3, 4))
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([])
>>> td.auto_batch_size_().batch_size
torch.Size([3, 4])
```

Adding an entry to a locked tensordict raises an error:

```
>>> td = TensorDict(obs=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3], lock=True)
>>> td["action"] = torch.zeros(3)
Traceback (most recent call last):
 ...
RuntimeError: Cannot modify locked TensorDict. For in-place modification, consider using the `set_()` method and make sure the key is present.
```

*classmethod*from_module(*module: [Module](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Returns a tensordict that holds the parameters and buffers of a module.

The entries are the parameters and buffers of the module themselves,
not copies. Submodules become nested tensordicts.

Note

This method does not lock the result by default (`lock=False`).
The function [`tensordict.from_module()`](tensordict.from_module.html#tensordict.from_module) locks it by default
(`lock=True`).

Parameters:

- **module** ([*Module*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `TensorDictParams`
instance is returned, which can be used to store parameters
within a [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `False`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict from the
module is used and unflattened into a TensorDict with
the tree structure of the model. Use it when the module has
state-dict hooks. Defaults to `False`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, submodules without
parameters or buffers (`nn.ReLU`, for example) get no
entry. If `False`, they get an empty tensordict.
Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

A `TensorDict`, or a
`TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> module = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 4), nn.ReLU())
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> params["0", "weight"] is module[0].weight
True
>>> list(params.keys())
['0']
>>> params.is_locked
False
```

# TensorDictBase

The methods of `TensorDictBase` are shared by every tensordict class and
by tensorclasses. They are listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods),
with one page for each method.

*class*tensordict.TensorDictBase(**args*, ***kwargs*)

The abstract base class of every tensordict.

[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict),
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) and the other tensordict classes
subclass it, and tensorclasses have the same methods. You do not create a
`TensorDictBase`: use it in type hints and in `isinstance` checks. A
tensorclass is not an instance of it: use
[`is_tensor_collection()`](tensordict.is_tensor_collection.html#tensordict.is_tensor_collection) to accept both. The methods are
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, TensorDictBase, lazy_stack
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> isinstance(td, TensorDictBase), isinstance(lazy_stack([td, td]), TensorDictBase)
(True, True)
```

# TensorDictBase.__and__

TensorDictBase.__and__(*other: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*) → Self

Computes `self & other` leaf by leaf and returns a new tensordict.

The operation is a logical AND for boolean leaves and a bitwise AND for
integer leaves. A tensordict `other` is paired with the tensordict key
by key and must have the same keys, or a `KeyError` is raised.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the other operand.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]), batch_size=[3])
>>> ((td > 1) & (td < 3))["a"]
tensor([False, True, False])
>>> (~(td > 1))["a"]
tensor([ True, False, False])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.__eq__

TensorDictBase.__eq__(*other: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*) → Self | [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Compares the tensordict with `other` leaf by leaf with `==`.

`other` can be a tensordict or a `dict` with the same keys, paired
with the tensordict key by key (a `KeyError` is raised if the keys
differ); a tensor, which is aligned with the batch dimensions of each
leaf; or a number. A batch size that differs from the tensordict's is
broadcast with it. An `other` of another type, such as `None`,
gives `False`. The other comparisons (`!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`,
`>=`) work the same way.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the value to
compare with.

Returns:

A new tensordict of boolean leaves, or `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0]), b=torch.zeros(2), batch_size=[2])
>>> (td == 1)["a"]
tensor([ True, False])
>>> (td == td.clone()).all()
True
>>> (td >= torch.tensor([2.0, 0.0]))["b"]
tensor([False, True])
>>> td == None
False
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.__getitem__

TensorDictBase.__getitem__(*index: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]*) → Any

TensorDictBase.__getitem__(*index: IndexType*) → Self

Returns the entry at a key, or the tensordict indexed along its batch dimensions.

A string or a tuple of strings reads an entry, as [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) does,
except that a missing key raises `KeyError`. A non-tensor entry
returns its content (the string, not the
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)), and a stack of non-tensor data
returns a list. See [Keys, nested keys, and locking](../../concepts/keys.html#keys).

Any other index (an int, a slice, a tensor, a boolean mask, `...`,
`None`, or a tuple of these) applies to the batch dimensions of every
entry, as it would to a tensor of shape [`batch_size`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.batch_size.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.batch_size), and
returns a tensordict. See [Batch size, shapes, and indexing](../../concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size).

Raises:

[**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if the key is missing.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"root": torch.arange(2), ("nested", "entry"): torch.arange(2)}, [2])
>>> td["root"]
tensor([0, 1])
>>> td["nested", "entry"]
tensor([0, 1])
>>> td[:1].batch_size, td[:1]["nested", "entry"]
(torch.Size([1]), tensor([0]))
>>> td[torch.tensor([True, False])]["root"]
tensor([0])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.abs

TensorDictBase.abs() → Self

Returns a new tensordict with [`torch.abs()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.abs.html#torch.abs) applied to every leaf.

The other unary operations ([`exp()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.exp.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.exp), [`log()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.log.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.log),
[`sqrt()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.sqrt.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.sqrt), [`sin()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.sin.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.sin)...) work the same way. Each has an
in-place twin with a trailing underscore ([`abs_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.abs_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.abs_),
[`exp_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.exp_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.exp_)...) that writes into the leaves and returns `self`.
See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... a=torch.tensor([-1.0, 2.0]),
... b=TensorDict(c=torch.tensor([-3.0, 0.0]), batch_size=[2]),
... batch_size=[2],
... )
>>> td.abs()["b", "c"]
tensor([3., 0.])
>>> td.exp()["a"]
tensor([0.3679, 7.3891])
>>> td.abs_() is td
True
>>> td["a"]
tensor([1., 2.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.add

TensorDictBase.add(*other: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, ***, *alpha: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *default: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with `other`, scaled by `alpha`, added to every leaf.

`td + other` and `other + td` call this method.

\[\text{out}_i = \text{input}_i + \text{alpha} \times \text{other}_i\]

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the value to add. A
tensordict is paired with the tensordict key by key. A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf and expanded over
its feature dimensions. Batch sizes that differ are broadcast
together.

Keyword Arguments:

- **alpha** (*Number**,**optional*) - the multiplier for `other`. Defaults to
`None`, which adds `other` as it is.
- **default** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - what to do with the keys
that only one of the two tensordicts has. `None` requires the
same keys and raises a `KeyError` otherwise.
`"intersection"` computes the keys that both have and drops
the others. A tensor stands in for the missing entry on either
side, and the result has the keys of both. Defaults to `None`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2, 3), b=torch.ones(2), batch_size=[2])
>>> td.add(1, alpha=2)["b"]
tensor([3., 3.])
>>> td.add(torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0]))["a"] # one value per batch element
tensor([[1., 1., 1.],
 [2., 2., 2.]])
>>> other = TensorDict(b=torch.ones(2), c=torch.ones(2), batch_size=[2])
>>> sorted(td.add(other, default="intersection").keys())
['b']
>>> sorted(td.add(other, default=torch.zeros(())).keys())
['a', 'b', 'c']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.add

TensorDictBase.add_(*other: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, ***, *alpha: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Adds `other`, scaled by `alpha`, to every leaf in place and returns `self`.

The in-place version of [`add()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.add.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.add), called by `td += other`. It
has no `default`: a tensordict `other` must have every key of the
tensordict, and its other keys are ignored.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the value to add,
paired with the leaves as in [`add()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.add.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.add).

Keyword Arguments:

**alpha** (*Number**,**optional*) - the multiplier for `other`. Defaults to
`None`, which adds `other` as it is.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.addcdiv

TensorDictBase.addcdiv(*other1: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *other2: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *value: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = 1*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with `value * other1 / other2` added to every leaf.

\[\text{out}_i = \text{input}_i + \text{value} \times \frac{\text{other1}_i}{\text{other2}_i}\]

Parameters:

- **other1** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the numerator. A tensordict
is paired with the tensordict key by key and must have all its
keys. A tensor is aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf
and expanded over its feature dimensions.
- **other2** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the denominator, paired
like `other1`. One of `other1` and `other2` can be a
tensordict and the other a tensor.
- **value** (*Number**,**optional*) - the multiplier for
\(\text{other1} / \text{other2}\). Defaults to `1`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.ones(2), batch_size=[2])
>>> td.addcdiv(torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0]), torch.tensor([2.0, 2.0]), value=2)["x"]
tensor([2., 3.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.all

# TensorDictBase.all_gather

TensorDictBase.all_gather(***, *group: 'torch.distributed.ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

Returns a list with the tensordict of each rank of the group, on every rank.

Every rank of the group must call it. The tensordicts can have different
structures. Each rank consolidates its tensordict (see
[`consolidate()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate)), the metadata is gathered with
[`torch.distributed.all_gather_object()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.all_gather_object), which pickles it, and the
storages with [`torch.distributed.all_gather()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.all_gather). Use it only with ranks
you trust. See [Collectives](../../distributed.html#distributed-collectives).

Keyword Arguments:

**group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - the process group.
Defaults to `None`, the default process group.

Returns:

A list of new consolidated tensordicts, one per rank, in the order of
the ranks.

Examples

This example runs in two processes: add it to the
[runner script of the distributed guide](../../distributed.html#distributed) and
pass it to `run`.

```
def all_gather(rank, world_size):
 local = TensorDict(a=torch.full((3,), float(rank)), batch_size=[3])
 tds = local.all_gather()
 print(rank, [td["a"][0].item() for td in tds]) # [0.0, 1.0] on every rank
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.all_reduce

TensorDictBase.all_reduce(*op=None*, ***, *group: 'torch.distributed.ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *async_op: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Reduces each leaf over all the ranks of the group, in place, so that every rank holds the result.

Every rank of the group must call it, with a tensordict of the same
structure. Each leaf is reduced with [`torch.distributed.all_reduce()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.all_reduce),
for example to sum or average gradients. See
[Collectives](../../distributed.html#distributed-collectives).

Parameters:

**op** ([*ReduceOp*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.ReduceOp)*,**optional*) - the reduction. Defaults to
`None`, which is `torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - the process group.
Defaults to `None`, the default process group.
- **async_op** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, returns the list of `Work`
objects of the reductions without waiting for them: call `wait()`
on each one before you use the tensordict. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

With `async_op=True`, a list of `Work` objects. Otherwise, `None`.

Examples

This example runs in two processes: add it to the
[runner script of the distributed guide](../../distributed.html#distributed) and
pass it to `run`.

```
def all_reduce(rank, world_size):
 td = TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3) * rank, batch_size=[3])
 td.all_reduce(op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM)
 print(rank, td["a"]) # with 2 ranks: tensor([1., 1., 1.]) on every rank
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.amax

TensorDictBase.amax(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | NO_DEFAULT = NO_DEFAULT*, *keepdim: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *reduce: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the maximum of every leaf, over all its elements or along a batch dimension.

Like [`max()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.max.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.max) with `return_indices=False`: the result holds the
values only.

Parameters:

- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch dimension to reduce. A negative `dim`
counts from the end of the batch dimensions. A tuple reduces only
its first dimension and is not checked against the batch dimensions.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to reducing
every dimension of the tuple, as [`torch.amax()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.amax.html#torch.amax) does. Defaults
to `None`, which reduces every element of each leaf, and the
result has an empty batch size.
- **keepdim** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the reduced batch dimension is
kept with size 1. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

**reduce** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reduces all the leaves together
and returns a single tensor. Without `dim`, the result is a
scalar. With `dim`, the leaves are concatenated along `dim`
first, so they must have the same number of dimensions. With feature
dimensions, a negative `dim` counts from the end of each leaf.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to counting
it from the end of the batch dimensions, as with `reduce=False`.
Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A new tensordict, or a tensor if `reduce=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([[1.0, 5.0], [3.0, 2.0]]), batch_size=[2])
>>> td.amax()["a"]
tensor(5.)
>>> td.amax(dim=0)["a"]
tensor([3., 5.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.apply

TensorDictBase.apply(*fn: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)*, **others: T*, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = NO_DEFAULT*, *names: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = NO_DEFAULT*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *default: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = NO_DEFAULT*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *propagate_lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *call_on_nested: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *is_leaf: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)], [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***constructor_kwargs*) → Self | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Applies a callable to every leaf and returns a new tensordict with the results.

`fn` is called on each tensor leaf, in the nested tensordicts too, and
its result is stored under the same key. If `fn` returns `None`, the
entry is left out of the result, which can be used to filter entries.
With `others`, `fn` receives the leaf of each tensordict under the
same key. For a callable that also receives the key, see
[`named_apply()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.named_apply.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.named_apply).

Parameters:

- **fn** (*Callable*) - the function called on each leaf, as
`fn(leaf, *other_leaves)`. It returns a tensor, a tensordict,
or `None` to leave the entry out.
- ***others** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - other tensordicts with the same structure
as the tensordict. An entry that one of them lacks raises
`KeyError`, unless `default` is given.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result, for a `fn` that changes the shape of the leaves:
the results must have it as their leading dimensions. `fn` is
then not called on [`UnbatchedTensor`](tensordict.UnbatchedTensor.html#tensordict.UnbatchedTensor) entries,
which keep their data and take the new batch size. Defaults to
`None`, which keeps the batch size of the tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. The results of `fn` are moved to it. `None` gives a
result with no device, which leaves each result where `fn`
put it. By default, the result has the device of the
tensordict.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the batch dimensions of
the result, one per dimension. By default, the names of the
tensordict are kept, or dropped if `batch_size` is given.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the results are written into
the existing leaves of the tensordict (as [`set_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_) does),
and `self` is returned. See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).
Defaults to `False`.
- **default** (*Any**,**optional*) - the value passed to `fn` for an entry
that one of `others` lacks. By default, a missing entry raises
`KeyError`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a nested tensordict
with no entry in the result (because `fn` returned `None`
for all its leaves, or because it was already empty) is left
out. If `False`, it is kept, empty. Defaults to `None`,
which leaves out the nested tensordicts that `fn` emptied and
keeps those that were already empty. Non-tensor data that
`fn` is not called on is kept in all cases.
- **propagate_lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the result of a locked
tensordict is locked too. Defaults to `False`.
- **call_on_nested** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `fn` is called on the
top-level entries, nested tensordicts and tensorclasses
included, and is responsible for going into them. If `False`,
`fn` is called on the leaves only. Defaults to `False`.
- **is_leaf** (*Callable**,**optional*) - called with the type of each entry:
`fn` is called on the entries for which it returns `True`,
and `apply` goes into the others. Defaults to `None`, which
uses [`default_is_leaf()`](tensordict.default_is_leaf.html#tensordict.default_is_leaf): `fn` is called on
tensors, and non-tensor data is kept unchanged. Pass
[`is_leaf_nontensor()`](tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor.html#tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor) to call `fn` on
non-tensor data too.
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the results
into, instead of a new one. When `batch_size` or `device` is
given, `out` must have it. For a lazy stack, `out` must be a
lazy stack too, stacked along any dimension. See the warning
below about `out=self`. Defaults to `None`.
- ****constructor_kwargs** - accepted and ignored.

Returns:

A new tensordict, `out` if it is given, or `self` if
`inplace=True`. `None` if `fn` returns `None` for every
leaf and `filter_empty` is not `False`. With
`filter_empty=None`, a tensordict that is already empty gives an
empty tensordict.

The result has the type of the tensordict for a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), a lazy stack and a tensorclass.
Other types, for example [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict)
or a memory-mapped tensordict, give a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)
that lives in memory. A locked tensordict gives an unlocked result
unless `propagate_lock=True`.

Warning

With `out=self`, the results are silently wrong if
`fn` reads other entries of the tensordict, which may already be
overwritten.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... a=-torch.ones(3),
... b=TensorDict(c=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3]),
... batch_size=[3],
... )
>>> td.apply(lambda x: x + 1)["b", "c"]
tensor([2., 2., 2.])
```

With another tensordict, `fn` receives one leaf of each:

```
>>> td.apply(lambda x, y: x + y, td)["a"]
tensor([-2., -2., -2.])
```

Returning `None` leaves the entry out:

```
>>> out = td.apply(lambda x: x if x.sum() > 0 else None)
>>> list(out.keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True))
[('b', 'c')]
```

A `fn` that changes the shape of the leaves needs a `batch_size`:

```
>>> td.apply(lambda x: x.unsqueeze(-1), batch_size=[3, 1]).batch_size
torch.Size([3, 1])
```

By default, `fn` is not called on non-tensor data:

```
>>> from tensordict import is_leaf_nontensor
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b="a string", batch_size=[3])
>>> seen = []
>>> _ = td.apply(lambda x: seen.append(type(x).__name__))
>>> seen
['Tensor']
>>> seen = []
>>> _ = td.apply(lambda x: seen.append(type(x).__name__), is_leaf=is_leaf_nontensor)
>>> seen
['Tensor', 'NonTensorData']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.apply

TensorDictBase.apply_(*fn: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)*, **others*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Applies a callable to every leaf and writes the results into the existing leaves.

Same as [`apply()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply) with `inplace=True`: each result is copied
into the leaf it comes from (as [`set_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_) does), so the leaves
keep their storage.

Parameters:

- **fn** (*Callable*) - the function called on each tensor leaf. It returns
a tensor that can be copied into the leaf.
- ***others** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - other tensordicts with the same
structure. `fn` receives the leaf of each, after the leaf of
the tensordict, under the same key.
- ****kwargs** - the keyword arguments of [`apply()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply).

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b=TensorDict(c=torch.ones(3)))
>>> a = td["a"]
>>> _ = td.apply_(lambda x: x + 1)
>>> a
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
>>> td["b", "c"]
tensor([2., 2., 2.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).
