# TensorDictBase.arecv

*async*TensorDictBase.arecv(*src: [TensorDictPipe](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe)*, ***, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Receives a tensordict from a UCXX pipe, into the tensordict if possible, asynchronously.

Awaits `src.arecv(self, device=device)`. If the tensordict is
consolidated with the layout of the received data, the data is written
into its storage. Otherwise, the pipe returns another tensordict: use the
return value. See [`TensorDictPipe`](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe), which needs
the optional `ucxx` package.

Parameters:

**src** ([*TensorDictPipe*](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe)) - the pipe to receive from.

Keyword Arguments:

**device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the storage
that the pipe allocates for a new structure. Defaults to `None`,
which uses the device of the sender with a consolidated pipe, and
the CPU otherwise.

Returns:

The received tensordict, `self` or another tensordict.

See also

[`recv()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.recv.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.recv), which also takes a pipe, and works without
`await`.

Examples

This example needs `ucxx` and a sender on the other end of the pipe:

```
async def consume(pipe):
 td = await TensorDict().arecv(pipe) # first receive: allocates
 for _ in range(9):
 td = await td.arecv(pipe) # same structure: writes into td
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.as_tensor

TensorDictBase.as_tensor() → Self

Returns a tensordict whose leaves are converted with their `as_tensor()` method, if they have one.

The leaves without an `as_tensor()` method, [`torch.Tensor`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)
and [`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) included, are kept as they
are. No tensordict leaf type defines `as_tensor()`, so the result
holds the same leaves as the tensordict. A locked tensordict gives a
locked result.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.asend

*async*TensorDictBase.asend(*dst: [TensorDictPipe](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe)*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Sends the tensordict through a UCXX pipe, asynchronously.

Awaits `dst.asend(self)`. See [`TensorDictPipe`](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe),

**dst** ([*TensorDictPipe*](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe)) - the pipe to send through.

# TensorDictBase.atleast_1d

TensorDictBase.atleast_1d()

Returns the tensordict with at least 1 batch dimension.

If the tensordict already has 1 or more batch dimensions, it is
returned as it is. Otherwise, a dimension of size 1 is prepended. The
leaves of the result are views of the original leaves.

It can be used as a context manager, as [`unsqueeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze) can.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3)}, batch_size=[])
>>> print(td.atleast_1d().shape)
torch.Size([1])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.atleast_2d

TensorDictBase.atleast_2d()

Returns the tensordict with at least 2 batch dimensions.

If the tensordict already has 2 or more batch dimensions, it is
returned as it is. Otherwise, dimensions of size 1 are prepended to
reach 2 dimensions. The leaves of the result are views of the original
leaves.

It can be used as a context manager, as [`unsqueeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze) can.

Examples

```
>>> import torch

```

# TensorDictBase.atleast_3d

TensorDictBase.atleast_3d()

Returns the tensordict with at least 3 batch dimensions.

If the tensordict already has 3 or more batch dimensions, it is
returned as it is. Otherwise, dimensions of size 1 are prepended to
reach 3 dimensions. The leaves of the result are views of the original
leaves. Unlike [`torch.atleast_3d()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.atleast_3d.html#torch.atleast_3d), the new dimensions always come
first.

It can be used as a context manager, as [`unsqueeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze) can.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> print(td.atleast_3d().shape)
torch.Size([1, 1, 3])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.attrs

TensorDictBase.attrs(***, *fields: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] = ('device', 'dtype', 'shape')*, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a tensordict that describes each tensor leaf with a [`TensorAttrs`](tensordict.TensorAttrs.html#tensordict.TensorAttrs).

Each tensor leaf is replaced by a [`TensorAttrs`](tensordict.TensorAttrs.html#tensordict.TensorAttrs) that
records its device, dtype and shape. The result has an empty batch size
and no device. Pass it to [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) to cast another tensordict leaf
by leaf, to the device and dtype of the matching leaf, when the leaves
do not all share one device or dtype.

Keyword Arguments:

- **fields** (*sequence**of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the attributes to record, any
subset of `("device", "dtype", "shape")`. The others are
`None`. Defaults to `("device", "dtype", "shape")`.
- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that build the
result. Defaults to `None`, which uses the calling thread
only.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... {"a": torch.zeros(3, device="cpu"),
... "b": torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int32)},
... batch_size=[3],
... )
>>> attrs = td.attrs(fields=("device", "dtype"))
>>> target = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, device="cpu"), b=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> out = target.to(attrs) # casts "b" to int32
>>> out["b"].dtype
torch.int32
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size

TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_(*batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *keep_compliant_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Sets the batch size to the largest leading shape that all the entries share.

The nested tensordicts get their own largest batch size first. Nested
lazy stacks keep their batch size, and a lazy stack itself raises a
`RuntimeError` if its batch size would change. See
[Batch size, shapes, and indexing](../../concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size).

Parameters:

- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the maximum number of batch dimensions,
for the tensordict and for each nested tensordict. Defaults to
`None`, which sets no maximum.
- **keep_compliant_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `batch_dims`
is passed, a nested tensordict that already has `batch_dims`
batch dimensions or more keeps its batch size. Defaults to
`False`.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3, 4, 5), "b": {"c": torch.zeros(3, 4, 6)}}, batch_size=[])
>>> _ = td.auto_batch_size_()
>>> td.batch_size, td["b"].batch_size
(torch.Size([3, 4]), torch.Size([3, 4, 6]))
>>> _ = td.auto_batch_size_(batch_dims=1)
>>> td.batch_size, td["b"].batch_size
(torch.Size([3]), torch.Size([3]))
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.auto_device

TensorDictBase.auto_device_() → Self

Sets the device of the tensordict to the device of its leaves, if they all share one.

If the leaves are on several devices, the device is set to `None`.
The nested tensordicts get the same device. The leaves are not moved.
See [Devices, dtypes, and memory](../../concepts/devices.html#devices).

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> print(td.device)
None
>>> td.auto_device_().device
device(type='cpu')
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.backward

TensorDictBase.backward(*gradient: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *retain_graph: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *create_graph: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inputs: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Computes the gradients of the leaves of the tensordict that require gradients.

Like [`torch.Tensor.backward()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.backward.html#torch.Tensor.backward) for every leaf at once: the leaves
that require gradients, nested ones included, are differentiated in a
single [`torch.autograd.backward()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.backward.html#torch.autograd.backward) call, and the others are
ignored. The gradients are accumulated in the `.grad` of the graph
leaves, as usual. Returns `None`.

Without `gradient`, every leaf that requires gradients must have a
single element, and its gradient is `1`: `td.backward()` is then
the same as `td.sum(reduce=True).backward()`.

Parameters:

- **gradient** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the gradient of each leaf, under
the same nested key and with the same shape. The leaves can
differ in shape, dtype and device. Defaults to `None`, which
needs single-element leaves.
- **retain_graph** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, the graph used to
compute the gradients is freed. Defaults to `None`, which
takes the value of `create_graph`.
- **create_graph** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the graph of the
derivative is built, for higher-order derivatives. Defaults to
`False`.
- **inputs** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**sequence**of*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**optional*) - the
tensors whose `.grad` receives the gradients; the others are
ignored. Defaults to `None`, which accumulates into all the
graph leaves used to compute the leaves of the tensordict.

Raises:

- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if no leaf requires gradients, if `gradient` is not
 given and a leaf has more than one element, or if a gradient
 has the wrong shape.
- [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if `gradient` has no entry for a leaf that requires
 gradients.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> x = torch.ones(3, requires_grad=True)
>>> losses = TensorDict(actor_loss=x.sum(), critic_loss=x.pow(2).sum())
>>> losses.backward() # a gradient of 1 for each single-element leaf
>>> x.grad
tensor([3., 3., 3.])
```

Weight the losses with a gradient tensordict:

```
>>> x.grad = None
>>> losses = TensorDict(actor_loss=x.sum(), critic_loss=x.pow(2).sum())
>>> weights = TensorDict(actor_loss=torch.tensor(0.5), critic_loss=torch.tensor(1.0))
>>> losses.backward(weights)
>>> x.grad
tensor([2.5000, 2.5000, 2.5000])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.batch_size

*property*TensorDictBase.batch_size*: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*

The batch size of the tensordict, as a [`torch.Size`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size). `shape` is the same attribute.

The batch size is the shape of the leading dimensions that all tensors
in the tensordict share. The other dimensions of each tensor are its
feature dimensions. For example, a batch of videos of shape
`[B, T, C, W, H]` can have batch size `[B, T]` (batch and time)
and feature dimensions `[C, W, H]` (channels and space).

You set the batch size when you create the tensordict. The batch size
is not inferred from the tensors unless you ask for it, with
`TensorDict.from_dict(..., auto_batch_size=True)` or
[`auto_batch_size_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_).

You can assign a new batch size if every tensor has the new leading
dimensions. Otherwise, the assignment raises `RuntimeError`. An empty
batch size `()` always fits a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). A
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) raises `RuntimeError` for
any new batch size. A nested tensordict with fewer batch dimensions than
the new batch size gets the new batch size. The other nested tensordicts
keep theirs. See [Batch size, shapes, and indexing](../../concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict({
... "key 0": torch.zeros(3, 4),
... "key 1": torch.zeros(3, 5),
... "nested": TensorDict({"key 0": torch.zeros(3, 4)}, batch_size=[3, 4])},
... batch_size=[3])
>>> data.batch_size
torch.Size([3])
>>> data.batch_size = () # an empty batch size always fits
>>> data.batch_size, data["nested"].batch_size
(torch.Size([]), torch.Size([3, 4]))
>>> data.batch_size = [4]
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
RuntimeError: the Tensor key 0 has shape torch.Size([3, 4]) which is incompatible with the batch-size torch.Size([4]).
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.bfloat16

TensorDictBase.bfloat16(***, *cast_filter: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a tensordict whose tensor leaves are cast to `torch.bfloat16`.

Keyword Arguments:

**cast_filter** (*Callable**,**optional*) - a predicate
`fn(key, value) -> bool` that selects the tensor leaves to
cast, as in [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to). Defaults to `None`, which casts every
tensor leaf (a tensorclass uses its own `cast_filter`, if it
declares one).

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.bitwise_and

TensorDictBase.bitwise_and(*other: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, ***, *default: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with the bitwise AND of every leaf and `other`.

\[\text{out}_i = \text{input}_i \land \text{other}_i\]

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the other operand. A
tensordict is paired with the tensordict key by key. A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf and expanded over
its feature dimensions. Batch sizes that differ are broadcast
together.

Keyword Arguments:

**default** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - what to do with the keys
that only one of the two tensordicts has. `None` requires the
same keys and raises a `KeyError` otherwise.
`"intersection"` computes the keys that both have and drops
the others. A tensor stands in for the missing entry on either
side, and the result has the keys of both. Defaults to `None`.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.broadcast

TensorDictBase.broadcast(*src: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, ***, *group: 'torch.distributed.ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *_tensorclass_type: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Sends the tensordict of rank `src` to every rank of the group, and returns it on each rank.

Every rank of the group must call it. The other ranks do not need to know
the structure: they can call it on an empty tensordict. Rank `src`
consolidates its tensordict (see [`consolidate()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate)), and broadcasts the
metadata with [`torch.distributed.broadcast_object_list()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.broadcast_object_list), which
pickles it, then the storage as one tensor. The other ranks build a new
tensordict from them. Use it only with ranks you trust. See
[Collectives](../../distributed.html#distributed-collectives).

Parameters:

**src** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the rank that sends its tensordict.

Keyword Arguments:

- **group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - the process group.
Defaults to `None`, the default process group.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - on rank `src`, the
device of the consolidated storage, if the tensordict is not
consolidated yet. On the other ranks, the device of the result.
With `nccl`, pass a CUDA device. Defaults to `None`, which keeps
the device of the tensordict on rank `src`, and uses the same
device on the other ranks.

Returns:

The consolidated tensordict of rank `src`. On rank `src`, it is
the tensordict itself if it is consolidated already, and a
consolidated copy otherwise. On the other ranks, it is a new
tensordict.

Examples

This example runs in two processes: add it to the
[runner script of the distributed guide](../../distributed.html#distributed) and
pass it to `run`.

```
def broadcast(rank, world_size):
 td = TensorDict(a=torch.arange(3.0), batch_size=[3]) if rank == 0 else TensorDict()
 td = td.broadcast(src=0)
 print(rank, td["a"]) # tensor([0., 1., 2.]) on every rank
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.broadcast_to

TensorDictBase.broadcast_to(*shape: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), ...]*)

Returns the tensordict broadcast to the batch size `shape`, as [`torch.broadcast_to()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.broadcast_to.html#torch.broadcast_to) does.

As for [`expand()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.expand.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.expand), the new shape can add leading dimensions and
expand the dimensions of size 1, and `-1` keeps the size of a
dimension. The leaves of the result are views of the original leaves,
and the result has no names.

Parameters:

**shape** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)) - the new batch size.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.arange(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> print(td.broadcast_to((2, 3)).shape)
torch.Size([2, 3])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.bytes

TensorDictBase.bytes(***, *count_duplicates: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

Returns the number of bytes of the tensor leaves.

Each tensor leaf counts `numel() * dtype.itemsize` bytes, and a leaf
with a gradient counts the bytes of its gradient too. Non-tensor data
is not counted. A view counts the bytes of its own elements, not those
of the storage it shares.

Keyword Arguments:

**count_duplicates** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a tensor stored
under several keys is counted once per key. If `False`, it
is counted once. Two different views of one tensor are counted
twice in both cases. Defaults to `True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> x = torch.zeros(6)
>>> td = TensorDict(a=x, b=x, c=torch.zeros(2, 3))
>>> td.bytes()
72
>>> td.bytes(count_duplicates=False)
48
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.cat

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.cat(*input*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*)

Concatenates tensordicts along an existing batch dimension `dim`.

It is equivalent to [`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat), and also works under
[`torch.compile()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile.html#torch.compile). The tensordicts must have the same keys, or a
`KeyError` is raised, and the same batch size except along `dim`.

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordicts to concatenate.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch dimension to concatenate along.
Defaults to `0`.

Keyword Arguments:

**out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into. Defaults to `None`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> a = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> b = TensorDict(x=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> TensorDict.cat([a, b]).batch_size
torch.Size([6])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.cat_from_tensordict

TensorDictBase.cat_from_tensordict(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *sorted: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Concatenates all the leaves of the tensordict into one tensor, with [`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat).

Parameters:

**dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension to concatenate along, counted
in the dimensions of the leaves. Defaults to `0`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **sorted** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the order of the
leaves. `True` sorts the keys alphabetically, and `False`
or `None` keeps the order of insertion. A list of keys gives
the order, and must hold every leaf key, or a
`RuntimeError` is raised. Defaults to `None`.
- **out** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**optional*) - a tensor to write the result into.
Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

The concatenated tensor.

See also

[`pack()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.pack.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.pack), which flattens leaves of any shape into one
tensor and returns the layout to rebuild the tensordict.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2, 1), b=torch.ones(2, 2), batch_size=[2])
>>> td.cat_from_tensordict(dim=1)
tensor([[0., 1., 1.],
 [0., 1., 1.]])
>>> td.cat_from_tensordict(dim=1, sorted=["b", "a"])
tensor([[1., 1., 0.],
 [1., 1., 0.]])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.cat_tensors

TensorDictBase.cat_tensors(**keys: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *out_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *keep_entries: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Concatenates entries of the tensordict into a new entry, and removes them by default.

Parameters:

***keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the entries to concatenate, with
[`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat).

Keyword Arguments:

- **out_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key of the result.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension to concatenate along, counted
in the dimensions of the entries. Defaults to `0`.
- **keep_entries** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, removes the entries
of `keys` once the result is written. If the concatenation or
the write fails, every entry is kept with its original value.
Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(1), b=torch.ones(1))
>>> _ = td.cat_tensors("a", "b", out_key="c")
>>> assert "a" not in td
>>> assert (td["c"] == torch.tensor([0, 1])).all()
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.chunk

TensorDictBase.chunk(*chunks: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection), ...]

Splits the tensordict into `chunks` pieces along a batch dimension, as [`torch.chunk()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.chunk.html#torch.chunk) does.

Each piece has `ceil(batch_size[dim] / chunks)` elements, except the
last one, which can be smaller. So there can be fewer than `chunks`
pieces. The pieces hold views of the original tensors.

Parameters:

- **chunks** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the number of pieces.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch dimension to split. Defaults to
`0`.

Returns:

A tuple of tensordicts.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.arange(5), batch_size=[5])
>>> [t["x"] for t in td.chunk(2)]
[tensor([0, 1, 2]), tensor([3, 4])]
>>> [t["x"] for t in td.chunk(4)]
[tensor([0, 1]), tensor([2, 3]), tensor([4])]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.clamp

TensorDictBase.clamp(*min: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *max: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *out=None*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with every leaf clamped into the range `[min, max]`.

\[y_i = \min(\max(x_i, \text{min}_i), \text{max}_i)\]

Where `min` is greater than `max`, the result is `max`, as with
[`torch.clamp()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.clamp.html#torch.clamp). At least one of `min` and `max` must be given;
with only one bound, `clamp` calls [`clamp_min()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_min.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_min) or
[`clamp_max()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_max.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_max).

Parameters:

- **min** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**Number**or**None**,**optional*) - the
lower bound. A tensordict is paired with the tensordict key by
key. `min` and `max` must both be tensordicts, or neither.
Defaults to `None`, which sets no lower bound.
- **max** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**Number**or**None**,**optional*) - the
upper bound. `min` and `max` must both be tensordicts, or
neither. Defaults to `None`, which sets no upper bound.

Keyword Arguments:

**out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the tensordict to write the result
into, and the one returned. The result is copied into its
leaves, so `out` must have the keys, shapes and dtypes of
the result. Defaults to `None`.

Raises:

- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if one of `min` and `max` is a tensordict and the
 other is not, or if `out` is given and both `min` and
 `max` are `None`.
- [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if `out` does not have the keys of the result.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if a leaf of `out` does not have the dtype of the
 result, as with [`torch.clamp()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.clamp.html#torch.clamp).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.tensor([-2.0, 0.5, 3.0]), batch_size=[3])
>>> td.clamp(0.0, 1.0)["x"]
tensor([0.0000, 0.5000, 1.0000])
>>> td.clamp(max=0.0)["x"]
tensor([-2., 0., 0.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.clamp_max

TensorDictBase.clamp_max(*other: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, ***, *default: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with every leaf clamped to at most `other`.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the upper bound. A
tensordict is paired with the tensordict key by key. A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf and expanded over
its feature dimensions. Batch sizes that differ are broadcast
together.

Keyword Arguments:

**default** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - what to do with the keys
that only one of the two tensordicts has. `None` requires the
same keys and raises a `KeyError` otherwise.
`"intersection"` computes the keys that both have and drops
the others. A tensor stands in for the missing entry on either
side, and the result has the keys of both. Defaults to `None`.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.clamp_max

TensorDictBase.clamp_max_(*other: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*) → Self

Clamps every leaf to at most `other` in place and returns `self`.

The in-place version of [`clamp_max()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_max.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_max). It has no `default`: a
tensordict `other` must have every key of the tensordict, and its
other keys are ignored.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the upper bound,
paired with the leaves as in [`clamp_max()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_max.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_max). A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf, except when
a leaf is an [`UnbatchedTensor`](tensordict.UnbatchedTensor.html#tensordict.UnbatchedTensor) or inside a
[`torch.func`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/func.api.html#module-torch.func) transform such as [`torch.vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap): then
every leaf broadcasts with it from the right, as in torch.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.clamp_min

TensorDictBase.clamp_min(*other: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *default: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with every leaf clamped to at least `other`.

Parameters:

- **other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the lower bound. A
tensordict is paired with the tensordict key by key. A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf and expanded over
its feature dimensions. Batch sizes that differ are broadcast
together.
- **default** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - what to do with the keys
that only one of the two tensordicts has. `None` requires the
same keys and raises a `KeyError` otherwise.
`"intersection"` computes the keys that both have and drops
the others. A tensor stands in for the missing entry on either
side, and the result has the keys of both. Defaults to `None`.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.clamp_min

TensorDictBase.clamp_min_(*other: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*) → Self

Clamps every leaf to at least `other` in place and returns `self`.

The in-place version of [`clamp_min()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_min.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_min). It has no `default`: a
tensordict `other` must have every key of the tensordict, and its
other keys are ignored.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the lower bound,
paired with the leaves as in [`clamp_min()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_min.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.clamp_min). A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf, except when
a leaf is an [`UnbatchedTensor`](tensordict.UnbatchedTensor.html#tensordict.UnbatchedTensor) or inside a
[`torch.func`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/func.api.html#module-torch.func) transform such as [`torch.vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap): then
every leaf broadcasts with it from the right, as in torch.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.clear_device

TensorDictBase.clear_device_() → Self

Sets the device of the tensordict and its sub-tensordicts to `None`, and returns it.

The leaves are not moved. After this call, you can set leaves on any
device. See [Devices, dtypes, and memory](../../concepts/devices.html#devices).

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3], device="cpu")
>>> td = td.clear_device_()
>>> print(td.device)
None
>>> td["a"].device

```

# TensorDictBase.clear_refs_for_compile

TensorDictBase.clear_refs_for_compile_() → Self

Clears the record of the last operation of the tensordict and its nested tensordicts.

The tensordict records its last operation, with a weak reference to its

# TensorDictBase.clone

TensorDictBase.clone(*recurse: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Returns a copy of the tensordict, of the same type.

With `recurse=True`, every tensor leaf is copied. The result is not
locked, even if the tensordict is: a clone is usually made to be
modified. To get a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) from any other type,
call [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict) instead.

Parameters:

- **recurse** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the leaves are copied too.
If `False`, only the tree of nested tensordicts is copied:
the nested tensordicts are new objects, and the leaves are the
same tensors as in the tensordict. Defaults to `True`.
- ****kwargs** - options of the class, for example `newfile`, the
destination file of a [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict)
cloned with `recurse=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3), "b": {"c": torch.ones(3)}}, [3])
>>> td_clone = td.clone()
>>> td_clone["a"] is td["a"]
False
>>> td_shallow = td.clone(recurse=False)
>>> td_shallow["a"] is td["a"], td_shallow["b"] is td["b"]
(True, False)
>>> td.lock_().clone().is_locked
False
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.consolidate

TensorDictBase.consolidate(*filename: [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *num_threads=0*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *return_early: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *use_buffer: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *share_memory: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *pin_memory: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *metadata: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Copies all the leaves into one contiguous storage, and returns a tensordict of views of it.

A consolidated tensordict pickles and moves between devices faster,
because its leaves are one block of memory: [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to),
[`pickle`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html#module-pickle), [`send()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.send.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.send) and [`broadcast()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast) move that block
in one copy. The result is locked (see [Locking and temporary changes](../../concepts/keys.html#keys-locking)): you can
write into its leaves in place, but you cannot add or remove entries.

If the tensordict is already consolidated, `self` is returned and
the other arguments are ignored. A `filename` other than its own
file writes nothing: `td.contiguous().consolidate(filename=other)`
writes a new file.

Parameters:

**filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path**,**optional*) - a file to use as the storage. The
leaves are views into a memory map of the file, and the
metadata is written after them, so that
[`from_consolidated()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_consolidated.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_consolidated) can read the file back. Defaults to
`None`, which keeps the storage in memory.

Keyword Arguments:

- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that copy the
leaves into the storage, by chunks of about equal size. When
`filename` is given, `return_early=False` and all the
leaves are on the CPU, one copy is faster and `num_threads`
is ignored. Defaults to `0`, which copies in the calling
thread.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
storage. Exclusive with `filename`, unless it is `"cpu"`.
Defaults to `None`, which uses the device of the tensordict,
or the CPU if it has none.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the leaves of the tensordict
are replaced by the views, and `self` is returned. Defaults
to `False`.
- **return_early** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `num_threads > 1`,
returns a [`TensorDictFuture`](tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture.html#tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture) at once,
while the threads copy the leaves: `future.result()` waits
for them and returns the tensordict. Not supported with
`use_buffer=True` or `non_blocking=True`. Defaults to
`False`.
- **use_buffer** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `filename` is given,
the leaves are copied into a buffer in shared memory, which is
written to the file at the end. This can be faster on a remote
file system (for example NFS). In-place writes into the leaves
then do not reach the file. Defaults to `False`.
- **share_memory** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the storage is placed
in shared memory. Defaults to `False`.
- **pin_memory** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the storage is placed in
pinned memory. Defaults to `False`.
- **metadata** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the structure of the
tensordict is stored with the storage, which changes how the
result is pickled; [`send()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.send.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.send) and [`init_remote()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.init_remote.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.init_remote) use
it. It is always stored when `filename` is given. Defaults to
`False`.

Returns:

A consolidated tensordict, `self` if `inplace=True`, or a
[`TensorDictFuture`](tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture.html#tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture) of it if
`return_early=True` and `num_threads > 1`.

Note

The file written with `filename` holds the batch sizes and names
at the time of the call. Setting `batch_size` or `names` on the
result later does not change the file: call
`consolidate(filename=filename)` again on the result to write
them. Likewise, a pickle of the result is rebuilt from metadata
recorded here: setting the batch size of a nested tensordict, as in
`td["nested"].batch_size = ...`, may not update it until
`consolidate()` is called again.

Examples

```
>>> import pickle
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": {"c": torch.zeros(())}})
>>> data_consolidated = data.consolidate()
>>> # All the leaves share one storage.
>>> assert torch.tensor([
... v.untyped_storage().data_ptr() for v in data_consolidated.values(True, True)
... ]).unique().numel() == 1
>>> data_consolidated.is_consolidated(), data_consolidated.is_locked
(True, True)
>>> # A consolidated tensordict pickles as one buffer.
>>> restored = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(data_consolidated))
>>> (restored == data).all()
True
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.contiguous

TensorDictBase.contiguous(***, *canonical: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with contiguous leaves.

Each leaf is replaced by [`torch.Tensor.contiguous()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.contiguous.html#torch.Tensor.contiguous): a leaf that
is already contiguous is shared with the tensordict, the others are
copied.

Keyword Arguments:

- **canonical** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a leaf whose strides are
not the row-major strides of its shape is copied too, even if
[`torch.Tensor.is_contiguous()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.is_contiguous.html#torch.Tensor.is_contiguous) returns `True` for it (as
it can with dimensions of size 1). Defaults to `False`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict keeps its
identity and keys, each leaf that is not contiguous is replaced
by a contiguous copy, and `self` is returned. See
[In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions). Defaults to `False`.

Note

On a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict), a
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) (h5, zarr) or a store,
the result is a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). If the tensordicts
of a lazy stack have no names, the result has no names either,
even when the stack dimension has a name (from `stack_dim_name`
or the `names` setter). [`densify()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.densify.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.densify) and
[`clone()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.clone.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.clone) keep that name. To keep it here, name the dimension
again with [`refine_names()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, lazy_stack
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(4, 3).T, batch_size=[3])
>>> td.is_contiguous(), td.contiguous().is_contiguous()
(False, True)
```

On a lazy stack, the result loses the name of the stack dimension:

```
>>> stack = lazy_stack(
... [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]) for _ in range(2)],
... stack_dim_name="s",
... )
>>> stack.names, stack.contiguous().names
(['s', None], [None, None])
>>> stack.contiguous().refine_names("s", ...).names
['s', None]
>>> stack.densify().names
['s', None]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.copy

TensorDictBase.copy() → Self

Returns a shallow copy of the tensordict: a new structure that holds the same leaves.

The same as `td.clone(recurse=False)`. The nested tensordicts are new
objects, but the leaves are the same tensors: an in-place change to a
leaf shows in both.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.zeros(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> c = td.copy()
>>> c["a"] is td["a"], c["b"] is td["b"]
(True, False)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.copy

TensorDictBase.copy_(*tensordict: T*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Copies the entries of `tensordict` into the existing entries, and returns `self`.

The same as [`update_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_), under the name of
[`torch.Tensor.copy_()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.copy_.html#torch.Tensor.copy_): the existing tensors keep their storage,
and every key of `tensordict` must exist in the tensordict.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the entries to copy.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.

Raises:

- [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if a key of `tensordict` is missing from the
 tensordict.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if a value does not fit the shape of its entry.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> x = torch.zeros(3)
>>> td = TensorDict(x=x, batch_size=[3])
>>> _ = td.copy_(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3]))
>>> x
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.copy_at

TensorDictBase.copy_at_(*tensordict: T*, *idx: [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [slice](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#slice) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), ...]*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *fast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → Self

Copies the tensors of `tensordict` into the existing entries at `idx`, and returns `self`.

`copy_at_` is a faster [`update_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_) for the hot paths where
every key of `tensordict` is a tensor entry of the tensordict. With
`fast=True`, a `tensordict` with only non-tensor entries raises a
`RuntimeError`. If it also holds tensors, its non-tensor entries are
skipped, not copied, with a `FutureWarning`: starting with
TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to raising the same
`RuntimeError`. Use `fast=False` or [`update_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_) to write
them.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the entries to copy. Their leading
dimensions are those of `td[idx]`.
- **idx** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,*[*slice*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#slice)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) - the index to write at,
along the batch dimensions.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.

Keyword Arguments:

**fast** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - 

if `True`, uses only the tensor-only copy,
and raises a `RuntimeError` if the source, the destination or
the index does not allow it (for example a dictionary source, a
tensordict that is not a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), a
tensor index, a value that needs broadcasting, or a key missing
from the tensordict). If `False`, calls
[`update_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_). Defaults to `True`.

Changed in version 0.15: `fast=None`, deprecated in 0.14, is no longer accepted.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3, 2), batch_size=[3])
>>> _ = td.copy_at_(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(2), batch_size=[]), 1)
>>> td["x"][:, 0]
tensor([0., 1., 0.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.cosh

# TensorDictBase.cpu

TensorDictBase.cpu(***kwargs*) → Self

Returns the tensordict on the CPU, as `to("cpu", **kwargs)` does.

A tensordict whose device is already the CPU is returned as it is.

Parameters:

****kwargs** - passed to [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to), for example `non_blocking`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> td.cpu().device
device(type='cpu')
```

# TensorDictBase.create_nested

TensorDictBase.create_nested(*key*)

Adds an empty nested tensordict at `key`, and returns `self`.

The new tensordict has the batch size, device and names of the
tensordict it is added to. An existing entry at `key` is replaced.
For a tuple key, a plain [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) keeps a
plain, unlocked `TensorDict` already on the path with its entries:
`("a", "b")` adds `"b"` to an existing `td["a"]`. A lazy stack of
plain `TensorDict` instances does this in each member, and a
tensorclass or a `TensorDictParams` follows the
rule of the tensordict it wraps. Any other entry on the path, such as a
tensor, a lazy stack, a tensorclass, a typed tensordict or a locked
tensordict, is replaced by a new empty tensordict, and so is every
level of the path when the tensordict is of any other type, such as a
view, a typed tensordict or a file.

Parameters:

**key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key of the new tensordict.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the tensordict is locked.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict({}, [3, 4, 5])
>>> _ = data.create_nested(("some", "nested", "value"))
>>> data["some", "nested", "value"].batch_size
torch.Size([3, 4, 5])
>>> list(data.keys(include_nested=True))
[('some', 'nested', 'value'), ('some', 'nested'), 'some']
>>> _ = data.create_nested(("some", "other"))
>>> list(data.keys(include_nested=True))
[('some', 'nested', 'value'), ('some', 'nested'), ('some', 'other'), 'some']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.cuda

TensorDictBase.cuda(*device: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Returns the tensordict on a CUDA device, as [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) does.

A tensordict that is already on that device is returned as it is.

Parameters:

- **device** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - the CUDA device. An
integer (or a string of digits) is a device index. Defaults to
`None`, which uses the current CUDA device.
- ****kwargs** - passed to [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to), for example `non_blocking`.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `device` is not a CUDA device.

Examples

The example needs a CUDA device, so it is not run when the
documentation is tested.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> td.cuda().device 
device(type='cuda', index=0)
>>> td.cuda(1).device 
device(type='cuda', index=1)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.cummax

TensorDictBase.cummax(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, ***, *reduce: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *return_indices: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → Self | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the cumulative maximum of every leaf along a batch dimension.

As with [`torch.cummax()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cummax.html#torch.cummax), the result is a named tuple of two
tensordicts, `values` and `indices`, with the structure and the batch
size of the tensordict.

Parameters:

**dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch dimension along which to compute it. A negative
`dim` counts from the end of the batch dimensions. A tuple uses
only its first dimension; passing one is deprecated and will be
removed in TensorDict 0.17.

Keyword Arguments:

- **reduce** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, concatenates the leaves along
`dim`, which requires them to have the same number of dimensions,
and returns what [`torch.cummax()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cummax.html#torch.cummax) returns for the result. With
feature dimensions, a negative `dim` counts from the end of each
leaf. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
counting it from the end of the batch dimensions, as with
`reduce=False`. Defaults to `False`.
- **return_indices** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, returns only the values
tensordict. Defaults to `True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([1.0, 3.0, 2.0]), batch_size=[3])
>>> td.cummax(dim=0).values["a"]
tensor([1., 3., 3.])
>>> td.cummax(dim=0).indices["a"]
tensor([0, 1, 1])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.cummin

Returns the cumulative minimum of every leaf along a batch dimension.

`dim` counts from the end of the batch dimensions. A tuple uses
only its first dimension; passing one is deprecated and will be
removed in TensorDict 0.17.

Keyword Arguments:

- **reduce** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, concatenates the leaves along

and returns what [`torch.cummin()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cummin.html#torch.cummin) returns for the result. With
feature dimensions, a negative `dim` counts from the end of each

- **return_indices** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, returns only the values

# TensorDictBase.data

*property*TensorDictBase.data*: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*

the same storage, without autograd.

The leaves of the result share storage with the leaves of the
tensordict, and do not require gradients. An in-place change to the
result changes the tensordict.

Assigning `td.data = other` rebinds the `.data` of each leaf of
the tensordict to the matching leaf of `other`, as `torch.Tensor.data`
does. The leaves then share storage with `other`: memory-mapped or
shared-memory leaves stop writing to their file or shared memory.
`other` and each of its nested tensordicts must have the batch size
of the matching tensordict, and each key of `other` must be in the
tensordict.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3, requires_grad=True), batch_size=[3])
>>> data = td.data
>>> data["x"].requires_grad, data["x"].data_ptr() == td["x"].data_ptr()
(False, True)
```

Type:

A tensordict of the `.data` of every leaf

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.data_ptr

TensorDictBase.data_ptr(***, *storage: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns the data pointers of the leaves, as a tensordict of integers.

The result has the keys of the tensordict, an empty batch size and the
CPU device. Each leaf is replaced by its
[`data_ptr()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.data_ptr.html#torch.Tensor.data_ptr), as a 0-d `int64` tensor. Compare two
results to check whether two tensordicts share memory. In a lazy stack,
each member is a nested entry named by its index (`"0"`, `"1"`,
...), which gives the data pointers of the leaves it really holds.

Keyword Arguments:

**storage** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, returns the data pointer of
the storage of each leaf
(`tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr()`) instead, which a view
shares with its base. Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2), b=torch.zeros(2), batch_size=[2])
>>> td0 = td.unsqueeze(0) # the leaves of td0 are views on the leaves of td
>>> assert (td0.data_ptr() == td.data_ptr()).all()
>>> td1 = td[1:] # views with an offset
>>> (td1.data_ptr() == td.data_ptr()).all()
False
>>> (td1.data_ptr(storage=True) == td.data_ptr(storage=True)).all()
True
>>> stack = TensorDict.lazy_stack([td, td])
>>> list(stack.data_ptr().keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True))
[('0', 'a'), ('0', 'b'), ('1', 'a'), ('1', 'b')]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.del

TensorDictBase.del_(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*) → Self

Deletes an entry of the tensordict in place and returns the tensordict.

A locked tensordict raises `RuntimeError` (see [`lock_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_)).
`del td[key]` does the same.

Parameters:

**key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key to delete. A missing key raises
`KeyError`, and a key whose path runs through an entry that
is not a tensordict raises `ValueError`. Until TensorDict
0.17, the stores and the zarr backend of
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) warn and do nothing
for a missing key.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b=TensorDict(c=torch.ones(3)))
>>> list(td.del_(("b", "c")).keys(True))
['a', 'b']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.densify

TensorDictBase.densify(*layout: [layout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout) = torch.strided*)

Returns the tensordict with its lazy stacks replaced by dense tensordicts.

The entries of a lazy stack are stacked into one tensor when their
shapes match, and into a nested tensor ([`torch.nested`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/nested.html#module-torch.nested)) along the
stack dimension otherwise. A tensordict that holds no lazy stack is
returned as it is.

Parameters:

**layout** ([*layout*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout)*,**optional*) - the layout of the nested tensors,
`torch.strided` or `torch.jagged`. Defaults to
`torch.strided`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> stack = TensorDict.lazy_stack(
... [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.ones(4))]
... )
>>> dense = stack.densify(layout=torch.jagged)
>>> type(dense).__name__, dense["a"].is_nested
('TensorDict', True)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

*property*TensorDictBase.depth*: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*

the maximum number of levels of nested tensordicts.

A tensordict with no nested tensordict has depth 0. Empty nested
tensordicts do not count.

>>> TensorDict({"a": {"b": {"c": 0}}}).depth

# TensorDictBase.detach

TensorDictBase.detach() → Self

Returns a new tensordict with every tensor leaf detached from the autograd graph.

The leaves are [`torch.Tensor.detach()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.detach.html#torch.Tensor.detach) views: they share their
storage with the leaves of the tensordict, and do not require
gradients. A locked tensordict gives a locked result.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, requires_grad=True) + 1)
>>> out = td.detach()
>>> out["a"].requires_grad, td["a"].requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> out["a"].data_ptr() == td["a"].data_ptr()
True
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.detach

TensorDictBase.detach_() → Self

Detaches every tensor leaf from the autograd graph in place, and returns the tensordict.

Each leaf is detached with [`torch.Tensor.detach_()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.detach_.html#torch.Tensor.detach_): it keeps its
storage and no longer requires gradients.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, requires_grad=True) + 1)
>>> a = td["a"]
>>> _ = td.detach_()
>>> a.requires_grad, td["a"] is a
(False, True)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.device

*property*TensorDictBase.device*: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*

The device of the tensordict, or `None` if it has none.

If the tensordict has a device, all its leaves, nested ones included,
are on that device: the tensors that you pass to the constructor or
set later are moved to it. If the device is `None`, the leaves can be
on different devices. The device is not inferred from the tensors.
Assigning it raises a `RuntimeError`: use [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) to get a
tensordict on another device. See [Devices, dtypes, and memory](../../concepts/devices.html#devices).

Examples

The examples use the `"meta"` device so that they run on CPU.
A CUDA device works the same way.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({
... "cpu": torch.randn(3, device='cpu'),
... "meta": torch.randn(3, device='meta'),
... }, batch_size=[], device=None)
>>> td['cpu'].device
device(type='cpu')
>>> td['meta'].device
device(type='meta')
>>> print(td.device)
None
>>> td = TensorDict({
... "x": torch.randn(3, device='cpu'),
... "y": TensorDict({'z': torch.randn(3, device='cpu')}, batch_size=[], device=None),
... }, batch_size=[], device='meta')
>>> td['x'].device
device(type='meta')
>>> td['y'].device # nested tensordicts are also mapped onto the appropriate device.
device(type='meta')
>>> td['y', 'z'].device
device(type='meta')
>>> td['w'] = torch.zeros(3) # a new entry is moved to the device too
>>> td['w'].device
device(type='meta')
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.div

TensorDictBase.div(*other: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, ***, *default: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with every leaf divided by `other`.

`td / other` calls this method. Integer leaves are promoted to the
default floating-point dtype, as with [`torch.div()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.div.html#torch.div).

\[\text{out}_i = \frac{\text{input}_i}{\text{other}_i}\]

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the divisor. A
tensordict is paired with the tensordict key by key. A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf and expanded over
its feature dimensions. Batch sizes that differ are broadcast
together.

Keyword Arguments:

**default** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - what to do with the keys
that only one of the two tensordicts has. `None` requires the
same keys and raises a `KeyError` otherwise.
`"intersection"` computes the keys that both have and drops
the others. A tensor stands in for the missing entry on either
side, and the result has the keys of both. Defaults to `None`.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.div

TensorDictBase.div_(*other: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*) → Self

Divides every leaf by `other` in place and returns `self`.

The in-place version of [`div()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.div.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.div), called by `td /= other`. It
has no `default`: a tensordict `other` must have every key of the
tensordict, and its other keys are ignored.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the divisor,
paired with the leaves as in [`div()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.div.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.div).

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).
