# TensorDictBase.named_apply

TensorDictBase.named_apply(*fn: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)*, **others: T*, *nested_keys: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = NO_DEFAULT*, *names: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = NO_DEFAULT*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *default: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = NO_DEFAULT*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *propagate_lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *call_on_nested: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *is_leaf: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)], [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***constructor_kwargs*) → Self | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Applies a callable to every leaf and its key, and returns a new tensordict with the results.

Same as [`apply()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply), except that `fn` also receives the key of
each leaf: the last string of its nested key, or the whole nested key
with `nested_keys=True`. If `fn` returns `None`, the entry is left
out of the result, which can be used to filter entries by key.

Parameters:

- **fn** (*Callable*) - the function called on each leaf, as
`fn(key, leaf, *other_leaves)`. It returns a tensor, a
tensordict, or `None` to leave the entry out.
- ***others** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - other tensordicts with the same structure
as the tensordict. An entry that one of them lacks raises
`KeyError`, unless `default` is given.

Keyword Arguments:

- **nested_keys** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `fn` receives the whole
nested key of each leaf, a tuple of strings for an entry of a
nested tensordict. If `False`, it receives the last string of
the key. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result, for a `fn` that changes the shape of the leaves:
the results must have it as their leading dimensions. `fn` is
then not called on [`UnbatchedTensor`](tensordict.UnbatchedTensor.html#tensordict.UnbatchedTensor) entries,
which keep their data and take the new batch size. Defaults to
`None`, which keeps the batch size of the tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. The results of `fn` are moved to it. `None` gives a
result with no device, which leaves each result where `fn`
put it. By default, the result has the device of the
tensordict.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the batch dimensions of
the result, one per dimension. By default, the names of the
tensordict are kept, or dropped if `batch_size` is given.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the results are written into
the existing leaves of the tensordict (as [`set_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_) does),
and `self` is returned. See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).
Defaults to `False`.
- **default** (*Any**,**optional*) - the value passed to `fn` for an entry
that one of `others` lacks. By default, a missing entry raises
`KeyError`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a nested tensordict
with no entry in the result (because `fn` returned `None`
for all its leaves, or because it was already empty) is left
out. If `False`, it is kept, empty. Defaults to `None`,
which leaves out the nested tensordicts that `fn` emptied and
keeps those that were already empty. Non-tensor data that
`fn` is not called on is kept in all cases.
- **propagate_lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the result of a locked
tensordict is locked too. Defaults to `False`.
- **call_on_nested** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `fn` is called on the
top-level entries, nested tensordicts and tensorclasses
included, and is responsible for going into them. If `False`,
`fn` is called on the leaves only. Defaults to `False`.
- **is_leaf** (*Callable**,**optional*) - called with the type of each entry:
`fn` is called on the entries for which it returns `True`,
and `named_apply` goes into the others. Defaults to `None`, which
uses [`default_is_leaf()`](tensordict.default_is_leaf.html#tensordict.default_is_leaf): `fn` is called on
tensors, and non-tensor data is kept unchanged. Pass
[`is_leaf_nontensor()`](tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor.html#tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor) to call `fn` on
non-tensor data too.
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the results
into, instead of a new one. When `batch_size` or `device` is
given, `out` must have it. For a lazy stack, `out` must be a
lazy stack too, stacked along any dimension. See the warning
below about `out=self`. Defaults to `None`.
- ****constructor_kwargs** - accepted and ignored.

Returns:

A new tensordict, `out` if it is given, or `self` if
`inplace=True`. `None` if `fn` returns `None` for every
leaf and `filter_empty` is not `False`. With
`filter_empty=None`, a tensordict that is already empty gives an
empty tensordict.

The result has the type of the tensordict for a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), a lazy stack and a tensorclass.
Other types, for example [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict)
or a memory-mapped tensordict, give a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)
that lives in memory. A locked tensordict gives an unlocked result
unless `propagate_lock=True`.

Warning

With `out=self`, the results are silently wrong if
`fn` reads other entries of the tensordict, which may already be
overwritten.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... a=torch.zeros(3),
... nested=TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3), b=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3]),
... batch_size=[3],
... )
>>> out = td.named_apply(lambda key, x: x if key == "a" else None)
>>> list(out.keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True))
['a', ('nested', 'a')]
>>> out = td.named_apply(
... lambda key, x: x + 1 if key == ("nested", "b") else x,
... nested_keys=True,
... )
>>> out["nested", "b"], out["nested", "a"]
(tensor([2., 2., 2.]), tensor([1., 1., 1.]))
```

With another tensordict, `fn` receives one leaf of each:

```
>>> td.named_apply(lambda key, x, y: x + y, td)["nested", "a"]
tensor([2., 2., 2.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.names

*property*TensorDictBase.names

The dimension names of the tensordict, one per batch dimension.

A dimension without a name is `None`. The names can be set at
construction time using the `names` argument, or by assignment
(`td.names = [...]`). The names must be unique. Shape operations and
indexing keep the names of the dimensions that remain. Assigning
`None` removes the names. See [Batch size, shapes, and indexing](../../concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size).

See also

[`refine_names()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names) and [`rename_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename_).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, 4), batch_size=[3, 4], names=["time", None])
>>> td.names
['time', None]
>>> td.names = ["time", "batch"]
>>> td[0].names
['batch']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.nanmean

TensorDictBase.nanmean(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['feature'] = NO_DEFAULT*, *keepdim: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = NO_DEFAULT*, ***, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *reduce: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the mean of the non-NaN elements of every leaf.

Works as [`mean()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.mean.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.mean), but ignores NaN values.

Parameters:

- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,*[*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the batch dimensions to
reduce. A negative `dim` counts from the end of the batch
dimensions. `"feature"` reduces the feature dimensions of each
leaf instead, and the result keeps the batch size. Defaults to
`None`, which reduces every element of each leaf, and the result
has an empty batch size.
- **keepdim** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the reduced batch dimensions are
kept with size 1. Not allowed with `dim="feature"`. Defaults to
`False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - if given, each leaf is cast to this dtype
before the reduction, which helps to prevent overflows. Defaults to
`None`.
- **reduce** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reduces all the leaves together
and returns a single tensor. Without `dim`, the result is a
scalar. With an int `dim`, the leaves are concatenated along
`dim` first, so they must have the same number of dimensions. With
`dim="feature"`, the result has the batch size as its shape. With
feature dimensions, a negative `dim` counts from the end of each
leaf. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
counting it from the end of the batch dimensions, as with
`reduce=False`. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A new tensordict, or a tensor if `reduce=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([[1.0, float("nan")], [3.0, 4.0]]), batch_size=[2])
>>> td.nanmean()["a"]
tensor(2.6667)
>>> td.mean()["a"]
tensor(nan)
>>> td.nanmean(dim=0)["a"]
tensor([2., 4.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.nansum

TensorDictBase.nansum(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['feature'] = NO_DEFAULT*, *keepdim: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = NO_DEFAULT*, ***, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *reduce: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the sum of the non-NaN elements of every leaf.

Works as [`sum()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.sum.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.sum), but counts NaN values as zero.

Parameters:

- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,*[*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the batch dimensions to
reduce. A negative `dim` counts from the end of the batch
dimensions. `"feature"` reduces the feature dimensions of each
leaf instead, and the result keeps the batch size. Defaults to
`None`, which reduces every element of each leaf, and the result
has an empty batch size.
- **keepdim** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the reduced batch dimensions are
kept with size 1. Not allowed with `dim="feature"`. Defaults to
`False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - if given, each leaf is cast to this dtype
before the reduction, which helps to prevent overflows. Defaults to
`None`.
- **reduce** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reduces all the leaves together
and returns a single tensor. Without `dim`, the result is a
scalar. With an int `dim`, the leaves are concatenated along
`dim` first, so they must have the same number of dimensions. With
`dim="feature"`, the result has the batch size as its shape. With
feature dimensions, a negative `dim` counts from the end of each
leaf. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
counting it from the end of the batch dimensions, as with
`reduce=False`. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A new tensordict, or a tensor if `reduce=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([[1.0, float("nan")], [3.0, 4.0]]), batch_size=[2])
>>> td.nansum()["a"]
tensor(8.)
>>> td.sum()["a"]
tensor(nan)
>>> td.nansum(dim=0)["a"]
tensor([4., 4.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.narrow

TensorDictBase.narrow(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *start: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *length: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*)

Returns a tensordict narrowed along a batch dimension, as [`torch.Tensor.narrow()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.narrow.html#torch.Tensor.narrow) does.

The result keeps the elements `start` to `start + length - 1` of
`dim`. Its leaves are views of the original leaves, and it keeps the
names.

Parameters:

- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch dimension to narrow.
- **start** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the first element to keep.
- **length** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the number of elements to keep.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.arange(6).view(2, 3)}, batch_size=[2, 3])
>>> print(td["a"])
tensor([[0, 1, 2],
 [3, 4, 5]])
>>> print(td.narrow(1, 1, 2)["a"])
tensor([[1, 2],
 [4, 5]])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.new_empty

TensorDictBase.new_empty(**size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = NO_DEFAULT*, *requires_grad: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *layout: [layout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout) = torch.strided*, *pin_memory: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *empty_lazy: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns a tensordict of batch size `size` with uninitialized leaves.

The values of the leaves are not set, as with [`torch.empty()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.empty.html#torch.empty).

Each leaf keeps its feature dimensions: a leaf of shape
`(*self.batch_size, *f)` becomes `(*size, *f)`. By default, each
leaf keeps its dtype and device.

Parameters:

***size** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or**sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch size of the result, as
integers or as one list, tuple or `torch.Size`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of every leaf of the
result. Defaults to `None`: each leaf keeps its dtype.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result and of its leaves. If not passed, each leaf keeps its
device, and the result keeps the device of the tensordict.
- **requires_grad** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, autograd records the
operations on the new leaves. Defaults to `False`.
- **layout** ([*layout*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout)*,**optional*) - the layout of the new leaves.
Defaults to `torch.strided`.
- **pin_memory** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the new leaves are
allocated in pinned memory. Works only for CPU tensors.
Defaults to `False`.
- **empty_lazy** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the lazy stacks of the
result are emptied of their content. Use it when the content
of a lazy stack is likely to change while you fill the new
tensordict. It applies to the sub-tensordicts too. Defaults to
`False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, 4), b=torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64), batch_size=[3])
>>> out = td.new_empty(5)
>>> out.batch_size, out["a"].shape
(torch.Size([5]), torch.Size([5, 4]))
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.new_full

TensorDictBase.new_full(*size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*, *fill_value*, ***, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = NO_DEFAULT*, *requires_grad: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *layout: [layout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout) = torch.strided*, *pin_memory: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *empty_lazy: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns a tensordict of batch size `size` with every leaf filled with `fill_value`.

Each leaf keeps its feature dimensions: a leaf of shape

- **size** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or**sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch size of the result, as an
int, or as a list, tuple or `torch.Size`.
- **fill_value** (*scalar*) - the value of every element of the result.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of every leaf of the
result. Defaults to `None`: each leaf keeps its dtype.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result and of its leaves. If not passed, each leaf keeps its
device, and the result keeps the device of the tensordict.
- **requires_grad** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, autograd records the
operations on the new leaves. Defaults to `False`.
- **layout** ([*layout*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout)*,**optional*) - the layout of the new leaves.
Defaults to `torch.strided`.
- **pin_memory** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the new leaves are
allocated in pinned memory. Works only for CPU tensors.
Defaults to `False`.
- **empty_lazy** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the lazy stacks of the
result are emptied of their content. Use it when the content
of a lazy stack is likely to change while you fill the new
tensordict. It applies to the sub-tensordicts too. Defaults to
`False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, 4), b=torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64), batch_size=[3])
```

# TensorDictBase.new_tensor

TensorDictBase.new_tensor(*data: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [ndarray](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray) | [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence) | [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, ***, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = NO_DEFAULT*, *requires_grad: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *pin_memory: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a tensordict whose leaves are copies of `data`, each with the dtype of its leaf.

Each leaf of the tensordict gives a leaf of the result, built as
`leaf.new_tensor(data)`: the batch size of the result and the shape
of every leaf are the shape of `data`. If `data` is a tensordict or
a tensorclass, each leaf is built from the matching leaf of `data`.

Parameters:

**data** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**array_like*) - the data to
copy. As for [`torch.Tensor.new_tensor()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.new_tensor.html#torch.Tensor.new_tensor), it can also be a
list, a tuple, a NumPy array or a scalar.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of every leaf of the
result. Defaults to `None`: each leaf keeps the dtype of the
matching leaf of the tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result and of its leaves. If not passed, the device of
`data`: the default device for a list, a tuple, a NumPy array
or a scalar.
- **requires_grad** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, autograd records the
operations on the new leaves. Defaults to `False`.
- **pin_memory** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the new leaves are
allocated in pinned memory. Works only for CPU tensors.
Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... a=torch.zeros(3), b=torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64), batch_size=[3]
... )
>>> out = td.new_tensor([1, 2])
>>> out.batch_size
torch.Size([2])
>>> out["a"], out["b"]
(tensor([1., 2.]), tensor([1, 2]))
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.non_tensor_items

TensorDictBase.non_tensor_items(*include_nested: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns a tuple of the `(key, value)` pairs of the non-tensor data of the tensordict.

The values are [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) (or
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack)) instances. See
[Non-tensor data and unbatched entries](../../concepts/non_tensor.html#non-tensor-data).

Parameters:

**include_nested** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the non-tensor data of
the nested tensordicts is also returned, under nested keys.
Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2), s="text", nested=TensorDict(t="more"))
>>> [key for key, _ in td.non_tensor_items(include_nested=True)]
['s', ('nested', 't')]
>>> td.non_tensor_items()[0][1].data
'text'
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.norm

TensorDictBase.norm(***, *out=None*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *key_transform: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)], [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a tensordict with the norm of each leaf.

Each tensor leaf is replaced by its 2-norm, computed over all its
elements, so the result has an empty batch size. Non-tensor data is
kept as it is.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the norms
into, with the keys of the tensordict and an empty batch size.
Defaults to `None`.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of the norms. Defaults to
`None`, which keeps the dtype of each leaf.
- **key_transform** (*Callable**,**optional*) - a function that renames the
keys of the result. It is called on each string key, level by
level: `("a", "b")` becomes
`(key_transform("a"), key_transform("b"))`. Defaults to
`None`, which keeps the keys.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.full((3, 4), 2.0), b=TensorDict(c=torch.ones(3)), batch_size=[3])
>>> norms = td.norm()
>>> norms["a"], norms["b", "c"], norms.batch_size
(tensor(6.9282), tensor(1.7321), torch.Size([]))
>>> list(td.norm(key_transform=lambda key: f"{key}_norm").keys(True, True))
['a_norm', ('b_norm', 'c_norm')]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.numel

TensorDictBase.numel() → [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

Returns the number of elements in the batch, which is the product of `batch_size`.

The feature dimensions of the leaves do not count. The minimum is 1: a
tensordict with batch size `[]` or `[0]` returns 1, unlike
[`torch.Tensor.numel()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.numel.html#torch.Tensor.numel), which returns 0 for a size of 0.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2, 3, 10), batch_size=[2, 3]).numel()
6
>>> TensorDict(batch_size=[]).numel()
1
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.numpy

TensorDictBase.numpy() → [ndarray](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray) | [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

Returns a nested dict of NumPy arrays with the entries of the tensordict.

Each tensor becomes a NumPy array with [`torch.Tensor.numpy()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.numpy.html#torch.Tensor.numpy),
so the arrays share memory with the tensors, and a tensor that
requires gradients or is not on the CPU raises a `RuntimeError` or
`TypeError`: call [`detach()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.detach.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.detach) or [`cpu()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.cpu.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.cpu) first. A nested
tensor becomes a tuple of arrays. Non-tensor data is returned as its
Python value. The `None` fields of tensorclasses are dropped.

See also

[`to_struct_array()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_struct_array.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_struct_array) to convert to a NumPy
structured array, and [`to_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict({"a": {"b": torch.zeros(()), "c": "a string!"}})
>>> data.numpy()
{'a': {'b': array(0., dtype=float32), 'c': 'a string!'}}
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.pack

TensorDictBase.pack(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = -1*, ***, *layout: [PackLayout](tensordict.PackLayout.html#tensordict.PackLayout) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor), [PackLayout](tensordict.PackLayout.html#tensordict.PackLayout)]

Packs all the leaves of a tensordict into one tensor of features.

Each leaf is flattened after the batch dimensions, and the leaves are
concatenated in the order of `keys(True, True, sort=True)`, so the
columns depend on the set of keys only. Leaves can have different
ranks. The result has shape `(*batch_size, F)` for `dim=-1`, where
`F` is the sum of the numbers of features of the leaves, and it is
contiguous for any `dim`. [`PackLayout.unpack`](tensordict.PackLayout.html#tensordict.PackLayout.unpack) inverts it.

Packing along the last dim copies the data once, with one
[`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat). Along another dim the result can take a second
copy: [`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat) keeps the channels-last strides that moving
the feature dim gives a 4-d or 5-d result, and the result is then made
contiguous.

All the leaves must share one dtype and one device. Non-tensor data
cannot be packed: drop it with [`filter_non_tensor_data()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.filter_non_tensor_data.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.filter_non_tensor_data) first.
A lazy stack packs like its dense equivalent if all its members have
the same keys and feature shapes.

Parameters:

**dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the position of the packed dimension in the
result, in `[-(batch_dims + 1), batch_dims]` as for
[`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack). Defaults to `-1`.

Keyword Arguments:

**layout** ([*PackLayout*](tensordict.PackLayout.html#tensordict.PackLayout)*,**optional*) - a layout to pack into. The columns
then follow its key order, and a missing, extra or reshaped
leaf raises. `dim` must match the layout's dim. Defaults to
`None`, which builds a new layout in sorted key order.

Returns:

A tuple of the packed tensor and its
[`PackLayout`](tensordict.PackLayout.html#tensordict.PackLayout).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... p=torch.zeros(5),
... v=torch.ones(5, 3),
... nested={"stress": torch.ones(5, 3, 3)},
... batch_size=[5],
... )
>>> flat, layout = td.pack()
>>> flat.shape
torch.Size([5, 13])
>>> layout.keys
(('nested', 'stress'), 'p', 'v')
>>> out = layout.unpack(flat.index_select(0, torch.tensor([0, 2])))
>>> out.batch_size
torch.Size([2])
>>> flat2, _ = td.pack(layout=layout)
>>> assert (flat2 == flat).all()
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.pad

TensorDictBase.pad(*pad_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]*, *value: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) = 0.0*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → Self

Returns the tensordict padded along its batch dimensions with a constant value.

Parameters:

- **pad_size** (*sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the padding, applied to the batch
dimensions starting from the first. For a tensordict with
`ndim` batch dimensions, it is a sequence of even length up
to `2 * ndim`:
`(dim0_left, dim0_right, dim1_left, dim1_right, ...)`.
- **value** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*,**optional*) - the fill value. Defaults to `0.0`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - 

if `True`, the tensordict keeps its
identity and keys, its leaves are replaced one by one by
their padded copies, and the call returns `self`. Peak memory
stays close to `1x` instead of `2x`. See
[In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions). Defaults to `False`.

Warning

If `inplace=True` and the padding of a later leaf fails
(for example, out of memory), the tensordict is left in an
inconsistent state. `safe=True` catches the user errors
before any leaf is changed.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, checks that the padding works
for every leaf before any leaf is changed. Pass `False` to
skip this check when the inputs are known to be valid.
Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

The padded tensordict, or `self` with `inplace=True`.

Note

On a lazy stack whose tensordicts have no names, the result of
`inplace=False` has no names, even when the stack dimension has
a name. See [`pad()`](tensordict.pad.html#tensordict.pad).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3, 4)}, batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> td.pad([0, 0, 0, 1]).batch_size
torch.Size([3, 5])
>>> td.pad([0, 0, 0, 1], inplace=True) is td
True
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([3, 5])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.param_count

TensorDictBase.param_count(***, *count_duplicates: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

Returns the total number of elements of the tensor leaves.

It sums [`numel()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.numel.html#torch.Tensor.numel) over the tensor leaves, nested
tensordicts included. Non-tensor data is not counted.

Keyword Arguments:

**count_duplicates** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a tensor stored
under several keys is counted once per key. If `False`, it
is counted once. Two different views of one tensor are counted
twice in both cases. Defaults to `True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> x = torch.zeros(6)
>>> td = TensorDict(a=x, b=x, c=torch.zeros(2, 3), s="text")
>>> td.param_count()
18
>>> td.param_count(count_duplicates=False)
12
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.permute

TensorDictBase.permute(**args*, ***kwargs*)

Returns a tensordict with its batch dimensions permuted, as [`torch.Tensor.permute()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.permute.html#torch.Tensor.permute) does.

The leaves keep their feature dimensions after the batch dimensions,
and are views of the original leaves. The names are permuted with the
dimensions.

It can be used as a context manager, as [`unsqueeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze) can: when
the `with` block exits, the entries of the block are written back to
the tensordict with the inverse operation.

Parameters:

***dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the new order of the batch dimensions, as integers,
as one list or tuple, or as the keyword argument `dims`.

Returns:

A tensordict with the batch dimensions in the new order.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3, 4, 5)}, [3, 4])
>>> td.permute(1, 0)["a"].shape
torch.Size([4, 3, 5])
>>> td.permute([1, 0]).batch_size
torch.Size([4, 3])
>>> td.permute(dims=[1, 0]).batch_size
torch.Size([4, 3])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.pin_memory

TensorDictBase.pin_memory(*num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Returns a tensordict whose tensor leaves are in pinned (page-locked) memory.

Calls [`pin_memory()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.pin_memory.html#torch.Tensor.pin_memory) on every tensor leaf. Copies
from pinned memory to an accelerator are faster, and can run
asynchronously with `to(device, non_blocking=True)`. Pinning needs an
accelerator, such as CUDA. A [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict)
or a [`TensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore) raises a
`RuntimeError`: call [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict) first. See
[Devices, dtypes, and memory](../../concepts/devices.html#devices).

Parameters:

- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that pin the
leaves, in a [`ThreadPoolExecutor`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/concurrent.futures.html#concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor).
Defaults to `None`, which, like `0`, pins them on the
calling thread.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict and its
nested tensordicts keep their identity, each leaf is replaced
by its pinned copy, and the call returns `self`. A locked
tensordict, one that holds a node other than a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), a lazy stack or a tensorclass,
or one with memory-mapped, shared, sparse, jagged or unbatched
leaves gets the pinned copies written back into its existing
leaves, which stay in pageable memory. Defaults to `False`.

Examples

The example needs an accelerator, so it is not run when the
documentation is tested.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(obs=torch.zeros(1000, 3), batch_size=[1000])
>>> pinned = td.pin_memory() 
>>> pinned["obs"].is_pinned() 
True
>>> td_cuda = pinned.to("cuda", non_blocking=True)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.pin_memory

TensorDictBase.pin_memory_(*num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*) → Self

Pins the tensor leaves of the tensordict and returns `self`.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Use `pin_memory(inplace=True)` instead. Pinning allocates new
storage, so it does not fit the trailing-underscore convention

in TensorDict 0.17.

Parameters:

**num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that pin the
leaves, as in [`pin_memory()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.pin_memory.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.pin_memory). Defaults to `0`, which
pins them on the calling thread.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.pop

TensorDictBase.pop(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *default: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = NO_DEFAULT*) → [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Removes an entry from the tensordict and returns its value.

A nested key removes one entry of a nested tensordict and keeps the
nested tensordict. A locked tensordict raises `RuntimeError` when
the key is present (see [`lock_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_)).

Parameters:

- **key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key of the entry to remove.
- **default** (*Any**,**optional*) - the value returned when the key is
missing, including a nested key that runs through a tensor.
Without it, a missing key raises `KeyError` and a nested key
that runs through a tensor raises `ValueError`.

Returns:

The value of the removed entry, or `default`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b=TensorDict(c=torch.ones(3)))
>>> td.pop(("b", "c"))
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
>>> sorted(td.keys(include_nested=True))
['a', 'b']
>>> td.pop("missing", None) is None
True
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.popitem

TensorDictBase.popitem() → [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)]

Removes the last top-level entry and returns it as a `(key, value)` pair.

The last entry is the last key of [`keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys), which is the last
one inserted for a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). A nested
tensordict is returned whole.

Raises:

- [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if the tensordict is empty.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the tensordict is locked.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> td.popitem()
('b', tensor([1., 1., 1.]))
>>> list(td.keys())
['a']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.pow

TensorDictBase.pow(*other: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, ***, *default: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a new tensordict with every leaf raised to the power `other`.

`td ** other` calls this method. `other ** td` with a number
`other` raises a `NotImplementedError`.

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or**Number*) - the exponent. A
tensordict is paired with the tensordict key by key. A tensor is
aligned with the batch dimensions of each leaf and expanded over
its feature dimensions. Batch sizes that differ are broadcast
together.

Keyword Arguments:

**default** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - what to do with the keys
that only one of the two tensordicts has. `None` requires the
same keys and raises a `KeyError` otherwise.
`"intersection"` computes the keys that both have and drops
the others. A tensor stands in for the missing entry on either
side, and the result has the keys of both. Defaults to `None`.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

Raises every leaf to the power `other` in place and returns `self`.

The in-place version of [`pow()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.pow.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.pow), called by `td **= other`. It

# TensorDictBase.prod

TensorDictBase.prod(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['feature'] = NO_DEFAULT*, *keepdim: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = NO_DEFAULT*, ***, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *reduce: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the product of every leaf, over all its elements or along a batch dimension.

Parameters:

- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the batch dimension to reduce. A negative
`dim` counts from the end of the batch dimensions. `"feature"`
reduces the feature dimensions of each leaf instead, and the result
keeps the batch size. A tuple reduces only its first dimension;
passing one is deprecated and will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.
Defaults to `None`, which reduces every element of each leaf, and
the result has an empty batch size.
- **keepdim** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the reduced batch dimensions are
kept with size 1. Not allowed with `dim="feature"`. Defaults to
`False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - if given, each leaf is cast to this dtype
before the reduction, which helps to prevent overflows. Defaults to
`None`.
- **reduce** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reduces all the leaves together
and returns a single tensor. Without `dim`, the result is a
scalar. With an int `dim`, the leaves are concatenated along
`dim` first, so they must have the same number of dimensions. With
`dim="feature"`, the result has the batch size as its shape. With
feature dimensions, a negative `dim` counts from the end of each
leaf. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
counting it from the end of the batch dimensions, as with
`reduce=False`. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A new tensordict, or a tensor if `reduce=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]), batch_size=[2])
>>> td.prod()["a"]
tensor(24.)
>>> td.prod(dim=0)["a"]
tensor([3., 8.])
>>> td.prod(dim="feature")["a"]
tensor([ 2., 12.])
>>> td.prod(reduce=True)
tensor(24.)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.quantile

TensorDictBase.quantile(*q: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['feature'] = NO_DEFAULT*, *keepdim: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = NO_DEFAULT*, ***, *interpolation: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'linear'*, *reduce: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *key_transform: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)], [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the `q`-th quantile of every leaf, over all its elements or along a batch dimension.

Parameters:

- **q** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the quantile, between 0 and 1. With a
1-dimensional tensor of `n` quantiles, every leaf of the result
gets a leading dimension of size `n`, and so does the batch size
when `dim` is given.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the batch dimension to reduce. A negative
`dim` counts from the end of the batch dimensions. `"feature"`
reduces the feature dimensions of each leaf instead, and the result
keeps the batch size. A tuple reduces only its first dimension;
passing one is deprecated and will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.
Defaults to `None`, which reduces every element of each leaf, and
the result has an empty batch size.
- **keepdim** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the reduced batch dimensions are
kept with size 1. Not allowed with `dim="feature"`. Defaults to
`False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **interpolation** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the method used when the quantile lies
between two data points: `"linear"`, `"lower"`, `"higher"`,
`"midpoint"` or `"nearest"`. Defaults to `"linear"`.
- **reduce** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reduces all the leaves together
and returns a single tensor. Without `dim`, the result is a
scalar. With an int `dim`, the leaves are concatenated along
`dim` first, so they must have the same number of dimensions. With
`dim="feature"`, the result has the batch size as its shape. With
feature dimensions, a negative `dim` counts from the end of each
leaf. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
counting it from the end of the batch dimensions, as with
`reduce=False`. Defaults to `False`.
- **key_transform** (*Callable**,**optional*) - a function applied to the name of
every entry of the result, at every level of nesting, such as
`lambda key: f"median_{key}"`. Ignored when `reduce=True`.
Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A new tensordict, or a tensor if `reduce=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.arange(5.0), b=torch.arange(5.0) * 2, batch_size=[5])
>>> td.quantile(0.5)["b"]
tensor(4.)
>>> td.quantile(torch.tensor([0.25, 0.75]), dim=0)["a"]
tensor([1., 3.])
>>> td.quantile(0.5, reduce=True) # the median of the ten elements
tensor(2.5000)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.record_stream

TensorDictBase.record_stream(*stream: [Stream](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cuda.streams.Stream.html#torch.cuda.streams.Stream)*) → Self

Marks the tensor leaves of the tensordict as used by `stream`.

Calls [`record_stream()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.record_stream.html#torch.Tensor.record_stream) on every tensor leaf: when
a leaf is freed, its memory is not reused until the work queued on
`stream` at that time is complete. A tensordict can be marked with
one stream only.

Parameters:

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

 stream.

# TensorDictBase.recv

TensorDictBase.recv(*src: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | 'TensorDictPipe' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *group: 'torch.distributed.ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *group_src: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *init_tag: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *pseudo_rand: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *consolidated: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

Receives the leaves that [`send()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.send.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.send) sends, and writes them into the tensordict in place.

The tensordict must have the keys, shapes and dtypes of the tensordict
that the sender sends. See [`send()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.send.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.send) for an example, and
[Distributed tensordicts](../../distributed.html#distributed).

Parameters:

**src** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*TensorDictPipe*](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe)*,**optional*) - the global rank of the sender,
or a [`TensorDictPipe`](tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe.html#tensordict._ucxx.TensorDictPipe) to receive from
with UCXX, which ignores the other arguments. Exclusive with
`group_src`: pass exactly one of them. Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - the process group.
Defaults to `None`, the default process group.
- **group_src** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the rank of the sender in `group`, which
must be given. Exclusive with `src`. The messages then go through
the backend of `group` directly, so `group` can be a standalone
`ProcessGroup` built on a store, never
registered by [`init_process_group()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.init_process_group) or
[`new_group()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.new_group). Defaults to `None`.
- **init_tag** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the `init_tag` that the sender passed.
Defaults to `0`.
- **pseudo_rand** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the `pseudo_rand` that the sender
passed. Defaults to `False`.
- **consolidated** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, receives one message into
the consolidated storage of the tensordict, which updates all its
leaves, as sent by `send(consolidated=True)`. The tensordict must
be consolidated already, for example by
`consolidate(metadata=True)` or [`from_remote_init()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_remote_init.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_remote_init);
otherwise an `AttributeError` is raised. `init_tag` and
`pseudo_rand` are ignored. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

With a pipe, the received tensordict, which is `self` only if the
tensordict is consolidated with the layout of the data, so use the
return value. With `consolidated=True`, `None`. Otherwise, the
tag of the last leaf received.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if both or none of `src` and `group_src` are given, or
 if `group_src` is given without `group`.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.reduce

TensorDictBase.reduce(*dst*, *op=None*, *async_op=False*, *return_premature=False*, *group=None*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Reduces each leaf over all the ranks of the group, into the tensordict of rank `dst`.

Every rank of the group must call it, with a tensordict of the same
structure. Each leaf is reduced in place with
[`torch.distributed.reduce()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.reduce). After the call, rank `dst` holds the
result. On the other ranks, the values of the tensordict are not defined
(with `gloo`, they can hold partial results): clone the tensordict
before the call if you need them. See [Collectives](../../distributed.html#distributed-collectives).

Parameters:

- **dst** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the rank that receives the result.
- **op** ([*ReduceOp*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.ReduceOp)*,**optional*) - the reduction. Defaults to
`None`, which is `torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM`.
- **async_op** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the reductions of all the
leaves run at the same time, and the call waits for them unless
`return_premature=True`. Defaults to `False`.
- **return_premature** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - with `async_op=True`, if
`True`, returns the list of `Work` objects of the reductions
without waiting for them: call `wait()` on each one before you use
the tensordict. Defaults to `False`.
- **group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - the process group.
Defaults to `None`, the default process group.

Returns:

With `async_op=True` and `return_premature=True`, a list of
`Work` objects. Otherwise, `None`.

Examples

This example runs in two processes: add it to the
[runner script of the distributed guide](../../distributed.html#distributed) and
pass it to `run`.

```
def reduce(rank, world_size):
 td = TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3) * (rank + 1), batch_size=[3])
 td.reduce(dst=0, op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM)
 if rank == 0:
 print(td["a"]) # with 2 ranks: tensor([3., 3., 3.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.refine_names

TensorDictBase.refine_names(**names*) → Self

Names the unnamed batch dimensions, and checks the named ones, in place.

Each entry of `names` goes with one batch dimension. An unnamed
dimension takes the new name, or stays unnamed for `None`. A named
dimension must get its own name. `names` can hold one `...`, which
keeps the names of the dimensions that it covers. This follows
`torch.Tensor.refine_names()`.

Parameters:

***names** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**None*) - one name per batch dimension, or fewer with
one `...`.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if a named dimension gets another name, or `None`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(batch_size=[3, 4, 5], names=["a", None, None])
>>> td.refine_names("a", None, "c").names
['a', None, 'c']
>>> td.refine_names(..., "b", "c").names
['a', 'b', 'c']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.rename

TensorDictBase.rename(**names*, ***rename_map*)

Returns a shallow copy of the tensordict with new names for its batch dimensions.

Pass either the new names, one per batch dimension, or keyword
arguments that map old names to new ones. The leaves are not copied
(see [`copy()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.copy.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.copy)), and the names of the tensordict do not change.
The nested tensordicts of the copy get the new names for the batch
dimensions they share with it.

Parameters:

- ***names** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**None*) - the new names, one per batch dimension, or
a single `None` to clear every name. Exclusive with
`**rename_map`.
- ****rename_map** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**None*) - new names by old name, as in
`rename(old="new")`. Exclusive with `*names`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if both or neither of `names` and `rename_map` are
 passed, or if a key of `rename_map` is not a name of the
 tensordict.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(batch_size=[1, 2, 3, 4], names=list("abcd"))
>>> td.rename(c="g").names
['a', 'b', 'g', 'd']
>>> td.rename("w", "x", "y", "z").names
['w', 'x', 'y', 'z']
>>> td.rename(None).names
[None, None, None, None]
>>> td.names
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.rename

TensorDictBase.rename_(**names*, ***rename_map*)

Renames the batch dimensions of the tensordict in place and returns `self`.

Pass either the new names, one per batch dimension, or keyword
arguments that map old names to new ones. The nested tensordicts get
the new names for the batch dimensions they share with the tensordict.

Parameters:

- ***names** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**None*) - the new names, one per batch dimension, or
a single `None` to clear every name. Exclusive with
`**rename_map`.
- ****rename_map** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**None*) - new names by old name, as in
`rename_(old="new")`. Exclusive with `*names`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if both `names` and `rename_map` are passed, or
 neither (except on a tensordict with no batch dimension), or if
 a key of `rename_map` is not a name of the tensordict.

See also

[`rename()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename), which returns a renamed copy.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(batch_size=[1, 2, 3, 4], names=list("abcd"))
>>> td.rename_(c="g") is td
True
>>> td.names
['a', 'b', 'g', 'd']
>>> td.rename_(None).names
[None, None, None, None]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.rename_key

TensorDictBase.rename_key_(*old_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *new_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Renames an entry of the tensordict in place and returns the tensordict.

The value is not copied. A locked tensordict raises `RuntimeError`
(see [`lock_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_)). Until TensorDict 0.17, a locked
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) or store renames the key and
warns instead.

Parameters:

- **old_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key to rename. A missing key raises
`KeyError`.
- **new_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the new key of the entry. An empty key raises
`KeyError`. A key inside `old_key`, such as `("a", "b")`
for `"a"`, moves the entry there, as
`td.set(new_key, td.pop(old_key))` does.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `KeyError` is raised when
`new_key` is already present in the tensordict, unless it
lies inside `old_key`, which moves with the entry. If
`False`, the existing entry is overwritten. Defaults to
`False`.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3), "b": {"c": torch.ones(3)}}, [3])
>>> td = td.rename_key_("a", "x")
>>> td = td.rename_key_(("b", "c"), ("b", "y"))
>>> list(td.keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True))
[('b', 'y'), 'x']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.rename_keys

TensorDictBase.rename_keys(*mapping: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*, ***, *strict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → Self

Returns a tensordict with several keys renamed at once.

The tensordict is not modified. The result has a new tree of nested
tensordicts and shares every leaf with the tensordict, tensors and
non-tensor data alike. Its batch size, device and dimension names are
those of the tensordict, and it is not locked.

Every source is read before any destination is written, so swaps
(`{"a": "b", "b": "a"}`) and chains (`{"a": "b", "b": "c"}`) work.
A nested tensordict that the renaming leaves empty is removed. Other
empty nested tensordicts are kept.

A lazy stack renames the keys in each of its tensordicts, and removes a
nested tensordict only if the renaming empties it in all of them. A
tensorclass returns the same class, its destinations must be fields,
and its fields are never removed.
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) and the stores raise
`NotImplementedError`: call [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict) first.

To rename a single key in place, see [`rename_key_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename_key_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.rename_key_).

Parameters:

**mapping** (*Mapping**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*]*) - the old key of each entry
mapped to its new key. Both sides can be nested keys, so an
entry can move to another nested tensordict and a whole nested
tensordict can be renamed.

Keyword Arguments:

**strict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a source missing from the
tensordict raises `KeyError`. If `False`, it is skipped.
Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

A new tensordict of the same type as `self`, except that a
sub-tensordict view and a `TensorDictParams`
return a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), as [`exclude()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.exclude.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.exclude) does.

Raises:

- [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if `strict=True` and a source is missing, or if a key is
 empty.
- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if two sources have the same destination, if a source
 lies inside another source or a destination inside another
 destination, or if a destination is already present and is not
 renamed away.
- [**AttributeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#AttributeError) - if `self` is a tensorclass and a destination is
 not one of its fields.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(()))
>>> out = td.rename_keys({"a": "b", "b": "a"})
>>> out["a"], td["a"]
(tensor(1.), tensor(0.))
>>> td = TensorDict(raw=TensorDict(p=torch.zeros(3), u=torch.ones(3)))
>>> out = td.rename_keys({("raw", "p"): "pressure", ("raw", "u"): "velocity"})
>>> sorted(out.keys(include_nested=True)) # "raw" was emptied and removed
['pressure', 'velocity']
>>> out = td.rename_keys({"raw": "solution"})
>>> sorted(out.keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True))
[('solution', 'p'), ('solution', 'u')]
>>> td.rename_keys({("raw", "zz"): "z", ("raw", "p"): "p"}, strict=False)["p"]
tensor([0., 0., 0.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.repeat

TensorDictBase.repeat(**repeats: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Repeats the batch along each batch dimension, as [`torch.Tensor.repeat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.repeat.html#torch.Tensor.repeat) does.

The whole batch is repeated, as with [`numpy.tile()`](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.tile.html#numpy.tile). To repeat
each element next to itself instead, as with [`numpy.repeat()`](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.repeat.html#numpy.repeat), use
[`repeat_interleave()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.repeat_interleave.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.repeat_interleave). Unlike [`expand()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.expand.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.expand), it copies the data.
The feature dimensions are not repeated, and the names are kept.

Parameters:

***repeats** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the number of repetitions along each batch
dimension, one per batch dimension, as integers or as one
`torch.Size`, list, tuple or tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

**inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict keeps its
identity and keys, its leaves are replaced one by one, and the
call returns `self`. A lazy stack, or a tensordict that
holds one, raises a `NotImplementedError`: call
[`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict) first. See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).
Defaults to `False`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if the number of repeats differs from the number of
 batch dimensions.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([[0, 1]]), b=torch.zeros(1, 2, 3), batch_size=[1, 2])
>>> out = td.repeat(2, 2)
>>> out["a"]
tensor([[0, 1, 0, 1],
 [0, 1, 0, 1]])
>>> out["b"].shape
torch.Size([2, 4, 3])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.repeat_interleave

TensorDictBase.repeat_interleave(*repeats: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *output_size: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Repeats each element of the batch along `dim`, as [`torch.Tensor.repeat_interleave()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.repeat_interleave.html#torch.Tensor.repeat_interleave) does.

Each element is repeated next to itself, as with [`numpy.repeat()`](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.repeat.html#numpy.repeat).
To repeat the whole batch instead, as with [`numpy.tile()`](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.tile.html#numpy.tile), use
[`repeat()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.repeat.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.repeat). The data is copied. With a `dim`, the names are
kept.

Parameters:

- **repeats** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the number of repetitions of each
element, broadcast to the size of `dim`.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch dimension to repeat along. Defaults
to `None`, which flattens the batch dimensions first, so the
result has one batch dimension. A `dim` past the batch
dimensions warns, and is used on the dimensions of the leaves.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
raising an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

- **output_size** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the size of the result along `dim`
(the sum of `repeats`). Passing it avoids the device
synchronization that computes it. Defaults to `None`, which
computes it.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict keeps its
identity and keys, its leaves are replaced one by one, and the
call returns `self`. It needs a `dim` and at least one
batch dimension. A lazy stack, or a tensordict that holds one,
raises a `NotImplementedError`: call [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict)
first. See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions). Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A tensordict with the same batch size, except along `dim`, or
`self` with `inplace=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.tensor([[0, 1], [2, 3]]), batch_size=[2, 2])
>>> td.repeat_interleave(2, dim=0)["a"]
tensor([[0, 1],
 [0, 1],
 [2, 3],
 [2, 3]])
>>> td.repeat_interleave(torch.tensor([1, 2]), dim=1)["a"]
tensor([[0, 1, 1],
 [2, 3, 3]])
>>> td.repeat_interleave(2).batch_size
torch.Size([8])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).
