# TensorDictBase.to

TensorDictBase.to(**args*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Returns a tensordict cast to another device, dtype or memory format, or with a new batch size.

It accepts the forms of [`torch.Tensor.to()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.to.html#torch.Tensor.to), and some more:

- `to(device, dtype=None)`: moves every leaf to `device` and, if
`dtype` is given, casts it.
- `to(dtype)`: casts every tensor leaf to `dtype`, whatever its
original dtype (integer and boolean leaves too), unless
`cast_filter` selects the leaves to cast.
- `to(tensor)`: uses the device and the dtype of `tensor`.
- `to(other=tensordict)`: uses the device of `other`, and its
dtype if all its leaves share one. Otherwise the dtypes are kept.
- `to(batch_size=...)`: only sets the batch size, in place, and
returns `self`.
- `to(td.attrs())`: casts each leaf to the device and the dtype that
[`attrs()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.attrs.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.attrs) recorded for the same key. See
[Devices, dtypes, and memory](../../concepts/devices.html#devices).

The result is `self` when the device is already the device of the
tensordict and no dtype or memory format is given. Otherwise it is a
new tensordict, unless `inplace=True`. When only the device changes,
a consolidated tensordict gives a consolidated result, whose leaves
are views of one storage on the new device.

Parameters:

- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Its nested tensordicts get it too.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - the dtype of the tensor leaves of
the result.
- **tensor** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**optional*) - a tensor whose device and dtype
are the device and dtype of the result.

Keyword Arguments:

- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - how the leaves are copied. `None`
copies them with `non_blocking=True` and, when the target
is not a CUDA device (for example a copy to the host),
synchronizes once after all the copies are issued; for a CPU
target, only if a leaf comes from another device. Under
[`torch.compile()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile.html#torch.compile), these copies are blocking instead.
`True` copies without synchronizing: synchronize before you
read the results. `False` makes blocking copies. Defaults to
`None`. It can also follow the device, dtype or tensor
positionally, as in `to("cpu", torch.float64, False)`. A
positional `True` is ignored for now, with a
`FutureWarning`: the copies synchronize as for `None`.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
honoring it as the keyword `True` is.
- **memory_format** ([*memory_format*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.memory_format)*,**optional*) - the memory format of
the 4D and 5D tensors of the result, as in
[`torch.nn.Module.to()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module.to). Defaults to `None`, which keeps
the memory format.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - the batch size of the result.
When the device or dtype changes, every nested tensordict gets
exactly this batch size and the names are erased. Starting with
TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to setting the batch
size as `to(batch_size=...)` does without a device: nested
tensordicts with more batch dimensions keep their batch size,
nested lazy stacks stay lazy stacks (or raise, as there, if
they need more batch dimensions) and the names are kept. A
`FutureWarning` is emitted when the result will change.
Defaults to `None`, which keeps the batch size.
- **other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict whose device, and
dtype if all its leaves share one, are those of the result.
Defaults to `None`.
- **cast_filter** (*Callable**,**optional*) - a predicate
`fn(key, value) -> bool` that selects the tensor leaves the
dtype cast applies to. `key` is the nested key of the leaf as
a tuple of str, for example `("obs",)` or
`("next", "done")`. Leaves for which it returns `False`
keep their dtype, but still move to the new device or memory
format. It is not called on non-tensor data, without a dtype,
or with an attrs tensordict. An
[`UnbatchedTensor`](tensordict.UnbatchedTensor.html#tensordict.UnbatchedTensor) leaf is passed as is.
Helpers such as [`is_inexact()`](tensordict.is_inexact.html#tensordict.is_inexact) can be passed
directly. Defaults to the `cast_filter` of a tensorclass that
declares one, and to casting every leaf otherwise; pass
`None` to cast every leaf. The dtype shorthands
([`float()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.float.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.float), [`bfloat16()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bfloat16.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bfloat16), ...) take it too.
- **non_blocking_pin** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - 

if `True`, pins the tensors
before sending them to the device, in `num_threads`
threads. Defaults to `False`.

Note

Each call starts and joins its pinning threads, which costs
the same however little data there is. So
`non_blocking_pin=True` pays off only for large
tensordicts, with leaves of a MiB or more and tens of MiB
in total. For smaller tensordicts, `td.to("cuda")` is
usually the fastest, and
`td.pin_memory().to("cuda", non_blocking=True)` is also
faster than `non_blocking_pin=True`. Measure the
crossover on your machine.
- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `non_blocking_pin=True`, the
number of threads that pin the leaves, at most one per leaf.
`0` pins them on the calling thread. Defaults to `None`,
which starts up to `max(1, torch.get_num_threads() // 2)`
threads.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, writes the cast leaves into
the tensordict, which keeps its identity and keys, and returns
`self`. This can be faster when building a new tensordict is
what costs the most. See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions). Defaults
to `False`.

Returns:

`self` when nothing changes, with `inplace=True`, or when only
`batch_size` is given; a new tensordict otherwise.

This operation can be used as a context manager too. Inside the
`with` block, you work on the cast tensordict. When the block exits,
its entries are written back to the original tensordict, on the
original device. Use it to run a module that expects its input on a
specific device. See [Devices, dtypes, and memory](../../concepts/devices.html#devices).

Note

On exit, every entry is moved back to the original device. The
entries that already existed get their original dtype back, but
the new entries keep the dtype of the `with` block: after
`with td.to(torch.float64) as td64`, a new entry of `td64` is
`float64` in `td`. The original tensordict must not be
locked. If the block raises an exception, nothing is written back.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict({"a": 1.0}, [], device=None)
>>> data_int = data.to(torch.int) # casts to int
>>> data_int["a"]
tensor(1, dtype=torch.int32)
```

Cast the floating-point leaves only:

```
>>> from tensordict import is_inexact
>>> data = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), done=torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.bool))
>>> data_bf16 = data.to(torch.bfloat16, cast_filter=is_inexact)
>>> data_bf16["x"].dtype, data_bf16["done"].dtype
(torch.bfloat16, torch.bool)
```

The next lines need a CUDA device, so they are not run when the
documentation is tested.

```
>>> data_cuda = data.to("cuda:0") 
>>> data_cuda_int = data.to("cuda:0", torch.int) 
>>> data_cuda = data.to(torch.randn(3, device="cuda:0")) 
>>> data_cuda = data.to(other=TensorDict({}, [], device="cuda:0"))
```

Use it as a context manager for a temporary device change (CUDA
needed):

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3], device="cpu")
>>> with td.to("cuda") as td_gpu: 
... _ = td_gpu.update(mod(td_gpu)) # runs on the GPU
>>> # The entries are written back on the original device
>>> assert td["y"].device.type == "cpu"
```

A temporary dtype change runs on CPU. The new entry keeps the dtype
of the `with` block:

```
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with td.to(torch.float64) as td64:
... td64["y"] = td64["x"] + 1
>>> td["x"].dtype, td["y"].dtype
(torch.float32, torch.float64)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_csv

TensorDictBase.to_csv(*path*, ***, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*)

Writes the tensordict to a CSV file, with one column per leaf.

The tensordict is converted with [`to_pandas()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas), so the same
rules apply, and written with `pandas.DataFrame.to_csv()`
without the index. Requires pandas. [`from_csv()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_csv.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_csv) reads the
file back.

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the path of the CSV file.

Keyword Arguments:

- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if given, joins the keys of nested
entries with it to build the column names: with
`separator="."`, the entry `("obs", "x")` becomes the
column `"obs.x"`. Required when the tensordict has nested
tensordicts. Defaults to `None`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to `pandas.DataFrame.to_csv()`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - as [`to_pandas()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas).

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.arange(2), b=TensorDict(c=torch.zeros(2)), batch_size=[2])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "data.csv")
... td.to_csv(path, separator=".")
... with open(path) as f:
... print(f.read())
a,b.c
0,0.0
1,0.0
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_dict

TensorDictBase.to_dict(***, *retain_none: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *convert_tensors: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['numpy'] = False*, *tolist_first: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

Returns a nested dictionary with the entries of the tensordict.

Nested tensordicts and tensorclasses become nested dicts. The tensors
are not copied unless `convert_tensors` is set. Non-tensor data is
returned as its Python value.

Keyword Arguments:

- **retain_none** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the `None` fields of
tensorclasses are written in the dict as `None`. If
`False`, they are dropped. Defaults to `True`.
- **convert_tensors** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if `True`, tensors are
converted to (nested) Python lists with
[`torch.Tensor.tolist()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.tolist.html#torch.Tensor.tolist). If `"numpy"`, they are converted
to NumPy arrays. If `False`, they are kept as tensors.
Defaults to `False`.
- **tolist_first** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a nested tensordict is
converted with [`tolist()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.tolist.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.tolist), so that a nested tensordict
with batch dimensions becomes a list of dicts, one per element.
Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A dict whose keys are those of the tensordict.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - on a lazy stack whose tensordicts have different
 keys (see [Variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking-variable-size)).

See also

[`tolist()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.tolist.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.tolist), [`numpy()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.numpy.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.numpy) and
[`from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict), which converts back.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>>
>>> td = TensorDict(
... a=torch.arange(6).view(2, 3),
... b=TensorDict(c=torch.arange(4).reshape(2, 2), batch_size=(2, 2)),
... batch_size=(2,)
... )
>>> print(td.to_dict())
{'a': tensor([[0, 1, 2],
 [3, 4, 5]]), 'b': {'c': tensor([[0, 1],
 [2, 3]])}}
>>> print(td.to_dict(convert_tensors=True))
{'a': [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]], 'b': {'c': [[0, 1], [2, 3]]}}
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_h5

TensorDictBase.to_h5(*filename*, ***kwargs*) → [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

Writes the tensordict to a new HDF5 file and returns a tensordict backed by it.

Each leaf becomes a dataset of the file, and each nested tensordict a
group. An existing file at `filename` is overwritten. The batch size
and the names of the batch dimensions are kept. Requires `h5py`.
[`from_h5()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_h5.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_h5) opens the file again. See [Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving).

Parameters:

- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**path*) - the path of the HDF5 file.
- ****kwargs** - passed to `h5py.Group.create_dataset()`, for example
`compression="gzip"`.

Returns:

A [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) backed by the new file.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(1000), b={"c": torch.zeros(1000, 3)}, batch_size=[1000])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... td_h5 = td.to_h5(os.path.join(tmpdir, "data.h5"), compression="gzip")
... print(type(td_h5).__name__, td_h5.batch_size, td_h5["b", "c"].shape)
... td_h5.close()
PersistentTensorDict torch.Size([1000]) torch.Size([1000, 3])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_json

TensorDictBase.to_json(*path*, ***, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *lines: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs*)

Writes the tensordict to a JSON file, as an array of records.

Each element of the tensordict becomes one record, with one field per

and otherwise with the [`json`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html#module-json) module. [`from_json()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_json.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_json) reads
the file back.

Parameters:

Keyword Arguments:

- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if given, joins the keys of nested
entries with it to build the column names: with
`separator="."`, the entry `("obs", "x")` becomes the
column `"obs.x"`. Required when the tensordict has nested
tensordicts. Defaults to `None`.
- **lines** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, writes JSON Lines, one record
per line. Defaults to `False`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to `pandas.DataFrame.to_json()`. Ignored

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
```

# TensorDictBase.to_lazystack

TensorDictBase.to_lazystack(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*)

Returns a lazy stack of the slices of the tensordict along `dim`.

The tensordict is unbound along `dim` and the slices are stacked in
a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) (see [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)).
The slices are views: writing into a tensordict of the stack in place
writes into the original data. The batch size does not change. A lazy
stack along `dim` is returned as it is, and a lazy stack along
another dimension is restacked, which changes its stack dimension.

Parameters:

**dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension to stack along. Defaults to
`0`.

Returns:

A lazy stack with `stack_dim == dim`, or `self` when the
tensordict is already one.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2, 3), batch_size=(2, 3))
>>> stack = td.to_lazystack()
>>> type(stack).__name__, stack.batch_size, stack.stack_dim
('LazyStackedTensorDict', torch.Size([2, 3]), 0)
>>> stack.to_lazystack(1).stack_dim
1
>>> stack.to_lazystack(0) is stack
True
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.to_mds

TensorDictBase.to_mds(***, *columns: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]*, *keep_local: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *compression: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *hashes: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *size_limit: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = 67108864*, *writer: 'streaming.MDSWriter' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *finish_writer: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Writes the tensordict to a MosaicML Streaming (MDS) dataset.

Each element along the first batch dimension is one sample of the
dataset; a tensordict without batch dimensions is one sample. Tensors are
written as NumPy arrays, and zero-dimensional ones as Python numbers.
Read the dataset back with `streaming.StreamingDataset`. See the
[streaming documentation](https://docs.mosaicml.com/projects/streaming).

The MDS writer has limited support for nested dictionaries: call
[`flatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys) before writing, and
[`unflatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unflatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unflatten_keys) after reading.

The type of a non-tensor column is read from its first sample, which
must not be `None`; the other samples must have the same type, or be
`None`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **columns** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*of**str to str**,**optional*) - the MDS encoding of each
column, for example `{"obs": "ndarray", "name": "str"}`.
Defaults to `None`, which infers them from the first sample.
- **out** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - 

where to write the shard files:

- a local directory: the shards are written there;
- a remote location: the shards are written to a local temporary
directory, uploaded, and deleted;
- a `(local_dir, remote_dir)` tuple: the shards are written to
`local_dir` and uploaded to `remote_dir`.
- **keep_local** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and the dataset is uploaded,
keeps the local copy. Defaults to `False`.
- **compression** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the compression, as `"name"` or
`"name:level"`. Defaults to `None`.
- **hashes** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the hash algorithms to apply to the
shard files. Defaults to `None`.
- **size_limit** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the size after which a new shard
starts, in bytes or as a string such as `"100kb"`. `None`
writes one shard. Ignored if `writer` is passed. Defaults to
`1 << 26` (64 MiB).
- **writer** (*streaming.MDSWriter**,**optional*) - the writer to use. Defaults to
`None`, which creates one from `out` and the other keyword
arguments, and finishes it after writing.
- **finish_writer** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - whether to finish a writer passed as
`writer` after writing, which writes the dataset index. Pass
`False` to write more samples through it, and finish it
yourself afterwards, once. A writer that `to_mds` creates is
always finished. Defaults to `None`, which leaves the writer
open for a tensordict without batch dimensions, and finishes it,
with a `FutureWarning`, for a tensordict with batch dimensions.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to leaving
the writer open in both cases.
- ****kwargs** - passed to `streaming.MDSWriter`.

Raises:

- [**ImportError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ImportError) - if `mosaicml-streaming` is not installed.
- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if the tensordict is empty.

Examples

The example needs `mosaicml-streaming` (`pip install mosaicml-streaming`).

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> td = LazyStackedTensorDict(
... TensorDict(a=0, c=torch.zeros(2), d="a string"),
... TensorDict(a=1, c=torch.zeros(3), d="another string"),
... )
>>> from streaming import StreamingDataset 
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir: 
... td.to_mds(out=tmpdir)
... dataset = StreamingDataset(local=tmpdir, remote=None, batch_size=2)
... loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
... dataset, batch_size=2, collate_fn=LazyStackedTensorDict.from_list
... )
... batch = next(iter(loader)) # a lazy stack of the two samples
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_module

TensorDictBase.to_module(*module: [Module](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)*, ***, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *return_swap: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *swap_dest=None*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *preserve_module_state: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *memo=None*)

Writes the content of the tensordict into the parameters and buffers of a module, recursively.

The keys of the tensordict must match the names of the module
attributes, as [`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_module) gives them. A nested key is a
submodule: `("layers", "0", "weight")` is `module.layers[0].weight`.

`to_module` can also be used as a context manager, to populate a
module with other parameters for the duration of a `with` block (see
the second example). When the block exits, the original parameters are
written back, also if the block raises an exception.

Parameters:

**module** (*nn.Module*) - a module to write the parameters into.

Keyword Arguments:

- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies the values into the
existing parameters and buffers of the module, which keep
their identity. Otherwise the leaves of the tensordict replace
them. Defaults to `None`, which behaves like `False`.
Cannot be passed with `use_state_dict=True`.
- **return_swap** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, returns the parameters
and buffers that the module held before the call. Defaults to
`True`.
- **swap_dest** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - with `return_swap`, a
tensordict to write the old values into and to return.
Defaults to `None`, which returns a new tensordict.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, loads the values
through the state-dict API, so that the module's state-dict
hooks run. Defaults to `False`.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.
- **preserve_module_state** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - 

if `True`, existing
`Parameter` and buffer registrations are
preserved when writing tensor leaves to `module`: parameters
remain parameters with their original `requires_grad` value,
and buffers remain registered buffers. Leaves that are not
parameters but require gradients, or that are batched by
[`vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap), are registered as they are, so that
gradients still reach them. If `False`, a leaf that is not a
`Parameter` replaces the attribute as it is,
which can deregister an existing parameter (the historical
behavior). Defaults to `True`.

Changed in version 0.15: `preserve_module_state=None`, deprecated in 0.14, is no
longer accepted.
- **memo** - no longer accepted: passing it raises a `RuntimeError`.

Returns:

A tensordict of the values that the module held before the call
(or `swap_dest`) if `return_swap` is `True`, `None`
otherwise.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> module = nn.Linear(3, 4)
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> zeros = params.data.clone().zero_()
>>> old_params = zeros.to_module(module)
>>> bool((module.weight == 0).all())
True
>>> _ = old_params.to_module(module) # restores the original values
>>> bool((module.weight != 0).any())
True
```

Use the tensordict as a context manager to make a functional call.
When the block exits, the original parameters are written back:

```
>>> with zeros.to_module(module):
... y = module(torch.ones(2, 3)) # runs with zeroed parameters
>>> bool((y == 0).all())
True
>>> bool((module.weight != 0).any())
True
```

The original parameters are written back if the block raises an
exception too:

```
>>> try:
... with zeros.to_module(module):
... raise ValueError("stop")
... except ValueError:
... pass
>>> bool((module.weight != 0).any())
True
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_namedtuple

TensorDictBase.to_namedtuple(*dest_cls: [type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

Converts the tensordict to a named tuple, recursively.

Each nested tensordict becomes a nested named tuple. Without
`dest_cls`, each level is an instance of a new named tuple class,
`GenericDict`, whose fields are the keys. The `None` fields of
tensorclasses are dropped.

Parameters:

**dest_cls** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*,**optional*) - the named tuple class of the result. A
nested tensordict is converted to `dest_cls` too if
`dest_cls` takes its keys, and to a `GenericDict`
otherwise. Defaults to `None`.

See also

[`from_namedtuple()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_namedtuple.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_namedtuple), which
converts back.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> import torch
>>> data = TensorDict({
... "a_tensor": torch.zeros((3)),
... "nested": {"a_tensor": torch.zeros((3)), "a_string": "zero!"}}, [3])
>>> data.to_namedtuple()
GenericDict(a_tensor=tensor([0., 0., 0.]), nested=GenericDict(a_tensor=tensor([0., 0., 0.]), a_string='zero!'))
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_padded_tensor

TensorDictBase.to_padded_tensor(*padding=0.0*, *mask_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a tensordict whose nested-tensor leaves are converted to padded tensors.

Calls [`torch.nested.to_padded_tensor()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/nested.html#torch.nested.to_padded_tensor) on every leaf that is a
nested tensor, and keeps the other leaves. If the batch size has a
`-1` (a ragged dimension, as in a dense version of a lazy stack
of tensordicts with different batch sizes), the batch size of the
result is computed from the padded leaves.

Parameters:

- **padding** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*,**optional*) - the value of the padding. Defaults to
`0.0`.
- **mask_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - a key where a boolean mask of the
valid (not padded) elements is written. It needs a ragged batch
dimension, or a `RuntimeError` is raised. Defaults to
`None`, which writes no mask.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> stack = TensorDict.lazy_stack([
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]),
... TensorDict(a=torch.ones(4), batch_size=[4]),
... ])
>>> td = stack.densify(layout=torch.jagged)
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([2, -1])
>>> padded = td.to_padded_tensor(padding=-1.0, mask_key="mask")
>>> padded.batch_size
torch.Size([2, 4])
>>> padded["a"]
tensor([[ 0., 0., 0., -1.],
 [ 1., 1., 1., 1.]])
>>> padded["mask"]
tensor([[ True, True, True, False],
 [ True, True, True, True]])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.to_pandas

TensorDictBase.to_pandas(***, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Converts the tensordict to a pandas DataFrame, with one column per leaf.

Each leaf must hold one value per row: a tensor of shape
`[num_rows]`, or non-tensor data. Tensors are copied to the CPU and
converted to NumPy arrays. Non-tensor data becomes a column of Python
values. Requires pandas.

Keyword Arguments:

**separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if given, joins the keys of nested
entries with it to build the column names: with
`separator="."`, the entry `("obs", "x")` becomes the
column `"obs.x"`. Required when the tensordict has nested
tensordicts. Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A `pd.DataFrame` with one row per element of the tensordict.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if the tensordict has a nested tensordict and no
 `separator`, or if a tensor has more than one dimension.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.arange(3), "b": torch.zeros(3)}, [3])
>>> df = td.to_pandas()
>>> print(df)
 a b
0 0 0.0
1 1 0.0
2 2 0.0
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_parquet

TensorDictBase.to_parquet(*path*, ***, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*)

Writes the tensordict to a Parquet file, with one column per leaf.

The columns are built as in [`to_pandas()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas), so the same rules
apply. Requires pyarrow or pandas. When pyarrow is installed, the
file is written with `pyarrow.parquet.write_table`, from a pandas
DataFrame if pandas is installed and from the columns directly
otherwise. With pandas alone, the file is written with
`pandas.DataFrame.to_parquet()`, which then needs fastparquet.
[`from_parquet()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_parquet.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_parquet) reads the file back.

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the path of the Parquet file.

Keyword Arguments:

- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if given, joins the keys of nested
entries with it to build the column names: with
`separator="."`, the entry `("obs", "x")` becomes the
column `"obs.x"`. Required when the tensordict has nested
tensordicts. Defaults to `None`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the Parquet writer.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - as [`to_pandas()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pandas).

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.arange(2), b=TensorDict(c=torch.zeros(2)), batch_size=[2])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "data.parquet")
... td.to_parquet(path, separator=".")
... td2 = TensorDict.from_parquet(path, separator=".")
>>> td2["b", "c"]
tensor([0., 0.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_pytree

TensorDictBase.to_pytree()

Rebuilds the pytree that [`from_pytree()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pytree.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pytree) converted to this tensordict.

# TensorDictBase.to_store

TensorDictBase.to_store(***, *backend: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *device=None*, ***kwargs*) → [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

Uploads the tensordict to a key-value server and returns a tensordict backed by it.

The entries are written to a Redis or Dragonfly server, under the key
namespace `prefix`. The result reads and writes the server. A lazy
stack is uploaded in chunks, without building the dense stack in
memory, and gives a [`LazyStackedTensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore).
Requires the `redis` Python package and a running server. See
[Large datasets and storage backends](../../storage.html#storage).

Keyword Arguments:

- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the server type: `"redis"` or
`"dragonfly"`. Defaults to `"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the server hostname. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the server port. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number. Defaults to `0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix domain socket
to connect through instead of `host` and `port`. Defaults
to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the key namespace of the data on the
server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensors that the result reads. Defaults to `None`, which
uses the device of the tensordict.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the connection of the client.

Returns:

A [`TensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore), or a
[`LazyStackedTensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore) for a lazy
stack.

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`, and the
last line a Dragonfly server on the host `dragonfly-host`, so it
is not run when the documentation is tested.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"obs": torch.randn(10, 84)}, [10])
>>> store_td = td.to_store(host="localhost") 
>>> store_td["obs"].shape 
torch.Size([10, 84])
>>>
>>> # Using Dragonfly instead of Redis
>>> store_td = td.to_store(backend="dragonfly", host="dragonfly-host")
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_struct_array

TensorDictBase.to_struct_array() → [ndarray](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray)

Converts the tensordict to a NumPy structured array, with one field per entry.

The shape of the array is the batch size. A nested tensordict becomes
a nested structured field, and the feature dimensions of a tensor
become the shape of its field. String values become `"U"` fields of
at least 10 characters. Unlike [`from_struct_array()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array), this
method copies the data: the array does not share memory with the
tensordict.

Returns:

A `np.ndarray` with a structured dtype.

See also

[`from_struct_array()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array), which converts back, and
[`numpy()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.numpy.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.numpy) to convert to a dict of NumPy arrays.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({'a': torch.tensor([1, 2, 3]), 'b': torch.tensor([4.0, 5.0, 6.0])}, batch_size=[3])
>>> arr = td.to_struct_array()
>>> print(arr)
[(1, 4.) (2, 5.) (3, 6.)]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.to_tensordict

TensorDictBase.to_tensordict(***, *retain_none: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) copy of this tensordict.

Every tensor is cloned, and every nested tensordict and tensorclass is
converted to a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), recursively. Use it to
get a regular, unlocked tensordict in memory from a lazy stack, a
memory-mapped or locked tensordict, a
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) or a tensorclass. The batch
size, device and names of the batch dimensions are kept, with one
exception: if the tensordicts of a lazy stack have no names, the
result has no names either, even when the stack dimension has a name
(from `stack_dim_name` or the `names` setter). Name the dimension
again with [`refine_names()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names), as in the example.

Keyword Arguments:

**retain_none** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the `None` fields of
tensorclass instances are written as entries of the result.
Defaults to `None`, which behaves like `False`: the
`None` fields are dropped.

Returns:

A new [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) with copies of the values.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import LazyStackedTensorDict, TensorDict
>>> stack = LazyStackedTensorDict(
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3)), stack_dim=0)
>>> td = stack.to_tensordict()
>>> type(td).__name__, td.batch_size
('TensorDict', torch.Size([2]))
>>> stack.names = ["s"]
>>> stack.to_tensordict().names
[None]
>>> stack.to_tensordict().refine_names("s").names
['s']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.to_zarr

TensorDictBase.to_zarr(*filename*, ***, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

Writes the tensordict to a new zarr store and returns a tensordict backed by it.

Each leaf becomes an array of the store, and each nested tensordict a
group. An existing store at `filename` is overwritten. The batch
size and the names of the batch dimensions are saved in the store
attributes, so that [`from_zarr()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_zarr.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_zarr) restores them. Requires
`zarr>=3.0`. See [Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving).

Parameters:

- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**path**or**zarr store*) - the path of the zarr store (a
directory), or a `zarr.abc.store.Store` instance (e.g. a
`zarr.storage.ZipStore`).
- ****kwargs** - passed to [`zarr.Group.create_array()`](https://zarr.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/zarr/group/#zarr.Group.create_array). By default
each tensor is stored as one uncompressed chunk. Pass
`chunks=...` or `compressors=...` to change that (for
example to read rows without loading the whole array, or to
compress on disk). `chunks` applies to the leading
dimensions of each leaf, and the trailing dimensions are left
whole: `chunks=(16,)` chunks every leaf along its first
dimension in blocks of 16.

Keyword Arguments:

**allow_pickle** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the read policy of the returned
tensordict for pickled non-tensor values. `False` rejects
them. `None` and `True` read them, since this call wrote
them. Opening the store again with [`from_zarr()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_zarr.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_zarr) uses
the policy of that call. Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) backed by the new store.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(1000), b={"c": torch.zeros(1000, 3)}, batch_size=[1000])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... td_zarr = td.to_zarr(os.path.join(tmpdir, "store.zarr"), chunks=(100,))
... print(type(td_zarr).__name__, td_zarr.batch_size, td_zarr["b", "c"].shape)
PersistentTensorDict torch.Size([1000]) torch.Size([1000, 3])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.tolist

TensorDictBase.tolist(***, *convert_nodes: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *convert_tensors: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['numpy'] = False*, *tolist_first: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *as_linked_list: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

Returns the elements of the tensordict as nested lists, one level per batch dimension.

The innermost elements are the tensordict indexed at every batch
index, converted with [`to_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict): for batch size `[2, 3]`,
the result is a list of 2 lists of 3 dicts. A tensordict without
batch dimensions returns one dict.

Keyword Arguments:

- **convert_nodes** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the elements are
converted to dicts. If `False`, they are kept as
tensordicts. Defaults to `True`.
- **convert_tensors** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - as in [`to_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict):
if `True`, tensors become Python lists, and if `"numpy"`,
NumPy arrays. Requires `convert_nodes=True`. Defaults to
`False`.
- **tolist_first** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - as in [`to_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict): if
`True`, a nested tensordict with batch dimensions becomes a
list of dicts. Defaults to `False`.
- **as_linked_list** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, returns a
[`LinkedList`](tensordict.utils.LinkedList.html#tensordict.utils.LinkedList): assigning an element of
the outer list (`result[0] = {...}`) writes it into the
tensordict. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A list (nested once per batch dimension), or a dict (or `self`
if `convert_nodes=False`) when the tensordict has no batch
dimensions.

Raises:

[**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - if `convert_tensors` is set and `convert_nodes=False`.

See also

[`to_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_dict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... a=torch.arange(4).view(2, 2),
... b=TensorDict(c=torch.arange(8).view(2, 2, 2), batch_size=(2, 2, 2)),
... batch_size=(2,),
... )
>>> td.tolist()
[{'a': tensor([0, 1]), 'b': {'c': tensor([[0, 1],
 [2, 3]])}}, {'a': tensor([2, 3]), 'b': {'c': tensor([[4, 5],
 [6, 7]])}}]
>>> td.tolist(convert_tensors=True)
[{'a': [0, 1], 'b': {'c': [[0, 1], [2, 3]]}}, {'a': [2, 3], 'b': {'c': [[4, 5], [6, 7]]}}]
>>> td.tolist(tolist_first=True, convert_tensors=True)[0]
{'a': [0, 1], 'b': [[{'c': 0}, {'c': 1}], [{'c': 2}, {'c': 3}]]}
>>> type(td.tolist(convert_nodes=False)[0]).__name__
'TensorDict'
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.transpose

TensorDictBase.transpose(*dim0*, *dim1*)

Returns a tensordict with the batch dimensions `dim0` and `dim1` swapped.

The leaves of the result are views of the original leaves, so an
in-place change of the result changes the tensordict too. The names
are swapped with the dimensions. To write new entries back to the
tensordict, use the result as a context manager.

Parameters:

- **dim0** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the first batch dimension to swap.
- **dim1** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the second batch dimension to swap.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> tensordict = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3, 4, 5)}, [3, 4])
>>> tensordict_transpose = tensordict.transpose(0, 1)
>>> print(tensordict_transpose.shape)
torch.Size([4, 3])
>>> with tensordict.transpose(0, 1) as tensordict_transpose:
... tensordict_transpose["b"] = torch.zeros(4, 3)
>>> print(tensordict.get("b").shape)
torch.Size([3, 4])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.type

TensorDictBase.type(*dst_type: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*, ***, *cast_filter: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Returns a tensordict whose tensor leaves are cast to `dst_type`.

Each leaf is cast with [`torch.Tensor.type()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.type.html#torch.Tensor.type).

Unlike [`int()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int), [`float()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.float.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.float) and `to(dtype)`, it returns an
unlocked tensordict for a locked one, with a `FutureWarning`.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to a locked
result, as these casts return.

Parameters:

**dst_type** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - the dtype, or the name of a tensor
type such as `"torch.IntTensor"`.

Keyword Arguments:

**cast_filter** (*Callable**,**optional*) - a predicate
`fn(key, value) -> bool` that selects the tensor leaves to
cast, as in [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to). Defaults to `None`, which casts every
tensor leaf (a tensorclass uses its own `cast_filter`, if it
declares one).

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.unbind

TensorDictBase.unbind(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase), ...]

Returns a tuple of the tensordicts along a batch dimension, as [`torch.Tensor.unbind()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.unbind.html#torch.Tensor.unbind) does.

The tensordicts of the result hold views of the original tensors. They
are locked if the tensordict is shared or memory-mapped.

Parameters:

**dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch dimension to remove. The result has
`batch_size[dim]` tensordicts.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({
... 'x': torch.arange(12).reshape(3, 4),
... }, batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> td0, td1, td2 = td.unbind(0)
>>> td0['x']
tensor([0, 1, 2, 3])
>>> td1['x']
tensor([4, 5, 6, 7])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.unflatten

TensorDictBase.unflatten(*dim*, *unflattened_size*, ***, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns a tensordict whose batch dimension `dim` is split into several.

It works as [`torch.unflatten()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.unflatten.html#torch.unflatten) does on the batch. The leaves keep
their feature dimensions, and are views of the original leaves when the
memory layout allows it. The last new dimension keeps the name of
`dim`, and the others have no name.

It can be used as a context manager, as [`unsqueeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze) can: when
the `with` block exits, the entries of the block are written back to
the tensordict with the inverse operation.

Parameters:

- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch dimension to unflatten.
- **unflattened_size** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)) - the sizes of the new
dimensions. Their product is `batch_size[dim]`, and one of
them can be `-1`.

Keyword Arguments:

**inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict keeps its
identity and keys, its leaves are replaced one by one, and the
call returns `self`. A leaf keeps its storage when the
unflatten can return a view of it. A lazy stack, or a
tensordict that holds one, raises a `NotImplementedError`:
call [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict) first. See
[In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions). Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({
... "a": torch.arange(60).view(3, 4, 5),
... "b": torch.arange(12).view(3, 4)},
... batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> td_flat = td.flatten(0, 1)
>>> td_unflat = td_flat.unflatten(0, [3, 4])
>>> assert (td == td_unflat).all()
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.unflatten_keys

TensorDictBase.unflatten_keys(*separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = '.'*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Returns a tensordict with the keys that hold the separator split into nested keys.

The leaf at `"a.b.c"` moves to `("a", "b", "c")` with the default
separator. The leaves are not copied. The new nested tensordicts take
the batch size, dimension names and device of the tensordict. The
result has the type of the tensordict for a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) and a lazy stack. A split key that
would overwrite an existing entry raises a `KeyError`.
[`flatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys) does the reverse.

It can be used as a context manager: the changes made to the nested
tensordict in the `with` block are written back to the tensordict
when the block exits.

Parameters:

- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the string that separates the parts of
a nested key. Defaults to `"."`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the entries are moved in
the tensordict itself, which is returned. Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": 1, "b.c": 2, "e.f.g": 3})
>>> nested = td.unflatten_keys()
>>> list(nested.keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True, sort=True))
['a', ('b', 'c'), ('e', 'f', 'g')]
>>> nested["e", "f", "g"]
tensor(3)
>>> td = TensorDict({"a/b": torch.zeros(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> td.unflatten_keys("/")["a"].batch_size
torch.Size([3])
```

With [`flatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys), it converts a state dict to a nested
tensordict and back:

```
>>> model = torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(3, 4))
>>> params = TensorDict(model.state_dict()).unflatten_keys(".")
>>> sorted(params.keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True))
[('0', 'bias'), ('0', 'weight')]
>>> _ = model.load_state_dict(params.flatten_keys(".").to_dict())
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.unlock

TensorDictBase.unlock_() → Self

Unlocks the tensordict and its nested tensordicts, and returns it.

After this call, entries can be added, removed and renamed again. See
[`lock_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_) for what a lock blocks.

Can be used as a context manager: the tensordict is locked again when
the `with` block exits, also if the block raises an exception.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the tensordict, or one of its nested tensordicts,
 is also an entry of another locked tensordict. Unlock that
 parent first. The tensordict stays locked.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3], lock=True)
>>> with td.unlock_():
... td["b"] = torch.ones(3)
>>> td.is_locked
True
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

Changing the shape of a TensorDict

# TensorDictBase.unsqueeze

TensorDictBase.unsqueeze(**args*, ***kwargs*)

Returns a tensordict with a new batch dimension of size 1 at position `dim`.

The tensors of the result are views of the original tensors. The new
dimension has no name.

Parameters:

**dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the position of the new dimension, in
`[-batch_dims - 1, batch_dims]` as for [`torch.unsqueeze()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.unsqueeze.html#torch.unsqueeze).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({
... 'x': torch.arange(24).reshape(3, 4, 2),
... }, batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> td = td.unsqueeze(-2)
>>> td.shape
torch.Size([3, 1, 4])
>>> td.get("x").shape
torch.Size([3, 1, 4, 2])
```

This operation can be used as a context manager too. Inside the
`with` block, you work on the unsqueezed tensordict. When the block
exits, the inverse operation ([`squeeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.squeeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.squeeze)) runs, and the entries
of the block are written back to the original tensordict. They replace
the original tensors instead of being copied into them. The original
tensordict must not be locked. If the block raises an exception,
nothing is written back.

```
>>> td = TensorDict({
... 'x': torch.arange(24).reshape(3, 4, 2),
... }, batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> with td.unsqueeze(-2) as tds:
... _ = tds.set("y", torch.zeros(3, 1, 4))
>>> assert td.get("y").shape == (3, 4)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

[Changing the shape of a TensorDict](../../tutorials/tensordict_shapes.html)

Changing the shape of a TensorDict

# TensorDictBase.update

TensorDictBase.update(*input_dict_or_td: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *clone: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *keys_to_update: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *is_leaf: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Type)], [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *update_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *ignore_lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Writes the entries of a dictionary or another tensordict into the tensordict, and returns `self`.

Each entry is written as with [`set()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set): by reference, unless
`clone=True`. Nested tensordicts are merged, not replaced: the
entries of the tensordict that the input does not have are kept.
Keyword arguments are top-level entries: `td.update(a=x)` writes
`x` at `"a"`, and wins over an entry `"a"` of the input. A key
named like an argument of `update` (`clone`, `inplace`...) must
go in the input dictionary.

Warning

`update` is not atomic. If one entry fails (for
example, its shape does not match the batch size), the entries
before it are already written. Do not catch the exception and
continue with the same tensordict. Update a copy, or make sure
that the input is valid first.

Parameters:

- **input_dict_or_td** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - the entries to
write. A dictionary can be nested and have tuple keys. If
`None`, only the keyword arguments are written. Defaults to
`None`.
- **clone** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, clones the tensors of the
input before writing them. Defaults to `False`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a value whose key exists is
copied into the existing tensor, which keeps its storage. A
new key is added. Defaults to `False`. See
[In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).

Keyword Arguments:

- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.
- **keys_to_update** (*sequence**of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - if passed, only
these keys are written, without the cost of
`td.update(other.select(*keys_to_update))`. Defaults to
`None`, which writes every entry.
- **is_leaf** (*Callable**[**[*[*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*]**,*[*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*]**,**optional*) - tells which types of
values are written whole. The other values are merged key by
key. Defaults to `None`, which is
[`is_leaf_nontensor()`](tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor.html#tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor). See also
[`default_is_leaf()`](tensordict.default_is_leaf.html#tensordict.default_is_leaf).
- **update_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch
size of the tensordict to that of the input when they differ.
A lazy stack is then refilled with copies of the tensordicts of
the input. It needs `keys_to_update=None` and
`inplace=False`, and the keys of the tensordict must all be in
the input. A batch size that is a prefix of the input's (`[]`
for an input of batch size `[2]`) is kept, with a
[`FutureWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#FutureWarning): starting with TensorDict 0.17, the
default will change to replacing it as well. A batch size whose
leading dims are those of the input (`[2, 3]` for `[2]`) is
kept. Defaults to `False`.
- **ignore_lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - deprecated: `True` warns, and the
argument will be removed in TensorDict 0.17. On a locked
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), it does not lift the lock: a
new or replaced entry still raises `RuntimeError`
([#2260](https://github.com/pytorch/tensordict/issues/2260)).
Use `inplace=True`, or unlock the tensordict first, as in
`with td.unlock_(): td.update(other)`. Defaults to `False`.
- ****kwargs** - entries to write at the top level, by key.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the tensordict is locked (see [Locking and temporary changes](../../concepts/keys.html#keys-locking))
 and the call adds or replaces an entry, or if the leading
 dimensions of a value do not match the batch size.

Note

With `update_batch_size=True`, a lazy stack of N
tensordicts updated with a lazy stack of M > N tensordicts along
the stack dimension gets copies of the M - N extra tensordicts
appended, so `update` can grow a lazy stack. Without it, the
extra tensordicts are left out.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> other = TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3), b=torch.ones(3, 4), batch_size=[3])
>>> td = td.update(other)
>>> td["a"] is other["a"] # written by reference unless clone=True
True
>>> td = td.update(c=torch.zeros(3)) # keyword form
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'c']
```

Nested tensordicts are merged:

```
>>> td = td.update({"nested": {"x": torch.zeros(3)}})
>>> td = td.update({"nested": {"y": torch.ones(3)}})
>>> sorted(td["nested"].keys())
['x', 'y']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.update

TensorDictBase.update_(*input_dict_or_td: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *clone: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *keys_to_update: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Copies the entries of a dictionary or tensordict into the existing entries, and returns `self`.

Each value is copied into the existing tensor, which keeps its
storage, as with [`set_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_). `update_` therefore works on a
locked tensordict. Every key of the input must exist in the tensordict.
Keyword arguments are top-level entries, and win over an entry of the
input with the same key. A key named like an argument of `update_`
must go in the input dictionary. See [In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).

On a shared or memory-mapped tensordict, a non-tensor value that its
shared buffer cannot store (for example `None`, or an int where a
string is shared) is skipped, with a [`UserWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#UserWarning) that names
its key.

Parameters:

- **input_dict_or_td** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - the entries to
copy. If `None`, only the keyword arguments are copied.
Defaults to `None`.
- **clone** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, clones the tensors of the
input before copying them. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.
- **keys_to_update** (*sequence**of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - if passed, only
these keys are copied, without the cost of
`td.update_(other.select(*keys_to_update))`. Defaults to
`None`, which copies every entry.
- ****kwargs** - entries to copy at the top level, by key.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

- [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if a key of the input is missing from the tensordict.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if a value does not fit the shape of its entry.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> a = torch.ones(3)
>>> td = TensorDict(a=a, b=torch.ones(3, 4), batch_size=[3])
>>> _ = td.update_(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b=torch.zeros(3, 4), batch_size=[3]))
>>> td["a"] is a, a.sum()
(True, tensor(0.))
>>> _ = td.update_(a=torch.ones(3)) # keyword form
>>> a.sum()
tensor(3.)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.update_at

TensorDictBase.update_at_(*input_dict_or_td: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | T*, *idx: [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [slice](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#slice) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), ...]*, *clone: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *keys_to_update: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Copies the entries of a dictionary or tensordict into the existing entries at `idx`.

`td.update_at_(other, idx)` writes each entry as
`td.set_at_(key, other[key], idx)`: the existing tensors keep their
storage, so `update_at_` works on a locked tensordict. Every key of
the input must exist in the tensordict. Tensor and non-tensor leaves
are supported. For a faster copy of tensors only, use
[`copy_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.copy_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.copy_at_).

Parameters:

- **input_dict_or_td** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the entries to copy.
Their leading dimensions are those of `td[idx]`.
- **idx** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,*[*slice*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#slice)*,*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) - the index to write at,
along the batch dimensions.
- **clone** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, clones the tensors of the
input before copying them. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, copies between devices
can run asynchronously with respect to the host. Defaults to
`False`.
- **keys_to_update** (*sequence**of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - if passed, only
these keys are copied. Defaults to `None`, which copies every
entry.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

- [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if a key of the input is missing from the tensordict.
- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if a value does not fit the shape of its entry.

Deprecated since version 0.15: The keyword names `index` (for `idx`) and `input_dict` (for
`input_dict_or_td`) warn, and will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3, 4, 5), b=torch.zeros(3, 4, 10), batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> other = TensorDict(a=torch.ones(1, 4, 5), b=torch.ones(1, 4, 10), batch_size=[1, 4])
>>> _ = td.update_at_(other, slice(1, 2))
>>> td["a"].sum(dim=(1, 2))
tensor([ 0., 20., 0.])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.values

TensorDictBase.values(*include_nested: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *leaves_only: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *is_leaf=None*, ***, *sort: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [Iterator](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)]

Returns a generator of the values of the tensordict.

By default, only the top-level values are returned, and a nested
tensordict is returned as one value. Non-tensor data comes as a
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData), not as the object that
`td[key]` returns. See [Keys, nested keys, and locking](../../concepts/keys.html#keys) for nested keys and leaves.

Parameters:

- **include_nested** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the entries of the
nested tensordicts are also returned, under nested keys (tuples
of strings). Defaults to `False`.
- **leaves_only** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, only the leaves are
returned, and nested tensordicts are skipped. Defaults to
`False`.
- **is_leaf** (*Callable**,**optional*) - a function that takes a class and
returns `True` if values of that class count as leaves. It
filters the result only when `leaves_only=True`. It does not
stop the recursion: with `include_nested=True`, a nested
tensordict is still searched even if `is_leaf` returns
`True` for it. Defaults to `None`, which uses
[`default_is_leaf()`](tensordict.default_is_leaf.html#tensordict.default_is_leaf): tensordicts,
tensorclasses and non-tensor data are not leaves. Pass
[`is_leaf_nontensor()`](tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor.html#tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor) to count non-tensor data
as leaves.

Keyword Arguments:

**sort** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the keys are sorted. Nested keys
are sorted by their joined name: `("a", "key")` sorts as
`"a.key"`. Sorting takes extra time on large tensordicts.
Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... a=torch.zeros(2),
... nested=TensorDict(b=torch.ones(2, 3), batch_size=[2]),
... batch_size=[2],
... )
>>> [type(value).__name__ for value in td.values()]
['Tensor', 'TensorDict']
>>> [value.shape for value in td.values(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True)]
[torch.Size([2]), torch.Size([2, 3])]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).
