# from_dataclass

tensordict.from_dataclass(*obj: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, ***, *dest_cls: [Type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Type) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *frozen: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *autocast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *nocast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *shadow: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *tensor_only: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

Converts a dataclass instance to a tensorclass instance, or a dataclass type to a tensorclass type.

Use it to move code from `@dataclass` to a tensorclass. For a type,
the result is a new tensorclass named `<name>_tc` with the same fields,
or the type itself, made a tensorclass, if `inplace=True`. A type that
is already a tensorclass is returned as it is. For an instance, the
result is an instance of a new `<name>_tc` tensorclass, or of
`dest_cls`, built from the fields of `obj`.

[`TensorDict.from_dataclass`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dataclass.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dataclass)
converts a dataclass instance to a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)
instead.

Parameters:

**obj** (*Any*) - the dataclass instance or type to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dest_cls** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*,**optional*) - for an instance, the tensorclass to build.
When it is given, the class flags below have no effect. Not used
for a type. Defaults to `None`, which creates a new tensorclass.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - for an instance, if `True`, sets
the batch size to the largest leading shape that all the entries
share. Exclusive with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Defaults to `None`, which allows
as many as the entries share.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - for an instance, the
batch size of the result: the leading dimensions that all its
entries share. Defaults to `None`, which gives an empty batch
size.
- **frozen** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the `frozen` class flag: if `True`,
assigning a field raises `dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **autocast** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the `autocast` class flag: if `True`, a
value set to a field is converted to the annotated type. Defaults
to `False`.
- **nocast** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the `nocast` class flag: if `True`,
tensor-compatible values (`int`, `float`, `np.ndarray`) are
stored as they are, not cast to tensors. Defaults to `False`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - for a type, if `True`, turns `obj`
itself into a tensorclass instead of creating a new class. Not
used for an instance. Defaults to `False`.
- **shadow** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the `shadow` class flag: if `True`,
fields can have the name of a tensorclass member (`batch_size`,
`sum`, ...) and hide it. Defaults to `False`.
- **tensor_only** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the `tensor_only` class flag: if
`True`, every field annotation must be a tensor type or a tensor
collection, and reading a field is faster. Defaults to `False`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - for an instance, the
device of the result. Defaults to `None`, which leaves each leaf
where it is.

The class flags are described in [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass). Pass
at most one of `autocast`, `nocast` and `tensor_only`, as for
[`tensorclass()`](tensordict.tensorclass.html#tensordict.tensorclass). When the flags are applied (not with
`dest_cls`, and not for a type that is already a tensorclass),
`autocast` with `nocast`, or, for a type, `tensor_only` with either
of them, emits a `FutureWarning` today. Starting with TensorDict 0.17,
the default will change to raising the `TypeError` that
[`tensorclass()`](tensordict.tensorclass.html#tensordict.tensorclass) raises.

Returns:

A tensorclass type if `obj` is a type, a tensorclass instance
otherwise.

Raises:

[**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - if `obj` is not a dataclass instance or type, or if, for
 an instance, `tensor_only` is combined with `autocast` or
 `nocast`, or `auto_batch_size=True` with `batch_size`.

Examples

```
>>> from dataclasses import dataclass
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import from_dataclass
>>>
>>> @dataclass
... class X:
... a: int
... b: torch.Tensor
...
>>> x = X(0, 0)
>>> x2 = from_dataclass(x)
>>> print(x2)
X_tc(
 a=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 b=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> X2 = from_dataclass(X, autocast=True)
>>> print(X2(a=0, b=0))
X_tc(
 a=NonTensorData(data=0, batch_size=torch.Size([]), device=None),
 b=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

---

# from_dict

tensordict.from_dict(*d*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Converts a dictionary to a tensordict, recursively.

Nested dicts become nested tensordicts, and the values are converted with
[`from_any()`](tensordict.from_any.html#tensordict.from_any). Unlike the [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) constructor,
it can compute the batch size. See
[`TensorDict.from_dict`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict).

Parameters:

**d** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the dictionary to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share, for the
result and for each nested tensordict. Defaults to `None`,
which behaves like `False` unless `batch_dims` is given.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Turns on `auto_batch_size` when that
is `None`. Exclusive with `batch_size`. Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. `None` leaves
each leaf where it is, and the result has no device. Defaults to
`None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Takes precedence over `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`,
an empty batch size unless it is computed.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the batch dimensions, one
per dimension. Used only with `batch_size`: when the batch size
is empty or computed, the names are dropped. Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if both `batch_size` and `batch_dims` are given.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import from_dict
>>> input_dict = {"a": torch.zeros(3, 4), "b": {"c": torch.zeros(3, 4, 5)}}
>>> from_dict(input_dict).batch_size
torch.Size([])
>>> td = from_dict(input_dict, auto_batch_size=True)
>>> td.batch_size, td["b"].batch_size
(torch.Size([3, 4]), torch.Size([3, 4, 5]))
>>> from_dict(input_dict, batch_dims=1).batch_size
torch.Size([3])
>>> from_dict(input_dict, batch_size=[3], names=["n"]).names
['n']
```

---

# from_h5

tensordict.from_h5(*h5_file*, ***, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'r'*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_tensor_as_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Opens an HDF5 file as a [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict).

See [`TensorDictBase.from_h5`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_h5.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_h5).

Parameters:

**h5_file** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**path*) - the path to the HDF5 file.

Keyword Arguments:

- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - how the file is opened, as in
`h5py.File`: `"r"` (read only), `"r+"` (read and
write), and so on. Defaults to `"r"`.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, which
gives each nested tensordict the largest batch size that its
entries share.
- **non_tensor_as_stack** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a non-tensor
dataset that tensordict did not write reads as a
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) of its rows when its leading
dimensions equal the batch size. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) backed by the file.

# from_json

tensordict.from_json(*path*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *lines: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Reads a JSON file of records into a tensordict, with one entry per field.

The file holds an array of records, or one record per line with
`lines=True`. See [`TensorDictBase.from_json`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_json.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_json).

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the path of the JSON file.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. `None` leaves
each leaf where it is, and the result has no device. Defaults to
`None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, which
gives `[num_rows]`.
- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if given, splits the column names on it
to build nested entries: with `separator="."`, the column
`"obs.x"` becomes the entry `("obs", "x")`. Defaults to
`None`.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - if given, casts the numeric and
boolean columns to it. Defaults to `None`.
- **lines** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reads the file as JSON Lines,
one record per line. Defaults to `False`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to `pandas.read_json()`. Ignored without pandas.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

# from_module

tensordict.from_module(*module*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Returns a locked tensordict that holds the parameters and buffers of a module.

Same as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module), except for the default
of `lock`: this function locks the result by default, and the method
does not. The entries are the parameters and buffers of the
module themselves, not copies. Submodules become nested tensordicts.

Parameters:

- **module** ([*Module*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a
`TensorDictParams` instance is returned,
which can be used to store parameters within a
[`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `True`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict from the
module is used and unflattened into a TensorDict with the tree
structure of the model. Use it when the module has state-dict
hooks. Defaults to `False`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, submodules without
parameters or buffers (`nn.ReLU`, for example) get no entry.
If `False`, they get an empty tensordict. Defaults to
`True`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), or a
`TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from torch import nn
>>> import tensordict
>>> module = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 4), nn.ReLU())
>>> params = tensordict.from_module(module)
>>> params["0", "weight"] is module[0].weight
True
>>> params.is_locked
True
```

---

# from_modules

tensordict.from_modules(**modules*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lazy_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *expand_identical: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Stacks the parameters and buffers of several modules in one tensordict.

The result has one batch dimension, with one element per module. Use it to
run an ensemble of modules that have the same structure with
[`torch.vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap) and [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module). Same
as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_modules()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_modules.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_modules): see that page for the
difference between a dense and a lazy result, and for a full ensemble
example.

Parameters:

***modules** ([*Module*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)) - the modules to get the parameters from.

Keyword Arguments:

- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a
`TensorDictParams` instance is returned.
Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `True`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict of each
module is used. Defaults to `False`.
- **lazy_stack** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the parameters are stacked
in a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) that keeps the
original parameters. If `False`, they are stacked into new
parameters. Exclusive with `as_module`. Defaults to `False`.
- **expand_identical** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a parameter that is
the same object in every module is expanded instead of stacked.
Ignored when `lazy_stack=True`. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) with batch size `[len(modules)]`,
a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) if `lazy_stack=True`,
or a `TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> import tensordict
>>> modules = [nn.Linear(3, 4) for _ in range(2)]
>>> params = tensordict.from_modules(*modules)
>>> params.batch_size
torch.Size([2])
>>> params["weight"].shape
torch.Size([2, 4, 3])
```

---

# from_namedtuple

tensordict.from_namedtuple(*named_tuple*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Converts a named tuple to a tensordict whose keys are its field names.

Each field value is converted with [`from_any()`](tensordict.from_any.html#tensordict.from_any). See
[`TensorDictBase.from_namedtuple`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_namedtuple.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_namedtuple).

Parameters:

**named_tuple** (*NamedTuple*) - the named tuple to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. `None` leaves
each leaf where it is, and the result has no device. Defaults to
`None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, an empty
batch size.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import from_namedtuple
>>> td = from_namedtuple(torch.tensor([[2, 0, 1]]).max(dim=1))
>>> td["values"], td["indices"]
(tensor([2]), tensor([0]))
```

# from_pandas

tensordict.from_pandas(*dataframe*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Converts a pandas DataFrame to a tensordict, with one entry per column.

See [`TensorDictBase.from_pandas`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pandas.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pandas) for how each column type is
converted.

Parameters:

**dataframe** (*pd.DataFrame*) - the DataFrame to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. `None` leaves
each leaf where it is, and the result has no device. Defaults to
`None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, which
gives `[num_rows]`.
- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if given, splits the column names on it
to build nested entries: with `separator="."`, the column
`"obs.x"` becomes the entry `("obs", "x")`. Defaults to
`None`.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - if given, casts the numeric and
boolean columns to it. Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from tensordict import from_pandas
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({"obs.x": [1.0, 2.0], "obs.y": [3.0, 4.0], "done": [False, True]})
>>> td = from_pandas(df, separator=".")
>>> td["obs", "x"], td.batch_size
(tensor([1., 2.], dtype=torch.float64), torch.Size([2]))
```

tensordict.from_parquet(*path*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *columns: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Parameters:

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. `None` leaves
each leaf where it is, and the result has no device. Defaults to
`None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, which
gives `[num_rows]`.
- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - if given, splits the column names on it
to build nested entries: with `separator="."`, the column
`"obs.x"` becomes the entry `("obs", "x")`. Defaults to

`None`, which reads all the columns.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the Parquet reader.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

# from_pytree

tensordict.from_pytree(*pytree*, ***, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Converts a pytree (nested lists, tuples and dicts of tensors) to a tensordict.

Lists, tuples, named tuples and dicts become nested tensordicts, and
non-tensor entries record their types, so
[`to_pytree()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree) can rebuild the pytree. Same
as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_pytree()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pytree.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pytree): see that page for the
details.

Parameters:

**pytree** (*Any*) - the pytree to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result. Defaults to `None`, which gives `[]` unless
`auto_batch_size` is `True`.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the leaves share. Defaults to
`False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> td = tensordict.from_pytree(
... {"a": torch.zeros(3), "b": (torch.ones(3), torch.ones(3, 2))},
... auto_batch_size=True,
... )
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([3])
>>> td["b", "1"].shape
torch.Size([3, 2])
>>> type(td.to_pytree()["b"]).__name__
'tuple'
```

# from_struct_array

tensordict.from_struct_array(*struct_array*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Converts a NumPy structured array to a tensordict, with one entry per field.

The tensors share memory with the array. See
[`TensorDictBase.from_struct_array`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array).

Parameters:

**struct_array** (*np.ndarray*) - the structured array to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. `None` leaves
each leaf where it is, and the result has no device. Defaults to
`None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, which
uses the shape of the array.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from tensordict import from_struct_array
>>> x = np.array(
... [("Rex", 9, 81.0), ("Fido", 3, 27.0)],
... dtype=[("name", "U10"), ("age", "i4"), ("weight", "f4")],
... )
>>> td = from_struct_array(x)
>>> td.batch_size, td["age"]
(torch.Size([2]), tensor([9, 3], dtype=torch.int32))
>>> x["age"] += 1 # the tensordict shares memory with the array
>>> td["age"]
tensor([10, 4], dtype=torch.int32)
>>> bool((td.to_struct_array() == x).all())
True
```

# from_tuple

tensordict.from_tuple(*obj*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Converts a tuple to a tensordict with the keys `"0"`, `"1"`, ...

Each element is converted with [`from_any()`](tensordict.from_any.html#tensordict.from_any). See
[`TensorDictBase.from_tuple`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_tuple.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_tuple).

Parameters:

**obj** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) - the tuple to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. `None` leaves
each leaf where it is, and the result has no device. Defaults to
`None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, an empty
batch size.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import from_tuple
>>> td = from_tuple((torch.zeros(3, 4), torch.ones(3)), auto_batch_size=True)
>>> list(td.keys()), td.batch_size
(['0', '1'], torch.Size([3]))
```

# from_zarr

tensordict.from_zarr(*zarr_file*, ***, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'r'*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_tensor_as_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Opens a zarr store as a [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict).

Requires `zarr>=3.0`. See
[`TensorDictBase.from_zarr`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_zarr.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_zarr).

Parameters:

**zarr_file** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**path**or**zarr store*) - the path to the zarr store (a
directory), or a `zarr.abc.store.Store` instance.

Keyword Arguments:

- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - how the store is opened: `"r"` (read only),
`"r+"` (read and write), and so on. Defaults to `"r"`.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, sets the batch size to
the largest leading shape that all the entries share. Exclusive
with `batch_size`. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - with `auto_batch_size`, the maximum
number of batch dimensions. Ignored without `auto_batch_size`.
Defaults to `None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Exclusive with `auto_batch_size`. Defaults to `None`, which
reads the batch size that [`to_zarr()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_zarr.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_zarr)
stored, or computes it for a store written by another tool.
- **non_tensor_as_stack** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a non-tensor
array that tensordict did not write reads as a
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) of its rows when its leading
dimensions equal the batch size. Defaults to `False`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - whether to decode pickled non-tensor
values. `False` rejects them. `True` permits them, only for
data you trust. `None` permits them with a `FutureWarning`.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
`allow_pickle=False`. Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) backed by the store.

# fromkeys

tensordict.fromkeys(*keys: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*, *value: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = 0*)

Creates a tensordict with the same value for every key, like [`dict.fromkeys()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict.fromkeys).

Same as [`tensordict.TensorDict.fromkeys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.fromkeys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.fromkeys), and as [`dict.fromkeys()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict.fromkeys)
for a dict. The batch size of the result is `[]`.

Parameters:

- **keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys of the new tensordict. A tuple of
strings creates a nested entry.
- **value** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**number**or**Any**,**optional*) - the value of every
entry. Defaults to `0`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import tensordict
>>> td = tensordict.fromkeys(["a", ("b", "c")], 1)
>>> td["b", "c"]
tensor(1)
```

# get_defaults_to_none

tensordict.get_defaults_to_none(*set_to_none: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Returns whether [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) returns `None` for a missing key.

`False` means that `get` raises a `KeyError` when no default is
passed. See [`set_get_defaults_to_none()`](tensordict.set_get_defaults_to_none.html#tensordict.set_get_defaults_to_none).

Deprecated since version 0.15: Since v0.7, [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) returns `None` for a
missing key by default. This function is deprecated and will be removed in
TensorDict 0.17. Use `td[key]` to raise a `KeyError` for a missing key.

Parameters:

**set_to_none** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - ignored. Defaults to `True`.

# is_bool

tensordict.is_bool(**args*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether the last argument is a boolean tensor.

The predicate tests its last argument only, so it can be passed as
`fn(value)` and as `fn(key, value)`: see [`is_inexact()`](tensordict.is_inexact.html#tensordict.is_inexact).

Parameters:

***args** - the value to test is the last one. A key may come before it.

Returns:

`True` if the dtype of the value is `torch.bool`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import is_bool
>>> is_bool(torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.bool)), is_bool("mask", torch.zeros(3))
(True, False)
```

# is_inexact

tensordict.is_inexact(**args*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether the last argument is a floating-point or complex tensor.

The predicate tests its last argument only, so it works both as
`fn(value)`, for example inside a function given to
[`apply()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply), and as `fn(key, value)`, for
example as the `cast_filter` of [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to).

Parameters:

***args** - the value to test is the last one. A key may come before it.

Returns:

`True` if the dtype of the value is a floating-point or complex dtype.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, is_inexact
>>> is_inexact(torch.zeros(3)), is_inexact("a", torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.long))
(True, False)
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), i=torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.long))
>>> td_bf16 = td.bfloat16(cast_filter=is_inexact)
>>> td_bf16["x"].dtype, td_bf16["i"].dtype
(torch.bfloat16, torch.int64)
```

# is_leaf_nontensor

tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor(*cls: [Type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Type)*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Returns `True` if a type is a tensor or non-tensor data.

Pass it as `is_leaf` to [`keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.keys) and the
methods that walk the nested entries, to list the non-tensor entries
([`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData), [`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack))
with the tensors. A [`UnbatchedTensor`](tensordict.UnbatchedTensor.html#tensordict.UnbatchedTensor) is a leaf too.
Other tensordicts and tensorclasses are not leaves, and nor is a type that
is neither a tensor nor a tensor collection. See [Non-tensor data and unbatched entries](../../concepts/non_tensor.html#non-tensor-data).

Parameters:

**cls** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)) - the type of an entry, as returned by
[`entry_class()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.entry_class.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.entry_class).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, NonTensorData, is_leaf_nontensor
>>> is_leaf_nontensor(torch.Tensor), is_leaf_nontensor(NonTensorData), is_leaf_nontensor(TensorDict)
(True, True, False)
>>> td = TensorDict(a={}, b="a string!", c=torch.zeros(()))
>>> list(td.keys(leaves_only=True, is_leaf=is_leaf_nontensor))
['b', 'c']
```

See also

[`default_is_leaf()`](tensordict.default_is_leaf.html#tensordict.default_is_leaf).

# is_memmap_archive

tensordict.is_memmap_archive(*path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether `path` is a memory-mapped tensordict archive.

An archive is a zip file with a top-level `meta.json` entry, as
written by [`pack_memmap()`](tensordict.pack_memmap.html#tensordict.pack_memmap) or by
[`save()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.save.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.save) with a `".tdz"` path. A
directory, a missing path or another file gives `False`.

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the path to check.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, is_memmap_archive
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as path:
... _ = td.save(Path(path) / "td.tdz")
... _ = td.save(Path(path) / "td")
... print(is_memmap_archive(Path(path) / "td.tdz"), is_memmap_archive(Path(path) / "td"))
True False
```

# is_non_tensor

tensordict.is_non_tensor(*data*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Returns `True` if `data` is non-tensor data or a stack of non-tensor data.

Parameters:

**data** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check, for example a value read from a
tensordict with [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get).

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import NonTensorData, TensorDict, is_non_tensor
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(2), name=NonTensorData("a"))

(True, False)
>>> td["name"]
'a'
```

# is_tensor_collection

tensordict.is_tensor_collection(*datatype: [type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type) | [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Returns `True` if an object or a type is a tensordict or a tensorclass.

A tensor, a dict and any other object return `False`.

Parameters:

**datatype** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*or*[*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the type to check, or an object whose type
is checked.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, TensorDictBase, is_tensor_collection, tensorclass
>>> is_tensor_collection(TensorDictBase)
True
>>> is_tensor_collection(TensorDict())
True
>>> @tensorclass
... class MyClass:
... pass
...
>>> is_tensor_collection(MyClass)
True
>>> is_tensor_collection(MyClass(batch_size=[]))
True
>>> is_tensor_collection(torch.zeros(3)), is_tensor_collection({"a": 0})
(False, False)
```

# lazy_stack

tensordict.lazy_stack(*input: Sequence['T']*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*, ***kwargs*) → T

Stacks tensordicts into a lazy stack ([`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict)).

The result keeps each input as a separate tensordict, so the inputs can
have different keys, entry shapes and batch sizes. Use it for data whose
size changes from one sample to the next. [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking) compares this
function with [`stack()`](tensordict.stack.html#tensordict.stack) and
[`maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.maybe_dense_stack.html#tensordict.maybe_dense_stack). Same as
[`tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.lazy_stack()`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.lazy_stack), which takes the same
arguments and documents the ones for lists of tensors.

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to stack. It must not be empty. The batch sizes must
have the same number of dimensions. If a dimension differs
between inputs, it is `-1` in the stacked batch size.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the new dimension. Defaults to `0`. A `dim`
below `-batch_dims - 1` warns and wraps around once more (and
raises if it is still out of range).
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to raising
an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a lazy stack to write the result
into. Its batch size must be the stacked batch size. Defaults to
`None`.
- **stack_dim_name** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the name of the stack dimension.
Defaults to `None`.
- **strict_shape** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch sizes of the
inputs must be equal, or a `RuntimeError` is raised. Defaults
to `False`.

Returns:

A [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict). Tensorclass inputs give
an instance of their class that holds a lazy stack.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = tensordict.lazy_stack(
... [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]),
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(4), batch_size=[4])]
... )
>>> type(td).__name__
'LazyStackedTensorDict'
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([2, -1])
>>> td[1]["a"].shape
torch.Size([4])
```

[Building tensordicts from streams](../../tutorials/streamed_tensordict.html)

![](../../_images/sphx_glr_tensordict_shapes_thumb.png)

# load

tensordict.load(*prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *out: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *subpath: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Loads a tensordict that [`save()`](tensordict.save.html#tensordict.save) wrote.

Same as [`load_memmap()`](tensordict.load_memmap.html#tensordict.load_memmap), which takes the same arguments.
See [`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap) for every argument, and
[Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving) for the ways to save and load a tensordict.

Parameters:

- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the directory, or the `.tdz` archive file,
that holds the saved tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - if given, the data is
cast to that device. With `"meta"`, no file is read. Defaults
to `None`.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the cast to `device`
is not followed by a synchronization. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to load the data into.
Defaults to `None`.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reads the percent-encoded
file names that [`save()`](tensordict.save.html#tensordict.save) writes by default, and
falls back to the legacy names of keys that are safe file names.
If `False`, reads the legacy layout only. Defaults to `True`.
- **subpath** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the nested tensordict to load,
as a nested key (`("module", "0")`) or a `"/"`-separated path
(`"module/0"`). Only that subtree is read. Defaults to
`None`, which loads the whole tensordict.
- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - `"r"` maps the files copy-on-write (in-place
writes stay in memory), `"r+"` maps them shared (in-place writes
reach the files). See [`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap)
for the default.
- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that decompress
the leaves of a compressed archive. It has no effect on other
data. Defaults to `0`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries that
were pickled are unpickled. Only load pickles from trusted
sources. If `False`, pickled entries raise a `RuntimeError`. Defaults
to `None`, which unpickles them with a `FutureWarning`.

Returns:

The saved tensordict, of the class it had when it was saved. Its
leaves are [`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.ones(3, 2)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... _ = tensordict.save(td, tmpdir)
... loaded = tensordict.load(tmpdir)
... print(loaded["b", "c"].shape)
torch.Size([3, 2])
```

---

# load_memmap

tensordict.load_memmap(*prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *out: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *subpath: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Loads a tensordict that [`memmap()`](tensordict.memmap.html#tensordict.memmap) or [`save()`](tensordict.save.html#tensordict.save) wrote.

Same as [`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load), and as
[`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap), which holds the full text of
every argument. See [Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving) for the ways to save and load a
tensordict.

Parameters:

- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the directory, or the `.tdz` archive file,
that holds the saved tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - if given, the data is
cast to that device. With `"meta"`, no file is read. Defaults
to `None`.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the cast to `device`
is not followed by a synchronization. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to load the data into.
Defaults to `None`.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, reads the percent-encoded
file names that [`save()`](tensordict.save.html#tensordict.save) writes by default, and
falls back to the legacy names of keys that are safe file names.
If `False`, reads the legacy layout only. Defaults to `True`.
- **subpath** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the nested tensordict to load,
as a nested key (`("module", "0")`) or a `"/"`-separated path
(`"module/0"`). Only that subtree is read. Defaults to
`None`, which loads the whole tensordict.
- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - `"r"` maps the files copy-on-write (in-place
writes stay in memory), `"r+"` maps them shared (in-place writes
reach the files). See [`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap)
for the default.
- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that decompress
the leaves of a compressed archive. It has no effect on other
data. Defaults to `0`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries that
were pickled are unpickled. Only load pickles from trusted
sources. If `False`, pickled entries raise a `RuntimeError`. Defaults
to `None`, which unpickles them with a `FutureWarning`.

Returns:

The saved tensordict, of the class it had when it was saved. Its
leaves are [`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... _ = tensordict.memmap(td, tmpdir)
... loaded = tensordict.load_memmap(tmpdir)
... print(type(loaded["a"]).__name__)
MemoryMappedTensor
```

# make_tensordict

tensordict.make_tensordict(*input_dict: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)*) → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Returns a tensordict built from a dict or from keyword arguments.

Same as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict). Nested dicts become
nested tensordicts. With `auto_batch_size=True`, each nested tensordict
gets the largest batch size that its own entries share, which starts with
the batch size of its parent.

Parameters:

- **input_dict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*or*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the entries. Its
entries are added to those of `**kwargs` and replace them on a
shared key. Defaults to `None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size
of the result: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Defaults to `None`, which gives `[]` unless
`auto_batch_size` is `True`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
result. Leaves on another device are moved to it. Defaults to
`None`, which leaves each leaf where it is.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `batch_size` is
not given, sets the batch size to the largest leading shape that
all the entries share. Defaults to `None`, which does not.
- ****kwargs** - the entries, as keyword arguments.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import make_tensordict
>>> td = make_tensordict(a=torch.zeros(3, 4), b=torch.zeros(3))
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([])
>>> td = make_tensordict(
... {"a": torch.zeros(3), "b": {"c": torch.zeros(3, 4)}}, auto_batch_size=True
... )
>>> td.batch_size, td["b"].batch_size
(torch.Size([3]), torch.Size([3, 4]))
```

---

# maybe_dense_stack

tensordict.maybe_dense_stack(*input: Sequence['T']*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*, ***kwargs*) → T

Stacks tensordicts densely if possible, or into a lazy stack otherwise.

Use it when the inputs usually match, but can differ. If every input has
the same keys, entry shapes and batch size, the result is the dense
stack that [`stack()`](tensordict.stack.html#tensordict.stack) returns. Otherwise, the result is the
lazy stack that [`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) returns. [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)
compares these functions. Same as
[`tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.maybe_dense_stack).

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to stack.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the new dimension. Defaults to `0`. A `dim` outside
`[-batch_dims - 1, batch_dims]` warns, and is used on the dimensions
of the leaves. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will
change to raising an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into. Defaults to `None`.
- **strict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - used only with `out`. If `True`, `out`
must have the same keys as the inputs. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (or the tensorclass of the inputs)
if the inputs can be stacked densely, a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) otherwise.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> same = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3))]
>>> type(tensordict.maybe_dense_stack(same)).__name__
'TensorDict'
>>> different = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.ones(4))]
>>> type(tensordict.maybe_dense_stack(different)).__name__
'LazyStackedTensorDict'
```

---

# memmap

tensordict.memmap(*data: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *copy_existing: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *return_early: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *share_non_tensor: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *existsok: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *archive: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *compression: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Writes every leaf to a memory-mapped file and returns a new tensordict of them.

Same as [`save()`](tensordict.save.html#tensordict.save), and as
[`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap), which holds the full text of
every argument. Use it to share a tensordict between processes without
copies, or to keep data that is larger than RAM on disk. To convert the
tensordict in place, use [`memmap_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap_).
See [Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving) and [Load data and share it between processes](../../data_loading.html#data-loading).

Parameters:

- **data** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instance*) - the tensordict to write.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the directory to write to, or a file name that
ends with `".tdz"`. Defaults to `None`, which writes the
tensors to anonymous shared memory and saves nothing to disk.
- **copy_existing** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, an entry that is already
memory-mapped to a file outside `prefix` raises an error. If
`True`, it is copied. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that write the
files. Defaults to `0`.
- **return_early** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `num_threads > 1`,
returns a [`TensorDictFuture`](tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture.html#tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture) at once, while
the threads write the files. Defaults to `False`.
- **share_non_tensor** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries are
shared between the processes of a node. Defaults to `False`.
- **existsok** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, a tensor file that already
exists under `prefix` raises an error. Defaults to `True`.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, keys that hold path
separators or special characters are encoded in the file names.
Defaults to `True`.
- **archive** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `prefix` is a file and the
tensordict is written as a single zip archive that
[`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load) can memory-map. If `None`, an archive
is written when `prefix` ends with `".tdz"`. Defaults to
`None`.
- **compression** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the compression of the archive
entries: `"stored"`, `"deflate"`, `"bzip2"`, `"lzma"` or a
[`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile) constant. Only valid for an archive. Defaults to
`None`, which stores them uncompressed. Only uncompressed
entries load without a copy.

Returns:

A new, locked tensordict whose leaves are
[`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> td_memmap = tensordict.memmap(td)
>>> type(td_memmap["a"]).__name__
'MemoryMappedTensor'
>>> td_memmap.is_locked
True
```

# merge_tensordicts

tensordict.merge_tensordicts(**tensordicts: T*, *callback_exist: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → T

Merges the entries of several tensordicts into a new tensordict.

The result has the batch size of the first tensordict and every key of
every input. The values are not copied. For a key that several inputs
hold, the value comes from the first input that holds it, unless
`callback_exist` combines them.

Parameters:

***tensordicts** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordicts to merge, at least two,
or a `RuntimeError` is raised.

Keyword Arguments:

**callback_exist** (*Callable**or*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*of**NestedKey to Callable**,**optional*) - a function called as `callback_exist(*values)` for a leaf that
every input holds; its result becomes the value of the leaf. A
dict gives a function per key (`"a"` or `("a", "b")`), and
the keys it lacks take the first value. Leaves that only some
inputs hold, and non-tensor entries, always take the first value.
Defaults to `None`, which takes the first value for every key.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import merge_tensordicts, TensorDict
>>> td0 = TensorDict({"a": {"b0": 0}, "common": 0})
>>> td1 = TensorDict({"a": {"b1": 1}, "f": 1, "common": 1})
>>> td2 = TensorDict({"a": {"b2": 2}, "common": 2})
>>> td = merge_tensordicts(td0, td1, td2)
>>> list(td.keys(include_nested=True, leaves_only=True, sort=True))
[('a', 'b0'), ('a', 'b1'), ('a', 'b2'), 'common', 'f']
>>> td["common"]
tensor(0)
>>> td = merge_tensordicts(td0, td1, td2, callback_exist=lambda *v: torch.stack(v))
>>> td["common"]
tensor([0, 1, 2])
```
