```
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

build_dist_from_params(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution)

Builds the distribution of the last probabilistic module from parameters, without running the other modules.

The method calls [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.get_dist()`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.get_dist) of the
last [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) in the
sequence, nested sequences included. See the example of
`get_dist_params()`.

Parameters:

**tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - a tensordict with the distribution
parameters at the `in_keys` of that module.

Returns:

A `torch.distributions.Distribution`.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the sequence has no
 [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule).

*property*default_interaction_type

The `default_interaction_type` of the last module that has one.

If no module has one, the value of
[`interaction_type()`](tensordict.nn.interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.interaction_type), which is `None` outside of a
[`set_interaction_type`](tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type) block.

*property*det_part

The modules that compute the distribution parameters.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17. Use
`get_dist_params()` to compute the distribution parameters.

*property*device*: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*

The device of the first parameter of the module, or `cpu` if it has no parameter.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17 because modules may
contain parameters and buffers on multiple devices.

*property*dist_params_keys*: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*

The keys of the distribution parameters of all the probabilistic modules, those of the last module first.

*property*dist_sample_keys*: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*

The keys of the sampled values of all the probabilistic modules, those of the last module first.

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) = None*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *_requires_sample: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Runs the modules in order, and returns the tensordict with their outputs.

If the modules before the last one already write the sampled keys of
the last module, the last module does not sample again.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - if given, the modules
run on a shallow copy of `tensordict`, and the `out_keys`
are written into `tensordict_out`, which is returned (unless
`inplace` is set). Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

****kwargs** - with `return_composite=True`, passed to the modules
that are not
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule). With
`return_composite=False`, any keyword argument raises a
`RuntimeError`.

Returns:

The tensordict that holds the outputs (see `inplace`).

get_dist(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution)

Returns the distribution that the sequence samples from, given the input `tensordict`.

If `return_composite` is `False`, this is the distribution of the
last module. The method runs the modules before it with
`get_dist_params()`, so the intermediate entries are written into
`tensordict`.

If `return_composite` is `True`, this is a
[`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) that holds
the distributions of all the probabilistic modules, at their sample
keys. The method runs the modules on a shallow copy of
`tensordict`, so the input does not get new entries. Each
probabilistic module draws a value, which the modules after it read,
so their distributions are conditional on it. Only a probabilistic
module in the last position does not draw.
See the examples of `ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential`.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input, with the entries that the
first module reads.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - used only when
`return_composite` is `False`: the tensordict where the
intermediate entries are written, instead of `tensordict`.
Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

****kwargs** - ignored when `return_composite` is `True`. When it
is `False`, any keyword argument raises a `RuntimeError`.

Returns:

A `torch.distributions.Distribution`.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if the sequence has no probabilistic module.

get_dist_params(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Runs every module except the last one, and returns the tensordict with the distribution parameters.

The modules run with the interaction type of
[`interaction_type()`](tensordict.nn.interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.interaction_type) if it is set, and otherwise
with the `default_interaction_type` of the last module that has
one, so that the probabilistic modules among them sample as in a
call to the sequence.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input, with the entries that the
first module reads.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the tensordict where
the parameters are written. If `None`, they are written into
`tensordict`, which is returned. Pass
`tensordict.copy()` to keep the input unchanged.
Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

****kwargs** - not supported: any keyword argument raises a
`RuntimeError`.

Returns:

The tensordict that holds the distribution parameters.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import (
... ProbabilisticTensorDictModule,
... ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential,
... TensorDictModule,
... )
>>> seq = ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["loc"]),
... ProbabilisticTensorDictModule(
... in_keys=["loc"], out_keys=["y"], distribution_class=torch.distributions.Normal,
... distribution_kwargs={"scale": 1.0},
... ),
... )
>>> params = seq.get_dist_params(TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(2)))
>>> sorted(params.keys())
['loc', 'x']
>>> seq.build_dist_from_params(params)
Normal(loc: torch.Size([2]), scale: torch.Size([2]))
```

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*property*is_functional*: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

Whether the wrapped module is a legacy functorch functional module.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17. It only checks
for the `FunctionalModule` classes of the legacy
`functorch.make_functional` API and has no replacement.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Returns `True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys` attribute.

[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) wraps the callables that
fail this check in a [`WrapModule`](tensordict.nn.WrapModule.html#tensordict.nn.WrapModule).

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

log_prob(*tensordict*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *dist: [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the log-probability of the sampled values in `tensordict`.

If `return_composite` is `True`, the distribution is a
[`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) and the
method returns its [`log_prob()`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.log_prob):
while [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is `False`, a
tensordict with one entry per sampled key, at the key where a call to
the sequence writes it (see `log_prob_keys`); while it is
`True`, the sum, as a tensor.

If `return_composite` is `False`, the method returns the
log-probability of the value of the last module, as
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.log_prob()`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.log_prob) does. The intermediate
entries are then written into `tensordict`, as in `get_dist()`.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input, with the sampled values.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - if given, the
distribution is computed on a copy of `tensordict`, so the
input does not get new entries. Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

**dist** (*torch.distributions.Distribution**,**optional*) - the
distribution. Defaults to `None`, which builds it with
`get_dist()`.

Returns:

A tensor, or a tensordict for a composite distribution while
[`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is `False`.
See the examples of `ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential`.

*property*log_prob_key

The log-probability key of the sequence, when `log_prob_keys` has exactly one element.

See the [log-probability key table](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#log-prob-keys).

Raises:

[**AttributeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#AttributeError) - if `log_prob_keys` does not have exactly one
 element (use `log_prob_keys`), or if
 [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) changed since a
 module was built. The error message names the inner
 `ModuleList`.

*property*log_prob_keys

The log-probability keys of all the probabilistic modules, those of the last module first.

See the [log-probability key table](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#log-prob-keys).

*property*num_samples

The leading dimensions that the probabilistic modules add to the output.

The `num_samples` of each probabilistic module, those of the last
module first, as they appear in the shape of the output. An empty
tuple if no module sets `num_samples`.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the modules write, each listed once, or those chosen with `select_out_keys()`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Undoes `select_out_keys()`: the sequence writes all its `out_keys` again, and returns `self`.

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Resets the parameters of every submodule that has a `reset_parameters` method.

Without `parameters`, the parameters of the module are reset in
place. With `parameters`, the module is left as it is: the values in
`parameters` are reset in place, as if they were loaded into the
module (see [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module)). Use this
for parameters kept outside the module, for example in a functional
call. Values that share their storage with the module parameters,
such as those of [`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module), reset
the module too.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the parameters to reset,
with the structure of
[`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module) and an empty batch
size. Defaults to `None`, which resets the parameters of the
module.

Returns:

`None` without `parameters`. Otherwise a new tensordict of
tensors that share their storage with `parameters` and require
gradients.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `parameters` has batch dimensions.

Without `parameters`, the call warns if no submodule has a
`reset_parameters` method.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 3), nn.ReLU())
>>> old_weight = net[0].weight.clone()
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> module.reset_parameters_recursive()
>>> torch.equal(old_weight, net[0].weight)
False
```

The parameters can also live outside the module:

```
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module).clone()
>>> old_params = params.clone()
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
>>> torch.equal(net[0].weight, old_params["module", "0", "weight"])
True
```

select_out_keys(**selected_out_keys*) → [TensorDictSequential](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential)

Keeps only some of the `out_keys` in the output of the sequence, and returns the sequence.

The sequence changes in place, and `reset_out_keys()` undoes the
change. The modules still compute all their outputs; the call then
writes only the selected ones, and the entries of the input, into the
output.

Parameters:

***selected_out_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys to keep. Each one must be
in `out_keys`.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if a key in `selected_out_keys` is not part of `out_keys`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule as Mod, TensorDictSequential as Seq
>>> seq = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... Mod(lambda y: y + 1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> seq.out_keys
['z']
>>> td = seq(TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(())))
>>> "y" in td
False
>>> td["z"]
tensor(2.)
>>> _ = seq.reset_out_keys()
>>> seq.out_keys
['y', 'z']
```

select_subsequence(*in_keys: [Iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out_keys: [Iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictSequential](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential)

Returns a new sequence with only the modules that can run from `in_keys` and that `out_keys` need.

Two filters are applied, in this order:

- `in_keys`: a module is kept if each of its inputs is in
`in_keys` or is written by a module kept before it. The other
modules, and those that read their outputs, are dropped.
- `out_keys`: of the modules left, a module is kept if it writes one
of `out_keys`, or an input of a module kept after it.

A nested [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) is filtered the same way. The
modules are not copied: the new sequence holds the same module
objects. Modules of a named sequence keep their names, and the new
sequence keeps `partial_tolerant` and `inplace`.

Parameters:

- **in_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the keys that the modules
can start from. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
`in_keys` of the sequence.
- **out_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the keys to compute.
Defaults to `None`, which uses the `out_keys` of the
sequence.

Returns:

A new sequence of the same type.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if no module is left.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential as Seq, TensorDictModule as Mod
>>> idn = lambda x: x
>>> module = Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["b"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["c"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["c"], out_keys=["d"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["e"]),
... )
>>> # the modules that can run from "c"
>>> module.select_subsequence(in_keys=["c"]).out_keys
['d']
>>> # the modules that "c" depends on
>>> sub = module.select_subsequence(out_keys=["c"])
>>> sub.in_keys, sub.out_keys
(['a'], ['b', 'c'])
>>> sub[0] is module[0]
True
```

Nested sequences are filtered too:

```
>>> module = Seq(
... Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["b"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["c"]),
... ),
... Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["d"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["d"], out_keys=["e"]),
... ),
... )
>>> sub = module.select_subsequence(in_keys=["b", "d"], out_keys=["e"])
>>> len(sub), sub[0].out_keys
(1, ['d', 'e'])
```

# TensorClassModuleBase

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase(**args: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*)

Bases: [`Generic`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Generic)[`InputClass`, `OutputClass`], [`ABC`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/abc.html#abc.ABC), [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)

Base class of the modules that take and return a tensorclass.

Subclass `TensorClassModuleBase[InputClass, OutputClass]`, where each
type is a [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) subclass or
[`torch.Tensor`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor), and implement `forward()`. A type checker
then knows the type of the input and output, and can report a wrong
field name. The class reads both types from the subscript: a subclass
without it has no `input_type` and `output_type`, and its
`as_td_module()` raises a `ValueError`.

When both types are tensorclasses, `as_td_module()` returns a
module that takes and returns a tensordict, for example to put the
module in a [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential). See
[TensorClass](../../tensorclass.html#tensorclass-guide).

Variables:

- **input_type** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)) - the input type, `InputClass`.
- **output_type** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)) - the output type, `OutputClass`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import TensorClass
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorClassModuleBase
>>> import torch
>>>
>>> class InputTC(TensorClass):
... a: torch.Tensor
... b: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class OutputTC(TensorClass):
... result: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class AddModule(TensorClassModuleBase[InputTC, OutputTC]):
... def forward(self, x: InputTC) -> OutputTC:
... return OutputTC(
... result=x.a + x.b,
... batch_size=x.batch_size
... )
...
>>> module = AddModule()
>>> input_tc = InputTC(a=torch.tensor([1.0]), b=torch.tensor([2.0]), batch_size=[1])
>>> module(input_tc).result
tensor([3.])
```

as_td_module() → [TensorClassModuleWrapper](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper)

Returns a [`TensorClassModuleWrapper`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper) of the module, which takes and returns a tensordict.

The wrapper is a [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase). Its
`in_keys` and `out_keys` are the fields of the input and output
classes. It returns a new TensorDict with only the output fields (see
[`TensorClassModuleWrapper`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper)).

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if `input_type` or `output_type` is not a
 tensorclass, or if the subclass did not set each of them to a
 class with the subscript.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import TensorClass
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorClassModuleBase
>>> import torch
>>>
>>> class InputTC(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class OutputTC(TensorClass):
... y: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class MyModule(TensorClassModuleBase[InputTC, OutputTC]):
... def forward(self, input: InputTC) -> OutputTC:
... return OutputTC(y=input.x * 2, batch_size=input.batch_size)
...
>>> module = MyModule()
>>> td_module = module.as_td_module()
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.ones(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> td_module(td)["y"]
tensor([2., 2., 2.])
```

*abstract*forward(*x: InputClass*) → OutputClass

Computes the output of the module. Subclasses implement it.

Parameters:

**x** (*InputClass*) - the input.

Returns:

An instance of `OutputClass`.

# TensorClassModuleWrapper

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper(*module: [TensorClassModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase)[InputTensorClass, OutputTensorClass]*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Wraps a [`TensorClassModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase) so that it takes and returns a tensordict.

The wrapper converts the input tensordict to the input class of the
module, calls the module, and converts the output tensorclass back to a
TensorDict. Its `in_keys` and `out_keys` are the fields of the input
and output classes, with nested keys for nested tensorclasses.
[`TensorClassModuleBase.as_td_module()`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.as_td_module) returns one.

The wrapper returns a new TensorDict that holds only the output fields. It
does not write into the input. In a
[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential), the modules after it cannot
read the input keys, and by default the sequence returns only the
outputs.

Parameters:

**module** ([*TensorClassModuleBase*](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase)) - the module to wrap. Its input and
output types must be tensorclasses.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import TensorClass
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorClassModuleBase
>>> import torch
>>>
>>> class InputTC(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class OutputTC(TensorClass):
... y: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class MyModule(TensorClassModuleBase[InputTC, OutputTC]):
... def forward(self, input: InputTC) -> OutputTC:
... return OutputTC(y=input.x + 1, batch_size=input.batch_size)
...
>>> module = MyModule()
>>> td_module = module.as_td_module()
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> result = td_module(td)
>>> list(result.keys())
['y']
>>> "y" in td
False
```

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) = None*, *args=None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Converts `tensordict` to the input class, calls the module, and returns its output as a TensorDict.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input tensordict. Its entries that
are not fields of the input class are ignored.
- ***args** - ignored.
- ****kwargs** - ignored.

Returns:

A new TensorDict with the fields of the output tensorclass.

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Returns `True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys` attribute.

[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) wraps the callables that
fail this check in a [`WrapModule`](tensordict.nn.WrapModule.html#tensordict.nn.WrapModule).

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the module writes to the output tensordict.

After `select_out_keys()`, only the selected keys. The full list
is in `out_keys_source`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Undoes `select_out_keys()`: the module writes all its `out_keys` again.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x, y: (x + 2, y + 2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"]
... )
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> mod.out_keys
['d']
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod.out_keys
['c', 'd']
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(())))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Resets the parameters of every submodule that has a `reset_parameters` method.

Without `parameters`, the parameters of the module are reset in
place. With `parameters`, the module is left as it is: the values in
`parameters` are reset in place, as if they were loaded into the
module (see [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module)). Use this
for parameters kept outside the module, for example in a functional
call. Values that share their storage with the module parameters,
such as those of [`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module), reset
the module too.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the parameters to reset,
with the structure of
[`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module) and an empty batch
size. Defaults to `None`, which resets the parameters of the
module.

Returns:

`None` without `parameters`. Otherwise a new tensordict of
tensors that share their storage with `parameters` and require
gradients.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `parameters` has batch dimensions.

Without `parameters`, the call warns if no submodule has a
`reset_parameters` method.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 3), nn.ReLU())
>>> old_weight = net[0].weight.clone()
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> module.reset_parameters_recursive()
>>> torch.equal(old_weight, net[0].weight)
False
```

The parameters can also live outside the module:

```
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module).clone()
>>> old_params = params.clone()
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
>>> torch.equal(net[0].weight, old_params["module", "0", "weight"])
True
```

select_out_keys(**out_keys*) → [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Keeps only some of the `out_keys` in the output of the module, and returns the module.

Use it to drop intermediate outputs, for example those of a
[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential). The module changes in
place: `out_keys` becomes the selected keys, and
`out_keys_source` keeps the full list. A call still computes all
the outputs, and then removes the ones that are not selected. It
removes nothing else, so the input entries stay in the output. When
you call the module with tensors (see [`dispatch()`](tensordict.nn.dispatch.html#tensordict.nn.dispatch)),
it returns only the selected outputs. `reset_out_keys()` undoes
the selection.

Parameters:

***out_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys to keep. Each one must be in
`out_keys`.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if a key is not in `out_keys`. The error names the
 missing keys, and is also a `RuntimeError`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x, y: (x + 2, y + 2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"]
... )
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> mod.out_keys, mod.out_keys_source
(['d'], ['c', 'd'])
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(())))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'd']
>>> mod(torch.zeros(()), torch.ones(()))
tensor(3.)
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> sorted(mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(()))).keys())
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

It works on a [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) too:

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... TensorDictModule(lambda y: y + 1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> sorted(seq(TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(()))).keys())
['x', 'z']
```

# TensorDictModule

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule(*module: Callable*, *in_keys*, *out_keys: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | List[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*, ***, *out_to_in_map: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = True*, *method: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *method_kwargs: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *strict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *get_kwargs: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Wraps a callable so that it reads its inputs from a tensordict and writes its outputs to it.

When you call the module with a tensordict, it reads the entries at
`in_keys`, passes them to `module`, and writes the results at
`out_keys`. By default it writes into the input tensordict and returns
it. You can also call it with tensors as positional or keyword arguments
(see [`dispatch()`](tensordict.nn.dispatch.html#tensordict.nn.dispatch)). It then returns the output tensors.
See [Modules: TensorDictModule and tensordict.nn](../../modules.html#modules-guide) for a guide.

Parameters:

- **module** (*Callable*) - the callable to wrap, typically a
[`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). It can return a tensor, a tuple of
tensors, or a dict or a tensordict. A dict or a tensordict that
holds all the `out_keys` is read by key, so its order does not
matter.
- **in_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, or*[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the entries that the
module reads from the input tensordict. If a list, the values are
passed as positional arguments, in this order. If a dict, the values
are passed as keyword arguments. By default, the dict maps an
argument name to a tensordict key: `in_keys={"x": "obs"}` calls
`module(x=td["obs"])`. One tensordict key can feed several
arguments. `out_to_in_map=False` reverses the direction.
- **out_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys where the outputs
of `module` are written, one key per output, in order. An output
whose key is `"_"` is not written.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out_to_in_map** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the direction of a dict `in_keys`.
`True` reads it as `{argument: tensordict_key}`, `False` as
`{tensordict_key: argument}`. Only used when `in_keys` is a
dict. If you pass it with another type of `in_keys`, the
constructor warns. Defaults to `True` for a dict `in_keys`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - 

where the module writes its outputs.

- `True`: into the input tensordict, which `forward` returns.
- `False`: into a new [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) that holds only
the outputs, with an empty batch size and no device, whatever
the type of the input.
- `"empty"`: into `tensordict.empty()`, which keeps the type,
batch size and device of the input.

If you pass `tensordict_out` to `forward()`, the outputs are
written into it, whatever the value of `inplace`. Defaults to
`True`.
- **method** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the name of the method of `module` to call.
Unlike a lambda around the method, this keeps the parameters and
buffers of `module` registered in the wrapper. Defaults to
`None`, which calls `module` itself.
- **method_kwargs** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - keyword arguments passed to
`module` (or to `method`) at each call. Defaults to `None`.
- **strict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a missing input raises a
`KeyError`. If `False`, `None` is passed in its place, and if
`module` then fails, the error names the missing keys. Defaults to
`False`.
- **get_kwargs** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - keyword arguments passed to
[`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) when the inputs are read,
for example `{"as_padded_tensor": True}` for ragged inputs.
Defaults to `None`.

Attributes that the wrapper does not have, such as `weight` for a
[`Linear`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Linear.html#torch.nn.Linear), are read from `module`. Inside a
[`set_skip_existing`](tensordict.nn.set_skip_existing.html#tensordict.nn.set_skip_existing) block, the module does not run
when all its `out_keys` are already in the input.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> module = TensorDictModule(nn.Linear(3, 4), in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> data = TensorDict(x=torch.ones(2, 3), batch_size=[2])
>>> data = module(data)
>>> print(data)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> module(torch.ones(2, 3)).shape
torch.Size([2, 4])
```

A plain function works too. This one reads a nested key and writes two
nested keys:

```
>>> module = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x: (x - 1, x + 1),
... in_keys=[("input", "x")],
... out_keys=[("output", "x-1"), ("output", "x+1")],
... )
>>> td = module(TensorDict({("input", "x"): torch.zeros(())}))
>>> td["output", "x+1"]
tensor(1.)
```

With empty `in_keys`, the module only writes entries:

```
>>> module = TensorDictModule(lambda: torch.zeros(3), in_keys=[], out_keys=["x"])
>>> module(TensorDict())["x"]
tensor([0., 0., 0.])
```

A dict `in_keys` passes the values as keyword arguments. By default
(`out_to_in_map=True`), its keys are the argument names and its values
are the tensordict keys. One tensordict key can feed several arguments:

```
>>> module = TensorDictModule(lambda x, *, y, z: x+y+z,
... in_keys={'x': '1', 'y': '2', 'z': '2'}, out_keys=['t']
... )
>>> td = module(TensorDict({'1': torch.ones(()), '2': torch.ones(())*2}, []))
>>> td['t']
tensor(5.)
```

With `out_to_in_map=False`, the keys of the dict are the tensordict keys
and its values are the argument names:

```
>>> module = TensorDictModule(lambda x, *, y: x+y,
... in_keys={'1': 'x', '2': 'y'}, out_keys=['z'], out_to_in_map=False
... )
>>> td = module(TensorDict({'1': torch.ones(()), '2': torch.ones(())*2}, []))
>>> td['z']
tensor(3.)
```

`method` calls another method of the module, here with a keyword
argument from `method_kwargs`:

```
>>> class MyNet(nn.Module):
... def my_func(self, tensor, *, an_integer):
... return tensor + an_integer
...
>>> module = TensorDictModule(
... MyNet(),
... in_keys=["a"],
... out_keys=["b"],
... method="my_func",
... method_kwargs={"an_integer": 2},
... )
>>> module(TensorDict(a=0))["b"]
tensor(2)
```

To call the module with other parameters, put them in a tensordict and
use [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module) as a context manager:

```
>>> module = TensorDictModule(
... nn.GRUCell(4, 8), in_keys=["input", "hidden"], out_keys=["output"]
... )
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> params = params.apply(torch.zeros_like)
>>> td = TensorDict(input=torch.ones(3, 4), hidden=torch.ones(3, 8), batch_size=[3])
>>> with params.to_module(module):
... td = module(td)
>>> # with zero weights, the output is half the hidden state
>>> (td["output"] == 0.5).all()
tensor(True)
```

*property*device*: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*

The device of the first parameter of the module, or `cpu` if it has no parameter.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17 because modules may
contain parameters and buffers on multiple devices.

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) = None*, *args=None*, ***, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Reads `in_keys` from `tensordict`, calls the wrapped module, and writes `out_keys`.

If you call the module with tensors instead of a tensordict, the
tensors are put in a new tensordict first, and the call returns the
output tensors (see [`dispatch()`](tensordict.nn.dispatch.html#tensordict.nn.dispatch)).

Parameters:

**tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input tensordict.

Keyword Arguments:

- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - if given, the outputs
are written into it and it is returned, whatever the value of
`inplace`. Defaults to `None`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the wrapped module.

Returns:

The tensordict that holds the outputs (see `inplace`).

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*property*is_functional*: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

Whether the wrapped module is a legacy functorch functional module.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17. It only checks
for the `FunctionalModule` classes of the legacy
`functorch.make_functional` API and has no replacement.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Returns `True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys` attribute.

[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) wraps the callables that
fail this check in a [`WrapModule`](tensordict.nn.WrapModule.html#tensordict.nn.WrapModule).

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the module writes to the output tensordict.

After `select_out_keys()`, only the selected keys. The full list
is in `out_keys_source`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Undoes `select_out_keys()`: the module writes all its `out_keys` again.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x, y: (x + 2, y + 2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"]
... )
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> mod.out_keys
['d']
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod.out_keys
['c', 'd']
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(())))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Without `parameters`, the parameters of the module are reset in

# TensorDictModuleBase

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase(**args: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*)

Bases: [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)

Base class of the tensordict modules, which read `in_keys` from a tensordict and write `out_keys`.

Subclass it to write a module whose `forward` takes a tensordict and
returns a tensordict (`tensordict_out = module(tensordict_in)`). Set
`in_keys` and `out_keys` as class attributes or in `__init__`:
[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) and the other modules read
them to know which entries the module reads and writes. To wrap a
module that takes and returns tensors, use
[`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule) instead. See
[Modules: TensorDictModule and tensordict.nn](../../modules.html#modules-guide).

The base class gives every module `select_out_keys()` and
`reset_out_keys()`, to choose which outputs a call keeps, and
`reset_parameters_recursive()`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModuleBase
>>> class Mod(TensorDictModuleBase):
... in_keys = ["a"] # can also be specified during __init__
... out_keys = ["b", "c"]
... def forward(self, tensordict):
... b = tensordict["a"].clone()
... c = b + 1
... return tensordict.replace({"b": b, "c": c})
>>> mod = Mod()
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=0))
>>> td["b"]
tensor(0)
>>> td["c"]
tensor(1)
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("c")
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=0))
>>> td["c"]
tensor(1)
>>> "b" in td
False
```

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Returns `True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys` attribute.

[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) wraps the callables that
fail this check in a [`WrapModule`](tensordict.nn.WrapModule.html#tensordict.nn.WrapModule).

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the module writes to the output tensordict.

After `select_out_keys()`, only the selected keys. The full list
is in `out_keys_source`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Undoes `select_out_keys()`: the module writes all its `out_keys` again.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x, y: (x + 2, y + 2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"]
... )
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> mod.out_keys
['d']
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod.out_keys
['c', 'd']
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(())))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Resets the parameters of every submodule that has a `reset_parameters` method.

Without `parameters`, the parameters of the module are reset in
place. With `parameters`, the module is left as it is: the values in
`parameters` are reset in place, as if they were loaded into the
module (see [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module)). Use this
for parameters kept outside the module, for example in a functional
call. Values that share their storage with the module parameters,
such as those of [`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module), reset
the module too.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the parameters to reset,
with the structure of
[`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module) and an empty batch
size. Defaults to `None`, which resets the parameters of the
module.

Returns:

`None` without `parameters`. Otherwise a new tensordict of
tensors that share their storage with `parameters` and require
gradients.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `parameters` has batch dimensions.

Without `parameters`, the call warns if no submodule has a
`reset_parameters` method.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 3), nn.ReLU())
>>> old_weight = net[0].weight.clone()
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> module.reset_parameters_recursive()
>>> torch.equal(old_weight, net[0].weight)
False
```

The parameters can also live outside the module:

```
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module).clone()
>>> old_params = params.clone()
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
>>> torch.equal(net[0].weight, old_params["module", "0", "weight"])
True
```

select_out_keys(**out_keys*) → TensorDictModuleBase

Keeps only some of the `out_keys` in the output of the module, and returns the module.

Use it to drop intermediate outputs, for example those of a
[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential). The module changes in
place: `out_keys` becomes the selected keys, and
`out_keys_source` keeps the full list. A call still computes all
the outputs, and then removes the ones that are not selected. It
removes nothing else, so the input entries stay in the output. When
you call the module with tensors (see [`dispatch()`](tensordict.nn.dispatch.html#tensordict.nn.dispatch)),
it returns only the selected outputs. `reset_out_keys()` undoes
the selection.

Parameters:

***out_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys to keep. Each one must be in
`out_keys`.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if a key is not in `out_keys`. The error names the
 missing keys, and is also a `RuntimeError`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x, y: (x + 2, y + 2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"]
... )
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> mod.out_keys, mod.out_keys_source
(['d'], ['c', 'd'])
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(())))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'd']
>>> mod(torch.zeros(()), torch.ones(()))
tensor(3.)
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> sorted(mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(()))).keys())
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

It works on a [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) too:

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... TensorDictModule(lambda y: y + 1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> sorted(seq(TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(()))).keys())
['x', 'z']
```

# TensorDictModuleWrapper

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleWrapper(*td_module: [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Wraps a tensordict module and behaves like it, except for the methods that a subclass overrides.

Subclass it to change `forward()` and keep the `in_keys`,
`out_keys`, parameters and attributes of the wrapped module. An
attribute that the wrapper does not have is read from `td_module`.

Parameters:

**td_module** ([*TensorDictModuleBase*](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)) - the module to wrap.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictModuleWrapper
>>> class TimesTen(TensorDictModuleWrapper):
... def forward(self, tensordict):
... tensordict = self.td_module(tensordict)
... tensordict["y"] = tensordict["y"] * 10
... return tensordict
>>> inner = TensorDictModule(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> wrapped = TimesTen(inner)
>>> wrapped.in_keys, wrapped.out_keys
(['x'], ['y'])
>>> wrapped(TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(2)))["y"]
tensor([10., 10.])
```

forward(**args: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Calls `td_module` with the same arguments and returns its result.

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Returns `True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys` attribute.

[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) wraps the callables that
fail this check in a [`WrapModule`](tensordict.nn.WrapModule.html#tensordict.nn.WrapModule).

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the module writes, by default those of `td_module`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that `td_module` writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Undoes `select_out_keys()`: the module writes all its `out_keys` again.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x, y: (x + 2, y + 2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"]
... )
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> mod.out_keys
['d']
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod.out_keys
['c', 'd']
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(())))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Resets the parameters of every submodule that has a `reset_parameters` method.

Without `parameters`, the parameters of the module are reset in

`parameters` are reset in place, as if they were loaded into the

[`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module) and an empty batch
size. Defaults to `None`, which resets the parameters of the

# TensorDictSequential

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential(**modules: Callable[[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)], [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)]*, *partial_tolerant: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *selected_out_keys: List[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule)

Runs TensorDictModules one after the other on the same tensordict.

Like [`torch.nn.Sequential`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Sequential.html#torch.nn.Sequential), each module receives the output of the
previous one. Here the data is a tensordict, so a module can read any entry
that an earlier module wrote.

The `in_keys` of the sequence are the keys that a module reads and that no
earlier module writes. The input tensordict must contain them. The
`out_keys` are all the keys that the modules write, each listed once.
To call the sequence with other parameters, use
[`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module) (see the second example).
See [Modules: TensorDictModule and tensordict.nn](../../modules.html#modules-guide) for a guide.

The modules are given as positional arguments, as one list, or as one
dict (or `OrderedDict`) that maps names to modules. `seq[i]` and
`seq["name"]` return a module, and a slice returns a new sequence with
the same options. Assigning or deleting `seq[i]` or `seq["name"]`
edits the sequence (a new name appends the module), and `in_keys` and
`out_keys` are recomputed. A module registered under several names
runs once for each name.

Parameters:

***modules** ([*TensorDictModuleBase*](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)*or**Callable*) - the modules to run, in
order. A callable without `in_keys` and `out_keys`, such as a
function that takes and returns a tensordict, is wrapped in a
[`WrapModule`](tensordict.nn.WrapModule.html#tensordict.nn.WrapModule). Its keys are then not part of
the `in_keys` and `out_keys` of the sequence.

Keyword Arguments:

- **partial_tolerant** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the input can lack
some of the `in_keys`: a module runs only if all its inputs are
present, and is skipped otherwise. On a lazy stack, a module that
cannot run on the whole stack runs on each tensordict of the stack
that has its inputs, and its outputs are written into that
tensordict. Defaults to `False`.
- **selected_out_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the `out_keys` to
keep in the output, as with `select_out_keys()`. Each one must
be in `out_keys`. Defaults to `None`, which keeps all of them.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - 

where the sequence writes its `out_keys`
after the last module ran.

- `True`: into the input tensordict, which is returned.
- `False`: into a new, empty [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).
- `"empty"`: into `input.empty()`, which keeps the type, device
and batch size of the input.
- `None`: the sequence returns what the last module returns,
so the `inplace` value of each module decides.

With `False` or `"empty"`, the modules run on a shallow copy
of the input, so the input does not change. See the last example.
Defaults to `None`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>> module = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["x+1"]),
... TensorDictModule(nn.Linear(3, 4), in_keys=["x+1"], out_keys=["w*(x+1)+b"]),
... )
>>> # with tensordict input
>>> print(module(TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(3)}, [])))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 w*(x+1)+b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 x+1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> module.in_keys, module.out_keys
(['x'], ['x+1', 'w*(x+1)+b'])
>>> # with tensor input: returns all the output keys in the order of the modules, ie "x+1" and "w*(x+1)+b"
>>> module(x=torch.zeros(3))
(tensor([1., 1., 1.]), tensor([-0.7214, -0.8748, 0.1571, -0.1138], grad_fn=<ViewBackward0>))
>>> module(torch.zeros(3))
(tensor([1., 1., 1.]), tensor([-0.7214, -0.8748, 0.1571, -0.1138], grad_fn=<ViewBackward0>))
```

A sequence can hold probabilistic modules, and be called with other
parameters through [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module), also
under [`torch.vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap):

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import (
... ProbabilisticTensorDictModule,
... ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential,
... )
>>> from tensordict.nn.distributions import NormalParamExtractor
>>> from torch.distributions import Normal
>>> td = TensorDict({"input": torch.randn(3, 4)}, [3,])
>>> net1 = torch.nn.Linear(4, 8)
>>> module1 = TensorDictModule(net1, in_keys=["input"], out_keys=["params"])
>>> normal_params = TensorDictModule(
... NormalParamExtractor(), in_keys=["params"], out_keys=["loc", "scale"]
... )
>>> td_module1 = ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential(
... module1,
... normal_params,
... ProbabilisticTensorDictModule(
... in_keys=["loc", "scale"],
... out_keys=["hidden"],
... distribution_class=Normal,
... return_log_prob=True,
... )
... )
>>> module2 = torch.nn.Linear(4, 8)
>>> td_module2 = TensorDictModule(
... module=module2, in_keys=["hidden"], out_keys=["output"]
... )
>>> td_module = TensorDictSequential(td_module1, td_module2)
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(td_module)
>>> with params.to_module(td_module):
... _ = td_module(td)
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['hidden', 'hidden_log_prob', 'input', 'loc', 'output', 'params', 'scale']
>>> td["output"].shape
torch.Size([3, 8])
```

With [`torch.vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap) over 4 copies of the parameters, each entry gets
a leading dimension of size 4:

```
>>> from torch import vmap
>>> params = params.expand(4)
>>> def func(td, params):
... with params.to_module(td_module):
... return td_module(td)
>>> td_vmap = vmap(func, (None, 0))(td, params)
>>> td_vmap.batch_size
torch.Size([4, 3])
>>> td_vmap["output"].shape
torch.Size([4, 3, 8])
```

The `inplace` argument controls where the outputs go. In this example the
inner modules use `inplace=False`, so each one passes only its outputs to
the next. The sequence uses `inplace=True`, so it writes the final
`output` into the input object. The intermediate entries are not written
into it.

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule as Mod, TensorDictSequential as Seq
>>>
>>> class MyClass(TensorClass):
... input: torch.Tensor
... output: torch.Tensor | None = None
>>>
>>> obj = MyClass(torch.randn(2, 3), batch_size=(2,))
>>>
>>> model = Seq(
... Mod(
... lambda x: (x + 1, x - 1),
... in_keys=["input"],
... out_keys=[("intermediate", "0"), ("intermediate", "1")],
... inplace=False
... ),
... Mod(
... lambda y0, y1: y0 * y1,
... in_keys=[("intermediate", "0"), ("intermediate", "1")],
... out_keys=["output"],
... inplace=False
... ),
... inplace=True, )
>>> print(model(obj))
MyClass(
 input=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 output=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

*property*device*: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*

The device of the first parameter of the module, or `cpu` if it has no parameter.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17 because modules may
contain parameters and buffers on multiple devices.

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) = None*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Runs the modules in order on `tensordict` and returns the result (see `inplace`).

If you call the sequence with tensors instead of a tensordict, the
call returns the output tensors (see [`dispatch()`](tensordict.nn.dispatch.html#tensordict.nn.dispatch)).

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input tensordict.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - if given, the
`out_keys` are written into it and it is returned, whatever
the value of `inplace`. Defaults to `None`.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if other keyword arguments are given.

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*property*is_functional*: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

Whether the wrapped module is a legacy functorch functional module.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17. It only checks
for the `FunctionalModule` classes of the legacy
`functorch.make_functional` API and has no replacement.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Returns `True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys` attribute.

`TensorDictSequential` wraps the callables that
fail this check in a [`WrapModule`](tensordict.nn.WrapModule.html#tensordict.nn.WrapModule).

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the modules write, each listed once, or those chosen with `select_out_keys()`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Undoes `select_out_keys()`: the sequence writes all its `out_keys` again, and returns `self`.

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Resets the parameters of every submodule that has a `reset_parameters` method.

Without `parameters`, the parameters of the module are reset in
place. With `parameters`, the module is left as it is: the values in
`parameters` are reset in place, as if they were loaded into the
module (see [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module)). Use this
for parameters kept outside the module, for example in a functional
call. Values that share their storage with the module parameters,
such as those of [`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module), reset
the module too.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the parameters to reset,
with the structure of
[`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module) and an empty batch
size. Defaults to `None`, which resets the parameters of the
module.

Returns:

`None` without `parameters`. Otherwise a new tensordict of
tensors that share their storage with `parameters` and require
gradients.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `parameters` has batch dimensions.

Without `parameters`, the call warns if no submodule has a
`reset_parameters` method.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 3), nn.ReLU())
>>> old_weight = net[0].weight.clone()
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> module.reset_parameters_recursive()
>>> torch.equal(old_weight, net[0].weight)
False
```

The parameters can also live outside the module:

```
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module).clone()
>>> old_params = params.clone()
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
>>> torch.equal(net[0].weight, old_params["module", "0", "weight"])
True
```

select_out_keys(**selected_out_keys*) → TensorDictSequential

Keeps only some of the `out_keys` in the output of the sequence, and returns the sequence.

The sequence changes in place, and `reset_out_keys()` undoes the
change. The modules still compute all their outputs; the call then
writes only the selected ones, and the entries of the input, into the
output.

Parameters:

***selected_out_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys to keep. Each one must be
in `out_keys`.

Returns:

`self`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if a key in `selected_out_keys` is not part of `out_keys`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule as Mod, TensorDictSequential as Seq
>>> seq = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... Mod(lambda y: y + 1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> seq.out_keys
['z']
>>> td = seq(TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(())))
>>> "y" in td
False
>>> td["z"]
tensor(2.)
>>> _ = seq.reset_out_keys()
>>> seq.out_keys
['y', 'z']
```

select_subsequence(*in_keys: [Iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out_keys: [Iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → TensorDictSequential

Returns a new sequence with only the modules that can run from `in_keys` and that `out_keys` need.

Two filters are applied, in this order:

- `in_keys`: a module is kept if each of its inputs is in
`in_keys` or is written by a module kept before it. The other
modules, and those that read their outputs, are dropped.
- `out_keys`: of the modules left, a module is kept if it writes one
of `out_keys`, or an input of a module kept after it.

A nested `TensorDictSequential` is filtered the same way. The
modules are not copied: the new sequence holds the same module
objects. Modules of a named sequence keep their names, and the new
sequence keeps `partial_tolerant` and `inplace`.

Parameters:

- **in_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the keys that the modules
can start from. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
`in_keys` of the sequence.
- **out_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the keys to compute.
Defaults to `None`, which uses the `out_keys` of the
sequence.

Returns:

A new sequence of the same type.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if no module is left.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential as Seq, TensorDictModule as Mod
>>> idn = lambda x: x
>>> module = Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["b"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["c"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["c"], out_keys=["d"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["e"]),
... )
>>> # the modules that can run from "c"
>>> module.select_subsequence(in_keys=["c"]).out_keys
['d']
>>> # the modules that "c" depends on
>>> sub = module.select_subsequence(out_keys=["c"])
>>> sub.in_keys, sub.out_keys
(['a'], ['b', 'c'])
>>> sub[0] is module[0]
True
```

Nested sequences are filtered too:

```
>>> module = Seq(
... Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["b"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["c"]),
... ),
... Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["d"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["d"], out_keys=["e"]),
... ),
... )
>>> sub = module.select_subsequence(in_keys=["b", "d"], out_keys=["e"])
>>> len(sub), sub[0].out_keys
(1, ['d', 'e'])
```

# WrapModule

*class*tensordict.nn.WrapModule(*func: Callable[[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)], [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)]*, ***, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *in_keys: List[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out_keys: List[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Wraps a function that takes and returns a tensordict as a tensordict module.

Use it to put a function that works on the whole tensordict, such as a
reshape, in a [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential). A sequence
wraps the callables that have no `in_keys` and `out_keys` in a
`WrapModule` itself.

Parameters:

**func** (*Callable**[**[*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*]**,*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*]*) - the function to
wrap. It takes a tensordict and returns a tensordict.

Keyword Arguments:

- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the call writes the entries of
the result of `func` into the input with
[`update()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update) and returns the input.
If `False`, the call returns what `func` returns. Defaults to
`False`.
- **in_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the keys that `func` reads.
They are not checked: they tell a
[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) what the module
reads. Defaults to `None`, which sets `[]`.
- **out_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - the keys that `func`
writes. They are not checked, like `in_keys`. Defaults to
`None`, which sets `[]`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential as Seq, TensorDictModule as Mod, WrapModule
>>> seq = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x * 2, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... WrapModule(lambda td: td.reshape(-1)),
... )
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.ones(3, 4, 5), batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> td = seq(td)
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([12])
>>> td["y"].shape
torch.Size([12, 5])
```

forward(*data: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Calls `func` on `data` and returns the result, or `data` updated with it if `inplace=True`.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Returns `True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys` attribute.

[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) wraps the callables that
fail this check in a `WrapModule`.

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Undoes `select_out_keys()`: the module writes all its `out_keys` again.

Returns:

`self`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(
... lambda x, y: (x + 2, y + 2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"]
... )
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> mod.out_keys
['d']
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod.out_keys
['c', 'd']
>>> td = mod(TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(()), b=torch.ones(())))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Resets the parameters of every submodule that has a `reset_parameters` method.

Without `parameters`, the parameters of the module are reset in
place. With `parameters`, the module is left as it is: the values in
`parameters` are reset in place, as if they were loaded into the
module (see [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module)). Use this
for parameters kept outside the module, for example in a functional

such as those of [`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module), reset
the module too.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the parameters to reset,
with the structure of
[`from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module) and an empty batch
size. Defaults to `None`, which resets the parameters of the
module.

Returns:

`None` without `parameters`. Otherwise a new tensordict of
tensors that share their storage with `parameters` and require

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `parameters` has batch dimensions.

```
>>> old_weight = net[0].weight.clone()

>>> torch.equal(old_weight, net[0].weight)

```

```
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module).clone()
>>> old_params = params.clone()
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
>>> torch.equal(net[0].weight, old_params["module", "0", "weight"])
```
