# pack_memmap

tensordict.pack_memmap(*prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *archive_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, ***, *compression: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *compresslevel: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

Packs a memory-mapped tensordict directory into a single-file zip archive.

The entries of the archive are the files of the directory, so
[`unpack_memmap()`](tensordict.unpack_memmap.html#tensordict.unpack_memmap) (or `unzip`) gives the directory back. Tensor
payloads are stored uncompressed by default and aligned to 64 bytes, so
that [`load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap) can memory-map the
archive and make each leaf a view into the mapping, without a copy.
`td.save("x.tdz")` writes the same archive from a tensordict.

Parameters:

- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - a directory written by
[`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap) or a similar method.
- **archive_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the archive to create, outside
`prefix`. An existing file is replaced by a new file, which
needs write access to the file and to its directory: a symlink is
followed, but other hard links keep the old content.

Keyword Arguments:

- **compression** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the compression of the tensor
payloads: `"stored"`, `"deflate"`, `"bzip2"`, `"lzma"`, or
a [`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile) constant. A compressed archive is smaller, but its
leaves are decompressed in memory when they are loaded, instead of
being memory-mapped. Defaults to `None`, which stores them
uncompressed.
- **compresslevel** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the compression level, passed to
[`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile). Defaults to `None`, which uses the default
level of the compression method.

Returns:

The path of the archive, as a [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path).

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if `prefix` has no `meta.json` file, or if
 `archive_path` is inside `prefix` or is one of its files.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, pack_memmap
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b=TensorDict(c=torch.ones(3, 2)))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as path:
... _ = td.memmap(Path(path) / "saved")
... archive = pack_memmap(Path(path) / "saved", Path(path) / "saved.tdz")
... print(archive.name, (TensorDict.load_memmap(archive) == td).all())
saved.tdz True
```

# pad

tensordict.pad(*tensordict: T*, *pad_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]*, *value: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) = 0.0*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → T

Pads all tensors in a tensordict along the batch dimensions with a constant value.

Use it to grow the batch dimensions of one tensordict, for example to
bring samples to a common size before you stack them. To pad and stack a
list of tensordicts in one call, use [`pad_sequence()`](tensordict.pad_sequence.html#tensordict.pad_sequence)
(see [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)).

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instance*) - the tensordict to
pad.
- **pad_size** (*sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the padding before and after each batch
dimension, starting from the first one (unlike
[`torch.nn.functional.pad()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.pad.html#torch.nn.functional.pad), which starts from the last):
`(dim0_before, dim0_after, dim1_before, dim1_after, ...)`. Its
length must be even and at most twice the number of batch
dimensions, or a `RuntimeError` is raised.
- **value** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*,**optional*) - the value of the padded elements. Non-tensor
entries hold `None` there instead. Defaults to `0.0`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict keeps its
identity and keys, its leaves are replaced one by one with padded
tensors, and the call returns it. A lazy stack pads each of its
tensordicts in place and grows along the stack dimension with new
tensordicts filled with `value`. See
[In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions). Defaults to `False`.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, checks that every leaf can be
padded before anything is changed, so that a bad `pad_size`
raises before an in-place pad changes some of the leaves. Set it
to `False` to skip the check when the inputs are known to be
valid. Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

The padded tensordict. When `inplace=True` this is the same object as
the input; otherwise a new tensordict, or a new tensorclass of the
same type for a tensorclass input.

Note

With `inplace=False`, a lazy stack gives a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). If the stacked tensordicts have no
names, it has no names either, even when the stack dimension has a
name (from `stack_dim_name` or the `names` setter). To keep that
name, name the dimension of the result again with
[`refine_names()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names).

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, pad
>>> import torch
>>> td = TensorDict({'a': torch.ones(3, 4, 1),
... 'b': torch.ones(3, 4, 1, 1)}, batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> dim0_left, dim0_right, dim1_left, dim1_right = [0, 1, 0, 2]
>>> padded_td = pad(td, [dim0_left, dim0_right, dim1_left, dim1_right], value=0.0)
>>> print(padded_td.batch_size)
torch.Size([4, 6])
>>> print(padded_td.get("a").shape)
torch.Size([4, 6, 1])
>>> print(padded_td.get("b").shape)
torch.Size([4, 6, 1, 1])
```

---

# pad_sequence

tensordict.pad_sequence(*list_of_tensordicts: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[T]*, *pad_dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *padding_value: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) = 0.0*, *out: T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *return_mask: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) = False*, *padding_side: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'right'*) → T

Pads tensordicts to a common size along one dimension and stacks them densely.

Use it to batch samples whose entries differ in size along one
dimension, such as sequences of different lengths. Every entry is padded
along `pad_dim` to the largest size among the inputs, then the inputs
are stacked along a new first dimension. The inputs must have the same
keys, and the entry shapes must match in every dimension other than
`pad_dim`. To keep the inputs unpadded, use
[`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) instead (see [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)).

Parameters:

- **list_of_tensordicts** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the tensordicts to pad and stack.
- **pad_dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension of the entries to pad, counted
from the first dimension of each entry (batch dimensions
included). If it is a batch dimension, the batch size of the
result is padded too. A negative `pad_dim` counts from the last
dimension of each entry. If it lands on a batch dimension of some
entries and on another dimension of others, the batch size is not
padded, and, unless `out` is given, no entry may be longer along
it than the batch of the first sample. Defaults to `0`.
- **padding_value** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*,**optional*) - the value of the padded elements.
When `pad_dim` is a batch dimension, non-tensor entries hold
`None` there instead, as with [`pad()`](tensordict.pad.html#tensordict.pad). Defaults
to `0.0`.
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into. Defaults to `None`.
- **return_mask** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*or*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the result has
a `"masks"` entry. If `return_mask` is a nested key (a string
or a tuple of strings), the masks are stored under that key. The
masks entry is a tensordict with the structure of the stacked
tensordict. Each of its entries is the mask of the valid values.
If `pad_dim` is a batch dimension, the mask has the output's
batch size. Otherwise, its shape is the output's batch size
followed by the padded length, regardless of the feature
dimension's position. Tensorclass inputs raise a
`RuntimeError`. Use [`unpad_sequence()`](tensordict.unpad_sequence.html#tensordict.unpad_sequence) to turn
the result back into the variable-length samples. Defaults to
`False`.
- **padding_side** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - `"right"` puts the padding after the
data along `pad_dim`, `"left"` puts it before, as
`get(key, as_padded_tensor=True, padding_side=...)` does on a
lazy stack. The masks mark the data positions on either side.
Defaults to `"right"`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (or the tensorclass of the inputs)
with batch size `[len(list_of_tensordicts), *batch_size]`.

Raises:

- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `list_of_tensordicts` is empty, if the entry
 shapes differ in a dimension other than `pad_dim`, or if
 `return_mask` is set for tensorclass inputs.
- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if `padding_side` is neither `"left"` nor `"right"`,
 or if a negative `pad_dim` lands on a batch dimension of some
 entries and on another dimension of others, and, with no `out`,
 an entry is longer along it than the batch of the first sample.
- [**IndexError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#IndexError) - if `pad_dim` is out of range for an entry.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, pad_sequence
>>> list_td = [
... TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros((3, 8)), "b": torch.zeros((6, 8))}, batch_size=[]),
... TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros((5, 8)), "b": torch.zeros((6, 8))}, batch_size=[]),
... ]
>>> padded_td = pad_sequence(list_td, return_mask=True)
>>> padded_td["a"].shape, padded_td["b"].shape
(torch.Size([2, 5, 8]), torch.Size([2, 6, 8]))
>>> padded_td["masks", "a"].sum(-1)
tensor([3, 5])
```

# parse_tensor_dict_string

tensordict.parse_tensor_dict_string(*s: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*)

Builds a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) from its printed form.

It is a debugging tool: it rebuilds a tensordict with the keys, shapes,
dtypes, devices and batch sizes of a printed one, so that you can
reproduce a tensordict from a log. The values are not in the repr, so
every tensor of the result is filled with zeros.

Parameters:

**s** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - the repr of a tensordict, as printed with the default print
options (see [`set_printoptions()`](tensordict.set_printoptions.html#tensordict.set_printoptions)).

Returns:

A new [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if a field is not a `Tensor` or a `TensorDict` printed
 with the default print options, or if `s` is the repr of a lazy
 stack with exclusive keys.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, parse_tensor_dict_string
>>> td = TensorDict(
... obs=torch.ones(3, 4),
... next=TensorDict(done=torch.ones(3, 1, dtype=torch.bool)),
... batch_size=[3],
... )
>>> rebuilt = parse_tensor_dict_string(repr(td))
>>> rebuilt["next", "done"].dtype, rebuilt.batch_size
(torch.bool, torch.Size([3]))
>>> rebuilt["obs"].sum()
tensor(0.)
```

# TDGraphModule

*class*tensordict.prototype.fx.TDGraphModule(*graph_module: [GraphModule](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.GraphModule)*, *out_keys: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*)

Bases: [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)

The module that `symbolic_trace()` returns: an FX graph that reads and writes a tensordict.

A call reads the `in_keys` of the traced module from the input
tensordict, runs the graph, and writes the outputs at `out_keys`, into
`tensordict_out` if given, else into the input. The `graph` and
`code` attributes are those of the underlying
[`torch.fx.GraphModule`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.GraphModule).

This class is a prototype: its API can change without a deprecation
period. See `symbolic_trace()` for an example.

Parameters:

- **graph_module** ([*GraphModule*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.GraphModule)) - the traced graph.
- **out_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys where the outputs are written.

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Runs the graph on `tensordict` and writes the outputs at `out_keys`.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input tensordict.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - the tensordict to write
the outputs into. Defaults to `None`, which writes them into
`tensordict`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the graph.

Returns:

The tensordict that holds the outputs.

# symbolic_trace

tensordict.prototype.symbolic_trace(*td_module: [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)*) → [TDGraphModule](tensordict.prototype.fx.TDGraphModule.html#tensordict.prototype.fx.TDGraphModule)

Traces a TensorDictModule or a TensorDictSequential into an FX graph.

This function is a prototype: its API can change without a deprecation
period. See [FX tracing (prototype)](../../fx.html#fx) for a guide.

It supports a [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule) that wraps an
[`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module) that [`torch.fx.symbolic_trace()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.symbolic_trace) can trace,
and a [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) of such modules. A
module that wraps a plain function or a lambda raises a `RuntimeError`
("Unsupported type ... passed for root!").

Parameters:

**td_module** ([*TensorDictModuleBase*](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)) - the module to trace.

Returns:

A `TDGraphModule` with the same inputs and outputs as
`td_module`.

Raises:

[**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - if `td_module` is not a
 [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule) or a
 [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> from tensordict.prototype.fx import symbolic_trace
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(nn.Linear(3, 4), in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["hidden"]),
... TensorDictModule(nn.ReLU(), in_keys=["hidden"], out_keys=["y"]),
... )
>>> graph_module = symbolic_trace(seq)
>>> td = graph_module(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(2, 3), batch_size=[2]))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['hidden', 'x', 'y']
>>> expected = seq(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(2, 3), batch_size=[2]))["y"]
>>> torch.equal(td["y"], expected)
True
```

# refresh_archive_checksums

tensordict.refresh_archive_checksums(*archive_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*) → [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

Recomputes the CRC-32 checksums of a memory-mapped archive after in-place writes.

A tensordict loaded with `TensorDict.load_memmap(path, mode="r+")`, or
created by `memmap_like` with a `".tdz"` path, writes into the
archive without updating the CRC-32 checksum that the zip format stores
for each entry. [`load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap) does not
check the checksums of uncompressed leaves, so call this function only
before you give the archive to a tool that checks them, such as
`unzip`, [`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile) or [`unpack_memmap()`](tensordict.unpack_memmap.html#tensordict.unpack_memmap). The archive is
changed in place.

Parameters:

**archive_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the archive to update.

Returns:

The path of the archive, as a [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path).

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if `archive_path` is not an archive (see
 [`is_memmap_archive()`](tensordict.is_memmap_archive.html#tensordict.is_memmap_archive)).

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import zipfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, refresh_archive_checksums
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as path:
... archive = Path(path) / "td.tdz"
... _ = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)).save(archive)
... _ = TensorDict.load_memmap(archive, mode="r+")["a"].add_(1)
... print(zipfile.ZipFile(archive).testzip()) # the first bad entry
... _ = refresh_archive_checksums(archive)
... print(zipfile.ZipFile(archive).testzip())
a.memmap
None
```

# save

tensordict.save(*data: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *copy_existing: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *return_early: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *share_non_tensor: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *archive: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *compression: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Saves a tensordict to disk, and returns a memory-mapped copy of it.

Same as [`memmap()`](tensordict.memmap.html#tensordict.memmap), and as
[`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap), which holds the full text of
every argument. The directory mirrors the key structure of the
tensordict: one file per tensor and one metadata file per nested
tensordict. If `prefix` ends with `".tdz"`, a single archive file is
written instead. Load the result with [`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load). See
[Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving).

Parameters:

- **data** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instance*) - the tensordict to save.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the directory to write to, or a file name that
ends with `".tdz"`. Defaults to `None`, which writes the
tensors to anonymous shared memory and saves nothing to disk.
- **copy_existing** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, an entry that is already
memory-mapped to a file outside `prefix` raises an error. If
`True`, it is copied. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **num_threads** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that write the
files. Defaults to `0`.
- **return_early** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `num_threads > 1`,
returns a [`TensorDictFuture`](tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture.html#tensordict.utils.TensorDictFuture) at once, while
the threads write the files. Defaults to `False`.
- **share_non_tensor** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries are
shared between the processes of a node. Defaults to `False`.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, keys that hold path
separators or special characters are encoded in the file names.
Defaults to `True`.
- **archive** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `prefix` is a file and the
tensordict is written as a single zip archive that
[`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load) can memory-map. If `None`, an archive
is written when `prefix` ends with `".tdz"`. Defaults to
`None`.
- **compression** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the compression of the archive
entries: `"stored"`, `"deflate"`, `"bzip2"`, `"lzma"` or a
[`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile) constant. Only valid for an archive. Defaults to
`None`, which stores them uncompressed. Only uncompressed
entries load without a copy.

Returns:

A new, locked tensordict whose leaves are
[`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances backed by the
saved files. `data` itself is not changed.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.ones(3, 2)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... saved = tensordict.save(td, tmpdir)
... print(saved.is_locked, type(saved["a"]).__name__)
... loaded = tensordict.load(tmpdir)
True MemoryMappedTensor
```

# set_capture_non_tensor_stack

*class*tensordict.set_capture_non_tensor_stack(*mode: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*)

Sets whether stacking identical non-tensor data gives one value instead of a stack.

By default, [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack) of [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)
returns a [`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack), even when all the values
are equal. With `mode=True`, a stack of equal values gives a single
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData). The `CAPTURE_NONTENSOR_STACK`
environment variable sets the mode at import. Use it as a context manager
or a decorator, or call `set_capture_non_tensor_stack(mode).set()` to
change the mode for the rest of the program.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Capturing identical non-tensor data (`set_capture_non_tensor_stack(True)`
or `CAPTURE_NONTENSOR_STACK=1`) is deprecated and will be removed in
TensorDict 0.17. Use [`NonTensorStack.data`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack.data)
to get the single value of a stack of identical values.
`set_capture_non_tensor_stack(False)`, the default, does not warn,
and will keep working, doing nothing, after the removal.

Parameters:

**mode** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) - if `True`, stacking identical non-tensor data gives one
value, and the call emits a `DeprecationWarning`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import NonTensorData, set_capture_non_tensor_stack
>>> with set_capture_non_tensor_stack(False):
... stack = torch.stack([NonTensorData("a"), NonTensorData("a")])
>>> type(stack).__name__, stack.data
('NonTensorStack', 'a')
```

---

# set_get_defaults_to_none

tensordict.set_get_defaults_to_none(*set_to_none: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Sets whether [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) returns `None` or raises for a missing key.

The setting applies to every call of `get` and `get_at` that passes no
default. The environment variable `TD_GET_DEFAULTS_TO_NONE` sets its
initial value.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Since v0.7, [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) returns `None` for a
missing key by default. This function, and setting `TD_GET_DEFAULTS_TO_NONE`
to a false value, are deprecated and will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.
Use `td[key]` to raise a `KeyError` for a missing key.

Parameters:

**set_to_none** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `get` returns `None` for
a missing key when no default is passed. If `False`, it raises a
`KeyError`. Defaults to `True`.

# set_lazy_legacy

*class*tensordict.set_lazy_legacy(*mode: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*)

Turns the legacy lazy mode on or off.

In the legacy lazy mode, [`unsqueeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unsqueeze),
[`squeeze()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.squeeze.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.squeeze),
[`view()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.view.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.view),
[`transpose()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.transpose.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.transpose) and
[`permute()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.permute.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.permute) return lazy views of the
tensordict instead of tensordicts, and [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack) returns a lazy
stack. The mode is off by default, and the `LAZY_LEGACY_OP`
environment variable sets it at import. Use it as a context manager or a
decorator, or call `set_lazy_legacy(mode).set()` to change the mode for
the rest of the program.

Deprecated since version 0.15: The legacy lazy mode (`set_lazy_legacy(True)`) is deprecated and will
be removed in TensorDict 0.17. `set_lazy_legacy(False)` will then do
nothing. Use [`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) to build a lazy stack.

Parameters:

**mode** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) - if `True`, turns the legacy lazy mode on, and emits a
`DeprecationWarning`.

---

# set_list_to_stack

*class*tensordict.set_list_to_stack(*mode: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*)

Sets whether assigning a list to a key stores a stack of non-tensor data.

By default (`mode=True`), `td[key] = ["a", "b"]` stores a
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) with one value per element along the
first batch dimension. With `mode=False`, the list is stored as one
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) value. The `LIST_TO_STACK`
environment variable sets the mode at import. Use it as a context manager
or a decorator, or call `set_list_to_stack(mode).set()` to change the
mode for the rest of the program.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Turning list-to-stack conversion off (`set_list_to_stack(False)` or
`LIST_TO_STACK=0`) is deprecated and will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.
Use [`td.set_non_tensor(key, value)`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_non_tensor.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_non_tensor)
to store a list as one value. `set_list_to_stack(True)`, the default,
does not warn, and will keep working, doing nothing, after the removal.

Parameters:

**mode** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) - if `True`, a list is stored as a stack. `False`
stores it as one value, and emits a `DeprecationWarning`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, set_list_to_stack
>>> td = TensorDict(batch_size=[2])
>>> with set_list_to_stack(True):
... td["x"] = ["a", "b"]
>>> type(td.get("x")).__name__, td["x"]
('NonTensorStack', LinkedList(['a', 'b']))
```

# set_printoptions

*class*tensordict.set_printoptions(***, *verbose: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, ***kwargs*)

Sets the options that control what the repr of a tensordict shows.

Use it as a context manager or a decorator to change the options for a
block of code; the previous options come back at the end of the block.
Call `set_printoptions(...).set()` to change them for the rest of the
program. The options that are not passed keep their current value.
[Printing and display](../../printing.html#printing) describes every option with examples, and
[`get_printoptions()`](tensordict.get_printoptions.html#tensordict.get_printoptions) returns the current values.

Keyword Arguments:

- **verbose** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, hides the device, dtype and
`is_shared` attributes, unless a keyword argument sets them.
Defaults to `True`.
- ****kwargs** - the options to set: `show_batch_size`, `show_device`,
`show_is_shared`, `show_shape`, `show_field_device`,
`show_dtype`, `show_field_is_shared`, `show_grad`,
`show_is_contiguous`, `show_is_view`, `show_storage_size`,
`plain`, `sort_keys` and `compact`. `compact=True` prints
each entry on one line as its dtype and its feature dimensions
(`f32[3]`).

Raises:

[**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - if an option is unknown.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, set_printoptions
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with set_printoptions(verbose=False):
... print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]))},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]))
```

# stack

tensordict.stack(*input: Sequence['T']*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*) → T

Stacks tensordicts into one dense tensordict along a new dimension `dim`.

Same as `torch.stack(input, dim)`. Every input must have the same keys,
entry shapes and batch size. If they do not, this function raises a
`RuntimeError`. To fall back to a lazy stack when the inputs differ, use
[`maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.maybe_dense_stack.html#tensordict.maybe_dense_stack). To always get a lazy stack, use
[`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack). [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking) compares these functions.

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to stack.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the new dimension. Defaults to `0`. A `dim` outside
`[-batch_dims - 1, batch_dims]` warns, and is used on the dimensions
of the leaves. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will
change to raising an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

**out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into. Its batch size must be the stacked batch size. Defaults to
`None`.

Returns:

A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) whose batch size is
`batch_size[:dim] + [len(input)] + batch_size[dim:]`. Tensorclass
inputs give an instance of their class. If every input is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict), the result is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> tds = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]) for _ in range(2)]
>>> td = tensordict.stack(tds, dim=1)
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([3, 2])
>>> type(td).__name__
'TensorDict'
```

---

# LazyStackedTensorDictStore

`LazyStackedTensorDictStore` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `LazyStackedTensorDictStore` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore(***, *backend: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['redis', 'dragonfly'] = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *count: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *stack_dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *inner_batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]*, *device=None*, *client=None*, *td_id: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *cache_metadata: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, ***redis_kwargs*)

Bases: `_StoreConnection`, `_StoreUnsupported`, [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

A lazy stack of tensordicts whose entries live on a Redis-compatible server.

Warning

`LazyStackedTensorDictStore` is experimental: its API can change in a
minor release without a deprecation cycle.

[`TensorDictStore.from_tensordict`](tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.from_tensordict)
returns this class when you pass a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict),
so that the elements of the stack can have entries of different shapes.
You can also call `from_lazy_stack()`, and `from_store()` to
reconnect. The class behaves like a lazy stack, but it is a
[`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) subclass, not a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) subclass.

Supports [Redis](https://redis.io), [Dragonfly](https://dragonflydb.io),
[KeyDB](https://docs.keydb.dev), and any other Redis-wire-compatible
server. The data lifetime, `close` and `clear_redis` work as for
[`TensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore) (see its "Lifecycle and
limits" section).

Warning

`store["nested"]` is an in-memory copy of the nested entry: writes
through it, for example `store["nested"].set_(...)` or
`store["nested"].zero_()`, change the copy only, not the store.
Write with the full key, `store.set(("nested", "b"), ...)`, or with
[`update()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update).

Each leaf key is one string on the server for the whole stack, with a
table of offsets when the shapes of the elements differ, so the number of
keys on the server does not grow with the number of elements.

The constructor makes an empty stack of `count` elements of batch size
`inner_batch_size`. To copy a lazy stack to the server, use
`from_lazy_stack()`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a label for the kind of server, as in
[`TensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore). Defaults to
`"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the host name of the server. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the port of the server. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number on the server. Defaults
to `0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix socket, for a
server on the same machine. If set, `host` and `port` are
ignored. Defaults to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the namespace of the keys of the store on
the server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **count** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the number of elements of the stack.
- **stack_dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension of the stack in the batch
size. Defaults to `0`.
- **inner_batch_size** (*sequence**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the batch size of each element.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the tensors
that reads return. Defaults to `None`: reads return CPU tensors,
and the store has no device.
- **client** (*redis.asyncio.Redis**,**optional*) - an existing client. If given,
`host`, `port`, `db` and `unix_socket_path` are ignored.
Defaults to `None`, which creates a client.
- **td_id** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the identifier of the store on the server.
Defaults to `None`, which creates a new UUID. To reconnect to an
existing store, use `from_store()`.
- **cache_metadata** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, keeps the shape and
dtype of each entry in the process, to save round-trips to the
server. Defaults to `True`.
- ****redis_kwargs** - passed to `redis.asyncio.Redis`.

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, lazy_stack
>>> from tensordict.store import TensorDictStore
>>> local = lazy_stack([TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(5))])
>>> store = TensorDictStore.from_tensordict(local) 
>>> type(store).__name__ 
'LazyStackedTensorDictStore'
>>> store[0]["x"].shape, store[1]["x"].shape 
(torch.Size([3]), torch.Size([5]))
>>> store[1] = TensorDict(x=torch.ones(5)) 
>>> store[1]["x"] 
tensor([1., 1., 1., 1., 1.])
>>> store.clear_redis() 
>>> store.close()
```

flatten_keys(*separator='.'*, *inplace=False*, *is_leaf=None*)

Returns a local copy of the store whose nested keys are joined by `separator`.

The data is read from the server with [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict), and the
store is not changed.

Parameters:

- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the string that joins the parts of a
nested key. Defaults to `"."`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - must be `False`; `True` raises a
`ValueError`. Defaults to `False`.
- **is_leaf** (*Callable**,**optional*) - see
[`flatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys). Defaults to
`None`.

See [`flatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys).

*classmethod*from_dict(*input_dict*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_size=None*, *device=None*, ***kwargs*)

Raises a `NotImplementedError`: build the store with `from_lazy_stack()`.

The arguments are those of [`from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict),
and are not used.

*classmethod*from_lazy_stack(*lazy_td*, ***, *backend: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['redis', 'dragonfly'] = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *device=None*, ***kwargs*) → LazyStackedTensorDictStore

Returns a new store that holds a copy of the data of a lazy stack.

The data is sent in chunks of 10,000 elements, so that the full stack
is not built in memory at once.

Parameters:

**lazy_td** ([*LazyStackedTensorDict*](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict)) - the lazy stack to copy to the
server.

Keyword Arguments:

- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a label for the kind of server, as in
[`TensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore). Defaults to
`"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the host name of the server. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the port of the server. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number on the server. Defaults
to `0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix socket, for a
server on the same machine. If set, `host` and `port` are
ignored. Defaults to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the namespace of the keys of the store on
the server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensors that reads return. Defaults to `None`, which takes
the device of `lazy_td`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the constructor, such as `client` or
`td_id`, and options of the Redis client.

Raises:

[**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - if `lazy_td` is not a
 [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict).

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, lazy_stack
>>> from tensordict.store import LazyStackedTensorDictStore
>>> local = lazy_stack([TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(2)), TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(4))])
>>> store = LazyStackedTensorDictStore.from_lazy_stack(local) 
>>> store.batch_size, store[1]["x"].shape 
(torch.Size([2]), torch.Size([4]))
>>> store.clear_redis() 
>>> store.close()
```

*classmethod*from_store(***, *backend: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['redis', 'dragonfly'] = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *td_id: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*, *device=None*, ***kwargs*) → LazyStackedTensorDictStore

Returns a store connected to a lazy stack that another store wrote to the server.

Reads the number of elements, the stack dimension, the batch size of
the elements and the device from the server.

Keyword Arguments:

- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a label for the kind of server, as in
[`TensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.TensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.TensorDictStore). Defaults to
`"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the host name of the server. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the port of the server. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number on the server. Defaults
to `0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix socket, for a
server on the same machine. If set, `host` and `port` are
ignored. Defaults to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the namespace of the keys of the store on
the server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **td_id** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - the identifier of the store to connect to. A store
shows it in its `repr`, and holds it in the private attribute
`_td_id`; there is no public accessor.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensors that reads return. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
device stored on the server.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the constructor, such as `client` or
`cache_metadata`, and options of the Redis client.

Returns:

A `LazyStackedTensorDictStore` connected to the existing data.

Raises:

[**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if the server has no lazy stack with this `td_id`.

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`. The
second store could be in another process.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, lazy_stack
>>> from tensordict.store import LazyStackedTensorDictStore
>>> local = lazy_stack([TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(2)), TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(4))])
>>> writer = LazyStackedTensorDictStore.from_lazy_stack(local) 
>>> reader = LazyStackedTensorDictStore.from_store(td_id=writer._td_id) 
>>> reader[1]["x"].shape 
torch.Size([4])
>>> writer.clear_redis() 
>>> writer.close() 
>>> reader.close()
```

# TensorDictStore

`TensorDictStore` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `TensorDictStore` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.store.TensorDictStore(***, *backend: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['redis', 'dragonfly'] = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *batch_size=None*, *device=None*, *client=None*, *td_id: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *cache_metadata: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, ***redis_kwargs*)

Bases: `_StoreConnection`, `_StoreUnsupported`, [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

A tensordict whose entries live on a Redis-compatible server.

Supports [Redis](https://redis.io), [Dragonfly](https://dragonflydb.io),
[KeyDB](https://docs.keydb.dev), and any other Redis-wire-compatible server.

Use it to share data between processes or machines, or to keep data out of
the RAM of the training process. Each tensor entry is stored as one string
of raw bytes on the server. Its shape and dtype are stored next to it, so
that `keys()` and `shape` do not download the data. See
[Large datasets and storage backends](../../storage.html#storage) for a guide.

Each read or write blocks until the server answers. One call sends its
commands to the server in one round-trip.

Lifecycle and limits

- The store needs a running server. By default it connects to
`localhost:6379`. To start a local Redis server, run
`docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis`.
- The data stays on the server after `close()`, after the object is
garbage collected, and after the process ends. The server keeps it in
its memory until you delete it.
- To reconnect from another process, pass the `td_id` of the store to
`from_store()`, which also reads the batch size and the device. The
id is in the private attribute `_td_id`, and is shown by `repr`.
There is no public accessor.
- `close()` closes the connection and stops the background loop. The
object cannot read or write after that, and the data stays on the
server. `clear_redis()` deletes the data and keeps the connection
open.
- Each tensor entry is one string on the server. Redis limits a string to
512 MB by default (`proto-max-bulk-len`), and a larger write raises
`redis.exceptions.ResponseError`. For larger entries, raise the limit
on the server, or split the entry.
- Non-tensor values are stored as JSON. A value that JSON cannot encode
is stored with [`pickle`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html#module-pickle), and each read unpickles it. Any client
that can write to the server can then run code in the readers, so
connect only to a server that you trust.

Keyword Arguments:

- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a label for the kind of server, kept in the
store and shown by its `repr`, for example `"redis"`,
`"dragonfly"` or `"keydb"`. Every server speaks the same
protocol, so the value does not change how the store connects.
Defaults to `"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the host name of the server. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the port of the server. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number on the server. Defaults to
`0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix socket, for a
server on the same machine. If set, `host` and `port` are
ignored. Defaults to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the namespace of the keys of the store on the
server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of
the store: the leading dimensions that all its entries share.
Defaults to `None`, which gives `torch.Size([])`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensors that reads return. The server holds CPU bytes. Defaults to
`None`: reads return CPU tensors, and the store has no device.
- **client** (*redis.asyncio.Redis**,**optional*) - an existing client. If given,
`host`, `port`, `db` and `unix_socket_path` are ignored.
Defaults to `None`, which creates a client.
- **td_id** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the identifier of the store on the server.
Defaults to `None`, which creates a new UUID. The constructor
does not read the batch size of an existing store: use
`from_store()` to reconnect.
- **cache_metadata** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, keeps the shape and
dtype of each entry in the process, to save round-trips to the
server. Defaults to `True`.
- ****redis_kwargs** - passed to `redis.asyncio.Redis`.

Raises:

[**ModuleNotFoundError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ModuleNotFoundError) - if the `redis` package is not installed
 (`pip install redis`).

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.store import TensorDictStore
>>> td = TensorDictStore(batch_size=[100]) 
>>> td["obs"] = torch.zeros(100, 84) 
>>> td["obs"].shape 
torch.Size([100, 84])
>>> type(td.to_tensordict()).__name__ 
'TensorDict'
>>> td.clear_redis() 
>>> td.close()
```

To connect to a Dragonfly server on another host, pass its address,
for example
`TensorDictStore(backend="dragonfly", host="dragonfly-host", batch_size=[100])`.

*classmethod*from_schema(*schema: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size), [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)]]*, ***, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *backend: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['redis', 'dragonfly'] = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *device=None*, ***kwargs*) → TensorDictStore

Returns a new store with zero-filled entries of the given shapes and dtypes.

Each key of `schema` is registered with its shape and dtype. The
server allocates each entry with `SETRANGE` and fills it with zeros.
No tensor data goes through the Python process, but the server
allocates the full size in its memory at once.

Use it for a replay buffer or another shared buffer whose schema you
know before you fill it.

Each entry is one string on the server. Redis limits a string to 512
MB by default (`proto-max-bulk-len`). A larger entry raises
`redis.exceptions.ResponseError`: raise the limit on the server, or
split the entry.

Parameters:

**schema** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - maps each key (a str, or a tuple of str for a
nested entry) to `(feature_shape, dtype)`, where
`feature_shape` is the shape after the batch dimensions. The
entry has shape `[*batch_size, *feature_shape]`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch size
of the store. Defaults to `None`, which gives
`torch.Size([])`.
- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a label for the kind of server, as in
`TensorDictStore`. Defaults to `"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the host name of the server. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the port of the server. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number on the server. Defaults
to `0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix socket, for a
server on the same machine. If set, `host` and `port` are
ignored. Defaults to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the namespace of the keys of the store on
the server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensors that reads return, as in `TensorDictStore`.
Defaults to `None`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the `TensorDictStore` constructor, such
as `client` or `td_id`, and options of the Redis client.

Returns:

A new `TensorDictStore` whose entries are zeros.

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`. The
`obs` entry takes 21 MB on the server.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.store import TensorDictStore
>>> store = TensorDictStore.from_schema( 
... {"obs": ([84, 84, 3], torch.uint8),
... "action": ([4], torch.float32),
... "reward": ([], torch.float32)},
... batch_size=[1000],
... )
>>> store["obs"].shape 
torch.Size([1000, 84, 84, 3])
>>> store[0] = TensorDict( 
... obs=torch.ones(84, 84, 3, dtype=torch.uint8),
... action=torch.ones(4),
... reward=torch.ones(()),
... batch_size=[],
... )
>>> store["action"][:2] 
tensor([[1., 1., 1., 1.],
 [0., 0., 0., 0.]])
>>> store.clear_redis() 
>>> store.close()
```

*classmethod*from_store(***, *backend: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['redis', 'dragonfly'] = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *td_id: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*, *device=None*, *tensorclass_cls: [type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → TensorDictStore

Returns a store connected to data that another store wrote to the server.

One process writes the data, with `from_tensordict()` or with
`td[key] = value`; another process, on any machine that reaches the
server, passes the same `td_id` to connect to it. The batch size and
the device are read from the server.

If the writer was a tensorclass, the server holds the path of its
class, and the result is an instance of that class, which must be
importable. `tensorclass_cls` overrides it.

Keyword Arguments:

- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a label for the kind of server, as in
`TensorDictStore`. Defaults to `"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the host name of the server. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the port of the server. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number on the server. Defaults
to `0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix socket, for a
server on the same machine. If set, `host` and `port` are
ignored. Defaults to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the namespace of the keys of the store on
the server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **td_id** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - the identifier of the store to connect to. A store
shows it in its `repr`, and holds it in the private attribute
`_td_id`; there is no public accessor.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensors that reads return. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
device stored on the server.
- **tensorclass_cls** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the tensorclass to wrap
the result in, as a class or as a path `"module.ClassName"`
to import. Defaults to `None`, which uses the class stored on
the server, if any.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the `TensorDictStore` constructor, such
as `client` or `cache_metadata`, and options of the Redis
client.

Returns:

A `TensorDictStore`, or a tensorclass that wraps one.

Raises:

[**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - if the server has no store with this `td_id` under
 `prefix`.

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`. The
second store could be in another process.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.store import TensorDictStore
>>> writer = TensorDictStore(batch_size=[100]) 
>>> writer["obs"] = torch.zeros(100, 84) 
>>> reader = TensorDictStore.from_store(td_id=writer._td_id) 
>>> reader.batch_size, reader["obs"].shape 
(torch.Size([100]), torch.Size([100, 84]))
>>> writer.clear_redis() 
>>> writer.close() 
>>> reader.close()
```

*classmethod*from_tensordict(*td: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, ***, *backend: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['redis', 'dragonfly'] = 'redis'*, *host: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'localhost'*, *port: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 6379*, *db: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *unix_socket_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'tensordict'*, *device=None*, ***kwargs*) → TensorDictStore

Returns a new store that holds a copy of the data of `td`.

A [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) gives a
[`LazyStackedTensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore), which keeps
entries of different shapes. For a tensorclass, the store records its
class, so that `from_store()` returns an instance of it.

Parameters:

**td** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict or tensorclass to copy to the
server.

Keyword Arguments:

- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a label for the kind of server, as in
`TensorDictStore`. Defaults to `"redis"`.
- **host** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the host name of the server. Defaults to
`"localhost"`.
- **port** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the port of the server. Defaults to `6379`.
- **db** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the database number on the server. Defaults
to `0`.
- **unix_socket_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path of a Unix socket, for a
server on the same machine. If set, `host` and `port` are
ignored. Defaults to `None`.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the namespace of the keys of the store on
the server. Defaults to `"tensordict"`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the device of the
tensors that reads return. Defaults to `None`, which takes
the device of `td`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the `TensorDictStore` constructor, such
as `client` or `td_id`, and options of the Redis client.

Returns:

A `TensorDictStore`, or a
[`LazyStackedTensorDictStore`](tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore.html#tensordict.store.LazyStackedTensorDictStore) for a lazy
stack.

Examples

The example needs a Redis server on `localhost:6379`. For a
server on another machine, pass `host`.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.store import TensorDictStore
>>> local = TensorDict(obs=torch.zeros(10, 84), batch_size=[10])
>>> remote = TensorDictStore.from_tensordict(local) 
>>> remote["obs"].shape 
torch.Size([10, 84])
>>> remote.clear_redis() 
>>> remote.close()
```

to_local() → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Returns a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) with a copy of the data of the store.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Use [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict) instead.

# tensorclass

tensordict.tensorclass(*cls: T = None*, */*, ***, *autocast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *frozen: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *nocast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *shadow: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *tensor_only: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *skip_post_init_on_rebuild: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *cast_filter: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

A decorator that turns a class with annotated fields into a tensorclass.

A tensorclass is a dataclass whose instances behave like a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict): they have a batch size, and they support
indexing, reshaping, `to(device)`, stacking and memory-mapping. For new
code, subclass [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) instead. It takes the same
flags, and type checkers understand it without a plugin. This decorator
is kept for existing code and for code that moves from
`@dataclass`. See [TensorClass](../../tensorclass.html#tensorclass-guide).

Parameters:

**cls** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*,**optional*) - the class to decorate, passed by
`@tensorclass` without parentheses.

Keyword Arguments:

- **autocast** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, when a field is set, the value
is converted to the annotated type. Exclusive with `nocast` and
`tensor_only`. Defaults to `False`.
- **frozen** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, assigning a field raises
`dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError`, as with
`@dataclass(frozen=True)`. To block writes on one instance only,
call `lock_()` on it or pass `lock=True` to the constructor:
writes then raise a `RuntimeError`. Defaults to `False`.
- **nocast** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, Tensor-compatible types such as
`int`, `np.ndarray` and the like are not cast to a tensor
type. Exclusive with `autocast` and `tensor_only`. Defaults
to `False`.
- **shadow** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, fields can have the name of a
tensorclass member (`batch_size`, `sum`, ...), and hide that
member. If `False`, such a name raises an `AttributeError`
when the class is defined. Defaults to `False`.
- **tensor_only** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, every field annotation must
be a tensor type or a tensor collection. Values that can be cast
to a tensor are cast. Reading a field then skips the lookup in the
non-tensor storage. Exclusive with `autocast` and `nocast`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **skip_post_init_on_rebuild** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`,
`__post_init__` runs in the generated `__init__`,
`from_tensordict`, `from_dict`, the other constructors such
as `from_any` or `fromkeys`, and when the data is loaded or
received from another process, but not when tensordict makes a
new instance from the data of an existing one, as in indexing,
`clone`, `to`, `apply` or `torch.stack`. Defaults to
`False`: `__post_init__` also runs on these rebuilds, except
on the shells that `empty()` builds. On a lazy stack it runs on
each stacked instance.
- **cast_filter** (*Callable**,**optional*) - the default `cast_filter` of
[`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) and of the dtype shorthands
(`float()`, `bfloat16()`, ...) on the instances of the class: a
predicate `fn(key, value) -> bool` that selects the tensor leaves
a dtype cast applies to, `key` being the nested key as a tuple of
str. A `cast_filter` passed to the call overrides it, and
`cast_filter=None` there casts every leaf. Subclasses inherit it.
It applies to calls on the tensorclass itself, not when the
tensorclass is a value of another tensordict or tensorclass that
is cast. Defaults to `None`: every leaf is cast.

Returns:

The tensorclass, or a decorator if the flags are given without a
class (`@tensorclass(autocast=True)`).

Examples

tensorclass can be used with or without arguments:

```
>>> from typing import Any
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import tensorclass
>>> @tensorclass
... class X:
... y: int
>>> X(torch.ones(())).y
tensor(1.)
>>> @tensorclass(autocast=False)
... class X:
... y: int
>>> X(torch.ones(())).y
tensor(1.)
>>> @tensorclass(autocast=True)
... class X:
... y: int
>>> X(torch.ones(())).y
1
>>> @tensorclass(nocast=True)
... class X:
... y: Any
>>> X(1).y
1
>>> @tensorclass(nocast=False)
... class X:
... y: Any
>>> X(1).y
tensor(1)
```

A tensorclass can have methods. Fields that are not tensors are stored
as [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData):

```
>>> @tensorclass
... class MyData:
... X: torch.Tensor
... y: torch.Tensor
... z: str
... def expand_and_mask(self):
... X = self.X.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(self.y)
... X = X[self.y]
... return X
...
>>> data = MyData(
... X=torch.ones(3, 4, 1),
... y=torch.zeros(3, 4, 2, 2, dtype=torch.bool),
... z="test",
... batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> print(data)
MyData(
 X=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4, 1]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4, 2, 2]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.bool, is_shared=False),
 z=NonTensorData(data=test, batch_size=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=None),
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 4]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(data.expand_and_mask())
tensor([])
```

A tensorclass instance can be a field of another tensorclass:

```
>>> @tensorclass
... class NestingMyData:
... nested: MyData
...
>>> nesting_data = NestingMyData(nested=data, batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> # although the data is stored as a TensorDict, the type hint helps us
>>> # to appropriately cast the data to the right type
>>> assert isinstance(nesting_data.nested, type(data))
```

`skip_post_init_on_rebuild` checks the data once, when it comes in:

```
>>> @tensorclass(skip_post_init_on_rebuild=True)
... class Ragged:
... offsets: torch.Tensor
... indices: torch.Tensor
... def __post_init__(self):
... if int(self.offsets[-1]) != len(self.indices):
... raise ValueError("the last offset must be len(indices)")
>>> r = Ragged(offsets=torch.tensor([0, 2, 3]), indices=torch.zeros(3))
>>> r.clone().offsets # not checked again
tensor([0, 2, 3])
```

`cast_filter` keeps the integer and boolean fields out of dtype casts:

```
>>> from tensordict import is_inexact
>>> @tensorclass(cast_filter=is_inexact)
... class Mesh:
... points: torch.Tensor
... cells: torch.Tensor
>>> mesh = Mesh(points=torch.zeros(4, 3), cells=torch.zeros(2, 3, dtype=torch.long))
>>> mesh.bfloat16().points.dtype, mesh.bfloat16().cells.dtype
(torch.bfloat16, torch.int64)
>>> mesh.bfloat16(cast_filter=None).cells.dtype # cast every leaf
torch.bfloat16
```

# unpack_memmap

tensordict.unpack_memmap(*archive_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*) → [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

Extracts a memory-mapped tensordict archive into a directory.

The inverse of [`pack_memmap()`](tensordict.pack_memmap.html#tensordict.pack_memmap), and the same as `unzip`: the
directory has one file per leaf, which
[`load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap) reads. Existing files in
`prefix` are overwritten.

Parameters:

- **archive_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - an archive written by [`pack_memmap()`](tensordict.pack_memmap.html#tensordict.pack_memmap)
or by [`save()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.save.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.save).
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the directory to extract into. It is created if
it does not exist.

Returns:

The path of the directory, as a [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path).

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if `archive_path` is not an archive (see
 [`is_memmap_archive()`](tensordict.is_memmap_archive.html#tensordict.is_memmap_archive)).

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, unpack_memmap
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as path:
... _ = td.save(Path(path) / "td.tdz")
... directory = unpack_memmap(Path(path) / "td.tdz", Path(path) / "td")
... print(sorted(p.name for p in directory.iterdir()))
['a.memmap', 'meta.json']
```
